records.label: archaeal cannula
records.definition: An extracellular hollow tubular archaeal cell projection, characterized in Pyrodictium species, that extends from the cell envelope as a proteinaceous filament and forms networks between cells.

Resolved #501 by scoping the taxonomic and canonical-example notes to their single direct citations, and resolved #502 by making CanA the subject of the calcium-coordination assembly edge.

Separated native AV2 CanX from recombinant TAG11 CanA evidence, added a label-only CanX constituent, restricted the CanA assembly graph to the demonstrated in vitro system, and named K1-CanA as the solved NMR construct. Preserved PROPOSED status and unresolved family, minor-subunit and physiological-function questions.

components.label: CanA cannula glycoprotein
components.grounding_notes: CanA is a cannula-forming glycoprotein characterized from Pyrodictium abyssi TAG11, distinct from the native AV2 major subunit CanX. No exact source-neutral InterPro, Pfam or NCBIfam family grounding was verified.
components.role: Cannula glycoprotein whose recombinant mature form assembles into hollow cannula-like fibers in vitro through calcium coordination and donor-strand complementation; warming accelerates assembly under the tested conditions.

evidence.notes: Sleutel et al. 2025 resolved in vitro filaments assembled from recombinant P. abyssi TAG11 CanA. The native ex vivo AV2 cannula reconstruction in the same paper instead identifies the distinct homologue CanX as its major subunit.
Munte et al. 2025 solved the NMR solution structure of the N-terminally truncated K1-CanA construct and separately characterized divalent-ion-induced polymerization of full-length recombinant CanA.

protein_examples.role: Representative unreviewed (TrEMBL) UniProtKB entry for gene canA, which UniProt lists without a gene symbol, in Pyrodictium abyssi. Identifier for the component's declared gene symbol; it is not itself evidence that the protein is part of this structure.

evidence.notes: UniProtKB unreviewed (TrEMBL) entry A0ACM8DFF3 for gene canA in Pyrodictium abyssi. Establishes the accession and gene identity only; the component's membership in this structure rests on the record's own sources.

components.label: CanX cannula glycoprotein
components.grounding_notes: CanX names the native cannula major-subunit class identified in P. abyssi AV2, not an alias of TAG11 CanA. Sleutel et al. found no Pfam or PANTHER domain match for the native subunit and placed cannula-like proteins in the broader TasA superfamily; no exact source-neutral family grounding is asserted here.
components.role: Major glycoprotein subunit of native cannulae resolved from P. abyssi AV2, joined by donor-strand complementation and calcium-coordinated interfaces. This does not establish obligatory coassembly with CanA or exclude low-occupancy minor subunits.

evidence.notes: Sleutel et al. 2025 assigned the native AV2 cannula cryo-EM map to CanX, a homologue distinct from the recombinant TAG11 CanA used in their in vitro assembly experiments.

taxonomic_distribution.note: Pyrodictium abyssi produces extracellular cannulae that were visualized as a cell-associated tubular network in ultrastructural studies.

canonical_examples.note: Hyperthermophilic archaeon in which cannulae were shown by cryo-electron tomography to enter the periplasmic space without crossing into the cytoplasm.

functions.label: extracellular Pyrodictium cell-network formation
functions.description: Cannulae extend from the Pyrodictium cell envelope and physically interconnect cells in an extracellular network; the transported cargo or signaling role of the network remains unresolved.

evidence.notes: Nickell et al. 2003 used cryo-electron tomography to show how Pyrodictium cannulae contact the cell envelope and interconnect cells.
Rieger et al. 1995 characterized the extracellular network of Pyrodictium abyssi cannulae in ultrastructural sections.
Rieger et al. 1995, Ultrastructure of the hyperthermophilic archaeon Pyrodictium abyssi, Journal of Structural Biology.
Nickell et al. 2003, Pyrodictium cannulae enter the periplasmic space but do not enter the cytoplasm, as revealed by cryo-electron tomography, Journal of Structural Biology.
Sleutel et al. 2025, Donor strand complementation and calcium ion coordination drive the chaperone-free polymerization of archaeal cannulae, Nature Communications.
Munte et al. 2025, Biophysical characterization and solution structure of the cannulae-forming protein CanA from the hyperthermophilic archaeon Pyrodictium abyssi, Scientific Reports.

causal_graphs.title: Recombinant CanA coordinates calcium during in vitro fiber assembly
causal_graphs.description: Recombinant mature P. abyssi TAG11 CanA coordinates calcium and undergoes donor-strand complementation to assemble hollow cannula-like fibers in vitro.
causal_graphs.scope_notes: Restricted to the experimentally characterized recombinant CanA assembly system. Calcium was necessary but not sufficient for rapid assembly under the tested conditions; warming accelerated polymerization. Native AV2 CanX fibers provide a distinct structural comparison, not evidence that the native subunit is CanA. Cell-level nucleation, envelope attachment, CanB/CanC incorporation and physiological cargo transport are not modeled.

edges.subject: cana_cannula_glycoprotein
edges.description: Recombinant CanA interfaces coordinate calcium ions in the in vitro filament, supporting donor-strand-complemented assembly.

evidence.notes: Sleutel et al. 2025 resolved calcium-bound interfaces in recombinant TAG11 CanA filaments assembled in vitro.

edges.subject: cana_cannula_glycoprotein
edges.description: Recombinant mature CanA polymerizes into hollow cannula-like fibers under the tested in vitro assembly conditions.

evidence.notes: Sleutel et al. 2025 used cryo-EM to resolve recombinant CanA filaments; their separate native AV2 reconstruction was composed principally of CanX.
Munte et al. 2025 assayed divalent-ion-induced polymerization of full-length recombinant CanA, distinct from the truncated K1-CanA NMR construct.

discussions.prompt: Resolve exact source-neutral protein-family groundings for CanA and CanX and the component boundaries of CanB and CanC.
discussions.rationale: The first archaeal cannula record keeps only CanA as a reviewed label-only component because this pass did not verify an exact Pfam, InterPro or NCBIfam family for CanA or resolve whether the homologous CanB and CanC glycoproteins should be separate curated components. Follow-up inspection of Sleutel et al. 2025 distinguishes the native AV2 major subunit CanX from recombinant TAG11 CanA. Both are now represented separately without implying that they coexist in one native filament; exact family mappings and CanB/CanC component boundaries remain unresolved.

evidence.notes: Munte et al. 2025 reviewed CanA, CanB and CanC as homologous Pyrodictium abyssi glycoproteins present in cannulae.
Sleutel et al. 2025 distinguish native CanX and recombinant CanA and discuss the unresolved possibility of low-occupancy minor subunits.

discussions.prompt: Resolve the physiological cargo or signaling role of the Pyrodictium cannula network.
discussions.rationale: Electron microscopy supports cannula-mediated physical interconnection of Pyrodictium cells, but the exchanged material, if any, remains unresolved.

evidence.notes: Nickell et al. 2003 showed that cannulae enter the periplasmic space rather than the cytoplasm.

components.label: ArlF/ArlG S-layer anchor

records.label: bacterial-type flagellum
records.definition: The rotary motility organelle of bacteria: a long helical filament of flagellin joined by a flexible hook to a basal body that spans the cell envelope. The basal body houses a rotor (MS and C rings) driven by membrane-embedded stator units that convert ion flow (H+ or Na+) into torque; the flagellar type III export apparatus at its base secretes the axial subunits. Not homologous to the archaeal archaellum or the eukaryotic cilium.

components.label: flagellin (FliC)
components.stoichiometry: ~20,000 subunits per filament; 11 protofilaments
components.role: Polymerises into the helical propeller filament.

evidence.notes: Macnab 2003 reviews filament assembly from FliC exported through the central channel and capped by FliD.

evidence.snippet: Around 20,000 subunits of flagellin assemble to form the flagellar filament, which can grow up to a 20 µm in length [ 25 , 75 ].
evidence.notes: Verbatim support for the ~20,000 subunits per filament in this component's stoichiometry, which #7 asked to be checked against Macnab 2003. It is not in that review's reachable text (#171); this open-access source states it.

evidence.snippet: Flagellar filaments of almost all bacteria contain 11 protofilaments, with the exception of Campylobacter jejuni , which only has seven 5 , 6 .
evidence.notes: Verbatim support for the 11 protofilaments in the same stoichiometry field, and it bounds the claim: Campylobacter jejuni has seven, so 11 is not universal.

components.label: C ring / switch complex (FliG, FliM, FliN)
components.role: Cytoplasmic rotor ring; FliG engages the stator and the complex sets rotational direction in response to CheY-P. Normally supports assembly; FliI overproduction can bypass an intact C ring in engineered Salmonella mutants, producing rare, nonmotile flagella with defective C-ring structures.

evidence.notes: Minamino & Imada 2015 describe the rotor–stator interface at FliG.

Konishi et al. 2009 studied Salmonella SJW1103-derived fliG, fliM or fliN deletion mutants overproducing FliI. Low-yield flagellar assembly was recovered, not motility; this does not establish normal assembly without C-ring proteins.

components.label: stator unit (MotA5MotB2)
components.role: Ion-driven torque generator anchored to peptidoglycan through MotB. A constituent of the motor, not machinery acting on it: DISPENSABLE here means the flagellum still assembles without MotA/MotB, but it cannot rotate (docs/CURATION.md, component boundary).

evidence.notes: Santiveri et al. 2020 resolve the 5:2 MotA:MotB architecture and propose a rotational model; the structure does not directly observe processive MotA rotation.
Deme et al. 2020 report the same 5:2 architecture independently.
Chang et al. 2019 imaged ΔmotA and ΔmotB cells with assembled but paralysed flagella, showing that the stator is required for torque rather than for flagellar assembly.

taxonomic_distribution.note: Patchy across bacterial lineages. A survey of 30,238 representative genomes across 131 phyla detected conserved FliP/Q/R markers in about 40%; this is genomic evidence of flagellar capacity, not direct observation of assembled flagella or proof of absence in every marker-negative genome.
Archaea swim with the archaellum, a type-IV-pilus-related structure with no homology to the bacterial flagellum.

causal_graphs.title: Ion flow through the stator turns the rotor and the filament

edges.subject: ion_motive_force
edges.description: An electrochemical H+ or Na+ gradient powers torque generation through the corresponding ion-coupled stator. MotA-ring rotation around MotB is a proposed coupling model.

evidence.notes: Santiveri et al. 2020 propose ion flow rotates MotA around the MotB dimer.
Deme et al. 2020 distinguish proton- and sodium-coupled stators and use MotA/MotB as generic subunit names. Sodium motive force is not proton motive force.

edges.subject: stator
edges.description: Ion-coupled stator A-subunit motions apply torque to FliG at the C-ring rim. Processive A-ring rotation is a proposed model; the cited structure also permits an oscillating ratchet.

evidence.notes: Deme et al. 2020 propose rotating and oscillating MotA models compatible with the A5B2 structure; this does not directly establish either dynamic trajectory.

edges.subject: c_ring
edges.description: Torque on FliG and the C ring turns the MS ring, rod, hook, and filament as a rigid flagellar rotor.

evidence.notes: The C ring, MS ring and rod rotate as one rigid rotor.

edges.subject: rotation
edges.description: Rotation is transmitted from the basal body through the hook to the external helical filament.

evidence.notes: Rotation of the helical filament produces thrust.

edges.subject: filament
edges.description: The rotating helical filament acts as a propeller that generates thrust for swimming motility.

evidence.notes: Berg 2003.

components.stoichiometry: 34 FliF subunits in the Salmonella native MS ring
components.role: Inner-membrane ring that anchors the basal body and templates rotor and export-apparatus assembly.

evidence.notes: Kawamoto et al. 2021 used Salmonella cryo-EM to show that the native MS ring is formed by 34 FliF subunits and acts as a core assembly template.

components.label: C ring / switch complex (FliG, FliM, FliN)
components.role: Cytoplasmic rotor ring that engages the stator and biases motor rotation direction. Normally supports assembly; FliI overproduction can bypass an intact C ring in engineered Salmonella mutants, producing rare, nonmotile flagella with defective C-ring structures.

evidence.notes: Minamino and Imada 2015 review the FliG/FliM/FliN C ring as the rotor-mounted switch complex that couples stator contacts to rotational switching.
Kawamoto et al. 2021 measured C-ring symmetry on isolated Salmonella basal bodies and related it to the 34-fold FliF MS ring.

Konishi et al. 2009 studied Salmonella SJW1103-derived fliG, fliM or fliN deletion mutants overproducing FliI. Low-yield flagellar assembly was recovered, not motility; this does not establish normal assembly without C-ring proteins.

taxonomic_distribution.note: Patchy across bacterial lineages. A survey of 30,238 representative genomes across 131 phyla detected conserved FliP/Q/R markers in about 40%; this is genomic evidence of flagellar capacity, not direct observation of assembled flagella or proof of absence in every marker-negative genome.
Archaea swim with archaella, which are type-IV-pilus-related machines rather than bacterial-type flagellar basal bodies.

functions.label: flagellum anchoring in the cell envelope
functions.description: The basal-body rings and rod span the inner membrane, peptidoglycan and, in Gram-negative bacteria, the outer membrane to mount the flagellar rotor.

evidence.notes: Macnab 2003 reviews assembly of the basal body as the envelope-spanning foundation for the bacterial flagellum.
Johnson et al. 2021 resolved the intact Salmonella basal body spanning the inner membrane, cell wall and outer membrane.

functions.label: rotary torque transmission
functions.description: Ion-driven stator units act on the C ring so the MS ring and basal-body rod rotate and transmit torque to the hook and filament.

evidence.notes: Tan et al. 2021 resolved structural couplings by which the MS ring, FliE, FlgB, distal rod and LP ring support torque transmission through the flagellar motor.
Deme et al. 2020 structurally modeled the MotA5MotB2 stator as the ion-driven unit that drives the FliG rotor.

causal_graphs.title: Basal-body rings couple ion-driven torque to the rod
causal_graphs.description: FliF forms the MS ring scaffold, the export gate occupies its center and builds the rod, LP rings let the distal rod spin through the Gram-negative envelope, and stator units apply torque through the C ring.

nodes.label: flagellar type III membrane export gate

edges.subject: ms_ring
edges.description: The FliF MS ring is the first ring scaffold and organizes later basal-body assembly around the inner membrane.

evidence.notes: Kawamoto et al. 2021 support the MS ring as a basal-body core and template for flagellar assembly.

edges.subject: c_ring
edges.description: The FliG/FliM/FliN C ring attaches to the cytoplasmic face of the FliF MS ring.

evidence.notes: Kawamoto et al. 2021 analyzed C-ring symmetry in native Salmonella basal bodies relative to the FliF MS ring.

edges.subject: export_apparatus
edges.description: The export gate lies in the central opening of the MS ring to secrete axial subunits.

evidence.notes: Kawamoto et al. 2021 linked the 23-subunit core of the M ring to a pore sized for the flagellar protein export gate.

edges.subject: export_apparatus
edges.description: The membrane export gate delivers the FliE, FlgB, FlgC, FlgF and FlgG axial proteins used to build the rod.

evidence.notes: Macnab 2003 reviews export of rod and other axial subunits through the flagellum-specific type III export apparatus.
Kubori et al. 1992 used Salmonella assembly intermediates to place FliE and the FlgB/FlgC/FlgF/FlgG proteins in the rod assembly pathway.

edges.subject: lp_rings
edges.description: The L and P rings surround the distal rod to let it rotate through the Gram-negative outer envelope.

evidence.notes: Yamaguchi et al. 2021 resolved the FlgH/FlgI LP ring encircling the Salmonella distal rod.

edges.subject: stator
edges.description: Ion-powered stators apply torque through FliG in the C ring. A rotating MotA pentamer is one structural model for this coupling, not a directly observed trajectory in the cited study.

evidence.notes: Deme et al. 2020 resolve A5B2 stator architecture and propose both processive MotA rotation and an alternative oscillating ratchet consistent with it.

edges.subject: c_ring
edges.description: Torque on the C ring turns the MS ring and rod as the basal-body rotor.

evidence.notes: Minamino and Imada 2015 describe the bacterial C ring, MS ring and rod as the rotor turned by stator interactions with FliG.
Tan et al. 2021 resolved the structural path used to transmit torque from the MS ring into the rod.

records.label: bacterial-type flagellum basal body, C ring
records.definition: The cytoplasmic FliG/FliM/FliN switch ring of the bacterial flagellar basal body, assembled on the MS ring to form the rotor face that receives torque from Mot/Pom stator units and changes rotational bias in response to phosphorylated CheY.

curation_history.changes: Scaffolded by scripts/new_record.py

Added GO C-ring synonymy and basal-body parthood; curated FliG, FliM and FliN components with exact InterPro groundings; added bacterial and archaeal taxonomic scope, Salmonella as a canonical example, rotor assembly, stator coupling and rotational switching functions, primary literature evidence, a FliG/FliM/FliN switch-complex causal graph, and resolved boundary discussions for Bacillus FliY and neighboring motor subcomplexes.

Resolved #274 by moving morphology-only Thomas 1999 evidence off the FliN component, resolved #275 by routing FliG/FliM/FliN graph edges into the GO:0009433 C-ring node, and resolved #276 by adding Welch 1993 as direct CheY-P-to-FliM binding evidence.

#183: added 3 protein example(s) by resolving each of the component's declared gene symbols to the single reviewed UniProtKB entry for that symbol in a taxon this record names, deduplicated by accession. Symbols resolving to more than one reviewed entry were skipped rather than chosen between.
Addressed #2129, #2134: Qualify proposed stator rotation in three flagellar records; Correct the C-ring FliY grounding rationale without erasing history.

Addressed adversarial issue #2135: qualified FliM/FliN assembly essentiality with the engineered partial-C-ring bypass, retained the distinct FliG result, and distinguished assembly from motor function.
added 1 verified UniProtKB xref(s) to GENE_OR_PROTEIN causal_graphs node(s).

discussions.prompt: Should Bacillus subtilis FliY be folded into the curated FliN component?
discussions.rationale: Ward et al. 2019 support FliY as the Bacillus subtilis lower switch-complex protein, but the exact InterPro grounding used for this record's FliN component is restricted to FliN from organisms such as Salmonella and Escherichia. Correction (2026-10-10): that taxonomic restriction is incorrect. InterPro IPR012826 also covers the corresponding region of longer FliY proteins, and reviewed Bacillus subtilis FliY P24073 carries this entry. A shared region does not by itself establish equivalent whole-protein scope.
discussions.resolution_note: Retain the enteric FliN component and document the Bacillus FliY replacement as a lineage variant. This boundary rests on whole-protein architecture and phosphatase function, not exclusion of FliY from IPR012826. A separate lineage-specific component remains to be modeled; the family match alone does not justify silently merging the proteins.
discussions.notes: 2026-10-10: Corrected the basis of the prior decline while retaining its original rationale and dates. Ward et al. 2019 describe the Bacillus switch organization and FliY phosphatase; current InterPro and UniProt demonstrate the shared region.

evidence.notes: InterPro describes the corresponding FliN-family region in longer FliY proteins.
Reviewed Bacillus subtilis FliY includes the IPR012826 cross-reference.
Ward et al. 2019 support the Bacillus FliY replacement and its phosphatase role.

records.label: dinoflagellate peduncle
records.definition: A small, flexible, finger-like projection of cytoplasm containing an array of microtubles and located near the flagellar pores in some photosynthetic as well as nonphotosynthetic dinoflagellate species. records.label: flagella connector

functions.label: new-to-old flagellum linkage
functions.description: The FC couples the distal tip of the growing new flagellum to the flank of the old flagellum during T. brucei flagellum biogenesis.

functions.label: new-flagellum tip tracking
functions.description: The FC remains associated with the tip of the assembling new flagellum while moving along the old flagellum.

evidence.notes: Moreira-Leite et al. 2001 first described the motile junction that connects the growing new flagellum to the old flagellum during trypanosome cell division.
Davidge et al. 2006 used intraflagellar-transport mutants to dissect FC movement from extension of the new flagellar axoneme.

functions.label: new-tip to old-shaft microtubule coupling
functions.description: FC-associated proteins link the connector membrane junction to extending microtubule tips in the assembling new flagellum and to axonemal microtubules along the lateral shaft of the mature old flagellum.

Hoog et al. 2016 resolved the connector between the new flagellum tip and the lateral side of the old flagellum; it travels along the old flagellum and stops roughly halfway along its length. This supplies the spatial context for the mature-flagellum microtubule attachment.

functions.label: context-dependent contribution to swimming
functions.description: Chlamydomonas mastigoneme-associated swimming phenotypes depend on the tested mutant and assay. Liu et al. 2020 observed slower swimming in an mst1 mutant, whereas Amador et al. 2020 found no significant forward-swimming speed or propulsive-flow benefit from mastigonemes using a different mstg line. A general hydrodynamic contribution is therefore not established.

evidence.notes: Liu et al. 2020 found that mst1 line LMJ.RY0402.052413 lacked mastigonemes and swam about 15% slower than their control. PKD2 organization and swimming phenotypes support a context-specific association, not a resolved universal hydrodynamic mechanism.

Amador et al. 2020 used mastigoneme-deficient mstg line LMJ.RY0402.136134 and compared it with cw15 and cc125. Mean swimming speed, normalized maximum speed, flagellar waveform and propulsive flows did not show significant enhancement by mastigonemes under these conditions. Increased turning in mstg was observed, so this is not evidence that all motility phenotypes are absent.

causal_graphs.title: OmcZ subunits branch hemes for nanowire conduction
causal_graphs.description: OmcZ octaheme c-type cytochromes polymerize into an extracellular filament whose branched heme arrangement and surface-exposed heme site provide a candidate structural basis for conductive OmcZ nanowires.
causal_graphs.scope_notes: This graph is restricted to OmcZ filament architecture and the proposed branched-heme conduction path; it does not model OmcZ proteolytic processing, export, biofilm regulation, or the distinct OmcS and OmcE cytochrome nanowire classes.

edges.subject: omcz_octaheme_c_type_cytochrome
edges.description: The OmcZ filament positions covalently bound hemes in a branched arrangement rather than the linear chains seen in OmcS and OmcE filaments.

edges.subject: branched_heme_network
edges.description: OmcZ's branched heme arrangement leaves one heme in every subunit highly exposed at the filament surface.

evidence.notes: Wang et al. 2022 proposed that the surface-exposed heme in each OmcZ subunit may help explain conductive biofilm network formation.

edges.subject: branched_heme_network
edges.description: The branched OmcZ heme arrangement provides a candidate electron-transfer path through the conductive cytochrome filament.

evidence.notes: Wang et al. 2022 proposed that the branched OmcZ heme architecture could account for highly conductive cytochrome filaments.

records.label: P pilus
records.definition: A chaperone-usher adhesive pilus of uropathogenic Escherichia coli built from a PapA helical rod, a PapG-PapF-PapE tip fibrillum, a PapK adaptor that bridges the fibrillum to the rod, and a basal PapH terminator. The PapD chaperone delivers subunits to the PapC usher, which assembles the pilus, and the distal PapG adhesin binds host glycolipid receptors.

Rephrased the PapE-to-PapK assembly edge as an adaptor connection rather than a polymerization edge into PapK.

functions.label: P pilus assembly
functions.description: PapD delivers folded PapG, PapF, PapE, PapK, PapA, and PapH subunits to the PapC usher, which incorporates them in a defined order to build the tip fibrillum, PapK tip-to-rod adaptor, helical rod, and basal terminator of the P pilus.

evidence.notes: Werneburg and Thanassi 2018 review P pilus assembly as an ordered PapD/PapC chaperone-usher pathway.
Hospenthal, Costa and Waksman 2017 review P pili within the broader chaperone-usher pilus biogenesis pathway.

causal_graphs.title: PapC assembles the PapD-delivered P pilus tip and rod
causal_graphs.description: PapD carries pilus subunits to the PapC usher. PapC initiates assembly with the distal PapG adhesin, then incorporates PapF and PapE to build the tip fibrillum, PapK to bridge the tip to the rod, PapA repeatedly to form the rod, and PapH to terminate and anchor the completed appendage.

edges.subject: papd_chaperone
edges.description: PapD stabilizes folded P pilus subunits and delivers them to the PapC outer-membrane usher.

evidence.notes: Werneburg and Thanassi 2018 review the PapD periplasmic chaperone and PapC usher steps of P pilus biogenesis.

edges.subject: papc_usher
edges.description: The PapC usher starts P pilus biogenesis with the distal PapG adhesin.

evidence.notes: Werneburg and Thanassi 2018 describe ordered P pilus subunit incorporation beginning with PapG.

edges.subject: papg_adhesin
edges.description: PapG caps the distal end of the P pilus and connects to PapF.

evidence.notes: Werneburg and Thanassi 2018 review PapF as the next incorporated subunit after the PapG adhesin.

edges.subject: papf_tip_adaptor
edges.description: PapF links the distal PapG adhesin to the PapE subunits of the tip fibrillum.

evidence.notes: Werneburg and Thanassi 2018 place PapE after PapF in the P pilus assembly order.

edges.subject: pape_tip_fibrillum_subunit
edges.description: PapE subunits form the tip fibrillum, and the proximal PapE subunit connects to PapK before the PapA rod begins.

evidence.notes: Werneburg and Thanassi 2018 place PapK between the PapE tip fibrillum and PapA rod subunits.

edges.subject: papk_tip_adaptor
edges.description: PapK joins the PapE tip fibrillum to the first PapA rod subunits.

evidence.notes: Werneburg and Thanassi 2018 describe PapK as the adaptor incorporated before the PapA rod.

edges.subject: papa_major_rod_subunit
edges.description: PapA is repeatedly incorporated to form the thick helical P pilus rod.

evidence.notes: Hospenthal et al. 2016 resolve the helical P pilus rod as an assembly of PapA subunits.

edges.subject: paph_terminator
edges.description: PapH terminates PapA addition and anchors the basal end of the completed P pilus at the outer membrane.

evidence.notes: Verger et al. 2006 identify the mechanism by which PapH terminates P pilus growth.

edges.subject: papc_usher
edges.description: The outer-membrane PapC usher polymerizes and secretes P pilus subunits through the envelope.

evidence.notes: Hospenthal, Costa and Waksman 2017 review outer-membrane ushers as assembly platforms for chaperone-usher pili.

evidence.notes: Werneburg and Thanassi 2018 distinguish PapD and PapC assembly factors from the assembled P pilus subunits.

records.label: paraflagellar rod
records.definition: A large lattice-like axial structure found in some flagellated protists which extends alongside the axoneme. Protein components of the paraflagellar rod are likely implicated, among other, in adenine nucleotide signaling and metabolism, and in calcium signaling.

curation_history.changes: Scaffolded by scripts/new_record.py

components.label: paraflagellar rod protein PFR1
components.role: Major lattice protein that co-assembles with PFR2 in the full paraflagellar rod of the studied trypanosome and Leishmania models; Leishmania PFR1 can associate with axoneme attachment fibers without PFR2.

evidence.notes: Deflorin et al. 1994 distinguished the T. brucei 73 kDa PFRC/PFRD product from 69 kDa PFRA/PFRB.
Gadelha et al. 2004 consolidate T. brucei PFRC as PFR1, orthologous to Leishmania PFR1.
Maga et al. 1999 found Leishmania mexicana PFR1 throughout the PFR and required for native formation; PFR1 can associate with attachment fibers without PFR2.

protein_examples.role: Reviewed UniProtKB entry for the PFRC/PFRD-encoded 73 kDa protein in Trypanosoma brucei brucei, assigned to consolidated PFR1 by Gadelha et al. 2004. The source protein name and historical UniProt mnemonic PFR2_TRYBB are not a cross-species orthology assertion (also declared as synonym PFRD).

evidence.notes: UniProtKB reviewed entry Q26789 verifies the source-native 73 kDa protein name and PFRC/PFRD genes. The consolidated family assignment follows Gadelha et al. 2004, not the ordinal UniProt mnemonic.
Table 1 and Fig. 1 map T. brucei PFRC to PFR1 and PFRA to PFR2, consistently with Leishmania nomenclature.

components.grounding_notes: InterPro:IPR007824 / Pfam:PF05149 covers both PFR1 and PFR2 rather than the individual consolidated PFR1 family. No exact source-neutral PFR1-only CURIE was curated.

components.label: paraflagellar rod protein PFR2
components.role: Major lattice protein required for full native PFR architecture in the studied trypanosome and Leishmania models, not for every reduced PFR. Gadelha et al. found no evidence for PFR2 in the reduced Crithidia deanei rod using several assays, while noting their detection limitations.

evidence.notes: Schlaeppi et al. 1989 characterized the helical PFRA/PFRB product, subsequently assigned to consolidated PFR2.
Gadelha et al. 2004 consolidate T. brucei PFRA as PFR2, orthologous to Leishmania PFR2.
Maga et al. 1999 showed that Leishmania PFR2 is required for native full PFR assembly, while PFR1 can form stable associations with attachment fibers without it.

Gadelha et al. 2005 imaged a reduced PFR in Crithidia deanei and found no PFR2 with PCR, hybridization and protein assays. The combined negative results support a lineage distinction, not proof of universal gene absence.

protein_examples.role: Reviewed UniProtKB entry for the PFRA/PFRB-encoded 69 kDa protein in Trypanosoma brucei brucei, assigned to consolidated PFR2 by Gadelha et al. 2004. The source protein name and historical UniProt mnemonic PFR1_TRYBB are not a cross-species orthology assertion (also declared as synonym PFRB).

evidence.notes: UniProtKB reviewed entry P22225 verifies the source-native 69 kDa protein name and PFRA/PFRB genes. The consolidated family assignment follows Gadelha et al. 2004, not the ordinal UniProt mnemonic.

taxonomic_distribution.note: The paraflagellar rod is restricted to a small set of flagellated protist lineages rather than a conserved feature of eukaryotic cilia.
Within Euglenozoa, PFRs are prominent in kinetoplastid flagella, but they can be greatly reduced and cryptic in some endosymbiont-bearing kinetoplastids.

canonical_examples.note: Trypanosome model in which deletion of cytoplasmic PFR-AF1 or PFR-AF2 showed that both assembly factors are required for paraflagellar rod formation.
Genetic model in which PFR1 and PFR2 knockouts established that both major proteins are required for native PFR formation and flagellar motility.

functions.label: flagellar waveform control
functions.description: The PFR provides an extra-axonemal scaffold needed for normal kinetoplastid flagellar beating and cell motility.

evidence.notes: Bastin et al. 1998 disrupted the PFR in T. brucei and linked PFR loss to a trypanosome motility defect.
Santrich et al. 1997 showed that a Leishmania mexicana PFR2 knockout lacks most PFR structure and has altered flagellar beat waveform and forward swimming.

functions.label: extra-axonemal PFR assembly
functions.description: New PFR lattice proteins are delivered into the flagellum and incorporated into the elongating paraflagellar rod, a process that requires cytoplasmic PFR assembly factors.

evidence.notes: Bastin et al. 1999 followed tagged PFRA during PFR growth and observed a major distal addition site plus minor incorporation along the partially assembled PFR.
Alves et al. 2020 identified cytoplasmic PFR-AF1 and PFR-AF2 as factors required for PFR formation.

functions.label: flagellar signaling platform
functions.description: The PFR-associated protein cohort includes calcium/calmodulin and adenine-nucleotide signaling or metabolic proteins that can influence flagellar beating.

evidence.notes: Portman et al. 2009 used RNAi-mutant comparative proteomics to expand the PFR cohort and infer calcium/calmodulin regulatory links among some components.
Portman and Gull 2010 review links between the PFR proteome, adenine-nucleotide metabolism, calcium signaling and motility regulation.

causal_graphs.title: PFR1 and PFR2 build the paraflagellar rod lattice
causal_graphs.description: PFR1 and PFR2 co-assemble into the full PFR lattice in the studied Trypanosoma and Leishmania models. In T. brucei, cytoplasmic PFR-AF1 and PFR-AF2 act upstream of flagellar assembly and support major PFR protein accumulation. This model does not require the same composition in reduced rods such as that of Crithidia deanei.

edges.subject: pfr1
edges.description: Leishmania PFR1 is a major structural constituent throughout the native PFR and can associate with axoneme attachment fibers without PFR2.

evidence.notes: Maga et al. 1999 examined PFR1 localization and its requirement for native Leishmania PFR formation.

edges.subject: pfr2
edges.description: PFR2 partners with PFR1 in the full native PFR of the studied trypanosome and Leishmania models; this is not a universal requirement for reduced rods.

evidence.notes: Bastin et al. 1999 tracked tagged PFRA, now consolidated as PFR2, into new and old T. brucei PFRs.
The nomenclature crosswalk maps historical T. brucei PFRA to PFR2.
Maga et al. 1999 showed Leishmania PFR2 is required for the full native PFR, with residual PFR1-containing material possible without PFR2.

edges.subject: paraflagellar_rod
edges.description: The PFR assembles next to the axoneme and is attached to it through axoneme attachment fibers.

evidence.notes: Maga et al. 1999 used Leishmania PFR mutants to show that fibers attaching the PFR to the axoneme can assemble in the absence of the bulk PFR.

edges.subject: pfr_af1
edges.description: Cytoplasmic PFR-AF1 is required for PFR formation and normal levels of major PFR proteins.

evidence.notes: Alves et al. 2020 found that deleting PFR-AF1 dramatically disrupts PFR formation in T. brucei.

edges.subject: pfr_af2
edges.description: Cytoplasmic PFR-AF2 is required for PFR formation and normal levels of major PFR proteins.

evidence.notes: Alves et al. 2020 found that deleting PFR-AF2 dramatically disrupts PFR formation in T. brucei.

discussions.prompt: Should all proteomic PFR candidates be curated as paraflagellar-rod components now?
discussions.rationale: The PFR proteome contains many low-abundance or regulatory proteins in addition to the two major lattice proteins; Portman et al. 2009 identified 20 novel PFR components by RNAi-ablation proteomics and epitope tagging. This first GO:0097740 record therefore enumerates only PFR1/PFR2, while additional candidates need family-by-family curation to avoid folding transient or nearby flagellar proteins into the structural lattice boundary.

discussions.prompt: Are PFR-AF1 and PFR-AF2 paraflagellar-rod components?
discussions.rationale: PFR-AF1 and PFR-AF2 are cytoplasmic proteins required for PFR formation, but the component boundary in docs/CURATION.md excludes factors that act on a subunit before assembly and then depart.
discussions.resolution_note: Curated PFR-AF1 and PFR-AF2 as assembly graph nodes rather than as components of the mature paraflagellar rod.

discussions.prompt: Reconcile historical PFRA/PFRC and UniProt names with cross-species PFR1/PFR2 orthology.
discussions.rationale: Gadelha et al. 2004 Table 1 and Fig. 1 consolidate T. brucei PFRC/PFRD (Q26789, 73 kDa) as PFR1 and PFRA/PFRB (P22225, 69 kDa) as PFR2. Historical UniProt mnemonics use the opposite ordinal numbering and must not substitute for this cross-species family assignment.
discussions.resolution_note: Aligned modern component families, gene symbols, protein examples and graph citations; retained source-native protein labels and all previous curation events.

evidence.notes: Primary nomenclature table and phylogeny establish the crosswalk.

records.label: periplasmic flagellum
records.definition: A bacterial-type flagellar appendage of spirochetes whose filaments reside in the periplasmic space between the cytoplasmic and outer membranes, attach near the cell poles, and rotate to deform the cell cylinder for motility.

functions.label: stalk nutrient capture and hydrolysis
functions.description: Caulobacter stalks can take up and hydrolyze the organic phosphate substrate fluorescein diphosphate. Modeling predicts that a long, thin stalk can improve diffusive nutrient capture, but delivery of captured nutrients to the cell-body cytoplasm and the resulting nutritional benefit remain unresolved.

evidence.notes: Wagner et al. 2006 directly observed uptake and hydrolysis of fluorescein diphosphate by attached and isolated stalks. Their diffusive-capture model predicts a length/geometry advantage, not direct proof of whole-cell nutritional benefit.
Ireland et al. 2002 identified transport-related proteins in isolated stalks, consistent with uptake competence but not proof of nutrient delivery to the cell body.
Schlimpert et al. 2012 show that mature crossbands block PstS protein exchange, challenging the proposed PstS-mediated phosphate shuttle. Possible small-molecule routes were not established.

Curtis 2017 discusses the unresolved Caulobacter nutritional role and shows PstA-GFP in some Brevundimonas stalks; that localization does not demonstrate a complete transporter or justify a shared mechanism across species.

functions.label: stalk compartmentalization
functions.description: Protein diffusion barriers divide the Caulobacter stalk from the cell body and separate stalk segments from each other.

evidence.notes: Schlimpert et al. 2012 show that crossband diffusion barriers compartmentalize the Caulobacter stalk.

records.label: type I pilus
records.definition: A mannose-sensitive adhesive bacterial pilus assembled by the chaperone-usher pathway. In the Escherichia coli model, a helical FimA rod carries an ordered FimH-FimG-FimF tip, is polymerized through the FimD usher, and ends in a basal FimI terminator. Other type I systems, including Salmonella, have different subunit inventories.

discussions.prompt: Keep PilB and PilT in the mechanism graph rather than the filament constituent table.
discussions.rationale: The cited review distinguishes the pilin filament from the cytoplasmic PilB/PilT motor subcomplex and its PilC platform. Motor activity is required for extension/retraction in the described type IVa systems but does not make either motor a filament constituent. Keeping motors as external graph nodes avoids assigning filament-formation essentiality to nonconstituents.

evidence.notes: T4P biogenesis and structure sections explicitly distinguish motor, alignment and secretin subcomplexes from the pilin filament.

discussions.prompt: Resolve exact family groundings for the pilins represented by this broad type IV filament record.

evidence.notes: The source separates pilin filament architecture from machinery and discusses distinct T4aP/T4bP systems.

records.label: Y-shaped link
records.definition: A Y-shaped protein complex in the ciliary transition zone that connects the cilium axoneme to the ciliary necklace. Both protein sorting and protein gating occur at this point in the cilium allowing some, but not all proteins to enter the cilium.

functions.label: transition-zone membrane tethering
functions.description: Microtubule-membrane connectors physically couple the transition-zone doublets to the surrounding ciliary membrane. The Chlamydomonas evidence concerns the connector ensemble, not purified Y-links acting alone.

evidence.notes: Figure 3 compares connector defects with greater and more variable membrane spacing and loss of detergent-resistant membrane attachment in cep290 cells.

causal_graphs.title: CEP290-supported connector architecture and membrane tethering
causal_graphs.description: A bounded physical mechanism supported by Chlamydomonas localization, mutant ultrastructure and membrane-extraction experiments.
causal_graphs.scope_notes: The experiment perturbs CEP290 and affects both Y-connectors and longitudinal wedge densities. It supports connector-mediated tethering, not a Y-link-only sufficiency assay, direct CEP290-lipid binding, an absolute requirement for every linker, or a molecular gating pathway.

nodes.label: transition-zone membrane tethering to microtubule doublets

edges.subject: cep290
edges.description: In Chlamydomonas, CEP290 supports normal connector architecture; its loss removes most Y-links but does not eliminate every connector.

evidence.notes: Figures 3C-D and 4 combine mutant cross sections with immunogold placement. Rare surviving Y-connectors limit the claim to normal architecture rather than absolute assembly dependence.

edges.subject: y_link
edges.description: Y-links participate in the connector ensemble that tethers the transition-zone membrane to doublet microtubules.

evidence.notes: Figure 3 shows cross-sectional links between doublets and membrane; connector disruption accompanies increased membrane spacing and loss of membrane retention after detergent extraction. Wedge densities are also affected, so this is not Y-link-specific sufficiency.

evidence.notes: Glucose-catabolism Results and Figure 4 distinguish metabolic flux from ATP replenishment.

records.label: basal body A-B inner junction
records.definition: A protein network at the lumen-facing interface between the A- and B-tubules of a basal-body triplet microtubule, forming connections between the two tubules with region-specific composition.

components.label: POC1 family protein
components.role: Bridges the A1/B10 inner junction in proximal and central-core basal-body regions. At the core it also provides an attachment toward the separate inner scaffold.

evidence.notes: Results, Figures 2 and 4, and Figure EV4 place Poc1 at the junction. Poc1 deletion produces heterogeneous defects and replacement compositions, not uniform absence of every A-B junction; assembly essentiality is not assigned.

components.grounding_notes: InterPro IPR050505 combines WDR55 and POC1; IPR020472 is a WD40 repeat. Neither is an exact POC1 family identity. The inspected Q229Z6 sequence belongs to the SB210 reference strain and is not paired to the B2086 experiment.

components.label: alpha-helical inner-junction ladder protein
components.grounding_notes: The source assigns the ladder to I7LY02, an unreviewed SB210 reference protein at TTHERM_00682980. UniProt lists no InterPro or Pfam cross-reference, and the native InterPro protein-to-integrated-entry endpoint returned no match. No exact source-neutral family is asserted. The PDB entity name SWIM-type domain-containing protein is not a verified family or activity. The structural experiment uses SB715, so no strain-paired protein example is added.
components.role: Forms the alpha-helical ladder assigned to the proximal A-B inner junction, bridging protofilaments A13 and B10 in the structural model. This assignment is not transferred to the distinct core-region LRR density or the FAP52-like protein.

evidence.notes: Cai et al. 2025, Figure 4D-F and Results identify an I7LY02-containing array in the A-B junction, following the MS-guided predicted-model assignment of the corresponding B-C ladder. This supports source-assigned membership, not a knockout dependency, biochemical binding assay or assembly essentiality. RCSB 9QZC entity 8 independently maps the study's ladder model to I7LY02, but its A-C/B-C composite scope is not treated as an A-B-specific deposition.

canonical_examples.note: Cryo-ET and focused subtomogram averages of isolated basal bodies resolve proximal and central-core A-B junction networks. Methods identify wild-type B2086; the canonical example is species-level. SB210 reference sequences and CU428 axonemal models are not asserted to be strain-matched experimental examples.

discussions.prompt: Distinguish the basal-body A-B junction from neighboring structures.
discussions.rationale: This is a named multiprotein junction network, not one protein or a whole triplet.
discussions.notes: Hidden- and ignored-inclusive repository searches found no existing identity record. Complete GO searches for inner junction, basal body and triplet found no exact basal-body A-B cellular component. GO:0160113 specifically denotes the axonemal doublet inner junction and remains a separate record. The A-C intertriplet linker, B-C junction, inner scaffold and proximal inner ladder are not synonyms. GO:0140535 is broader is-a; GO:0036064 is parthood.

discussions.prompt: Resolve exact POC1, FAP52, FAP106, IJ34 and alpha-helical inner-junction ladder protein family groundings.
discussions.rationale: Broader families, individual domains and organism-specific sequences do not define exact taxon-agnostic component classes.
discussions.notes: These five components remain REVIEWED_LABEL_ONLY for the documented reasons. FAP45 and FAP210 have exact InterPro family annotations. RCSB 8G2Z is a CU428 axonemal doublet, not a basal-body deposition; its sequence mappings are used only to crosscheck model identities. The inspected unreviewed UniProt entries are SB210 references, not strain-paired B2086 or SB715 experimental examples. I7LY02 has no integrated InterPro match in the inspected endpoint; the paper's limited detectable homology is not evidence for taxonomic absence of the structure.

discussions.prompt: Confirm the core LRR protein and resolve the remaining unassigned densities.
discussions.rationale: A plausible predicted-model fit does not establish a unique molecular identity.
discussions.notes: Q22N53 is a candidate for the core arch-shaped LRR density; Li et al. explicitly defer confirmation of identity and function. Its proposed N-terminal hairpin dimer and contacts remain models, not established components or stoichiometry. Its computational UniProt name is not evidence of kinase activity. The proximal FAP52-like paralog and core scaffold-attachment stem also remain unassigned. Cai et al.'s later I7LY02 assignment to the proximal inner-junction ladders is represented separately and does not identify these other densities.

discussions.prompt: Keep mutant replacements and neighboring proteins out of wild-type composition.
discussions.rationale: poc1 deletion affects multiple basal-body modules and yields heterogeneous junctions.
discussions.notes: PACRG, FAP20 and the CCDC81b/BMIP1-associated axonemal-like configurations occur in mutant core subclasses; they are not added as normal wild-type basal-body junction constituents. IJ34 is not equated to CCDC81b through shared domain annotations. Tubulins are junction substrates here, and the inner scaffold is a separate connected structure, not an extra component family. Subtomogram class percentages are not organismal prevalence.

discussions.prompt: Avoid inferring assembly timing, direct binding or universal geometry.
discussions.rationale: The analyzed basal bodies are mature; spatial comparisons are not time courses.
discussions.notes: Proximal-to-core composition and lattice-angle differences do not establish temporal recruitment order. FAP106 recruitment hierarchies from another species' axoneme are not transferred here. Potential FAP52-FAP106 and FAP52-FAP210 contacts in EV4 remain model-based. No assembly essentiality, force threshold, general stoichiometry or broad taxonomic distribution is asserted.

discussions.prompt: Use native deposition metadata to bound dataset links.
discussions.rationale: The article's B-C entry label conflicts with the native archive title.
discussions.notes: Table 2 labels EMD-46438 as core B-C, whereas its native EMDB title says proximal B-C. It is outside this A-B record and is not linked or silently relabeled. Only the three native-verified wild-type A-B datasets are included.

discussions.prompt: Reconcile the earlier unassigned proximal ladder with newer molecular evidence.
discussions.rationale: A later source assigns a protein to a density that the earlier study left unidentified; uncertainty must track the current evidence rather than stay blanket.
discussions.notes: Li et al. 2025 left the proximal A-B and B-C ladder identities open. Cai et al. 2025 subsequently assigned I7LY02 to ladders at both junctions by MS-guided model fitting, with the A-B array depicted in Figure 4D-F. This record now includes the supported alpha-helical ladder class, without claiming perturbation-proven identity, necessity, universal composition or whole-junction stoichiometry. The separate unassigned WD40 ladder at the B-C junction is not an A-B component. Prior timestamped review reports remain immutable snapshots.

functions.label: intertriplet microtubule linkage
functions.description: Connects the A-microtubule of one basal-body triplet to the C-microtubule of its neighbor through a proteinaceous A-link/C-link assembly. Proximal and transitional forms achieve this connection with different C-side compositions.

evidence.notes: Cryotomography and reconstructions in Figures 1-2 and 6 show the intertriplet bridge. This is a structural linkage function, not a measured force threshold or a demonstrated temporal assembly sequence.

causal_graphs.title: Structural contacts bridging adjacent basal-body triplets
causal_graphs.description: A density-supported model of the proximal Tetrahymena A-C linker's physical connections to neighboring microtubules.
causal_graphs.scope_notes: Edges describe modeled structural contacts, not perturbation-proven dependencies, binding kinetics or temporal assembly order. The model applies to the proximal form only. TBC1D31A/B accession aliases and the CEP135 variant assignment remain unresolved; unassigned helical elements are not invented as protein families. No Rab-GAP reaction or native force-resistance threshold is inferred.

edges.subject: wrap73
edges.description: WRAP73 contacts the modeled N-terminal CEP135 dimer in the A-link.

evidence.notes: Figure 5A-B and fitting of the predicted WRAP73-CEP135 complex into observed density support the contact arrangement.

edges.subject: cep135
edges.description: The approximately 325-360 coiled-coil segment bridges protofilaments A06 and A07 in the proximal reconstruction.

evidence.notes: Figure 5C; no claim that this contact alone induces the observed microtubule lattice compaction.

edges.subject: tbc1d31
edges.description: The proximal central-filament and WD40-containing region contacts the modeled N terminus of CEP135.

evidence.notes: Figure 3B and Figure 5A; a collective family-level relationship avoids assigning a contradictory A/B accession alias.

edges.subject: poc1
edges.description: The POC1 C-terminal helix participates in the modeled proximal C-link interface with TBC1D31-like proteins.

evidence.notes: Figure 3A and density fitting of the predicted subcomplex.

edges.subject: tbc1d31
edges.description: TBC1D31-like domains form the proximal C-link arrangement with POC1.

evidence.notes: Figure 3A; domain names do not establish a Rab GTPase reaction.

edges.subject: c_side_interface
edges.description: The modeled POC1/TBC1D31 interface connects to alpha-tubulins in protofilament C09 of the neighboring triplet.

evidence.notes: Results and Figure 3A support the subcomplex-level contact; it is not assigned exclusively to one protein.

edges.subject: cep135
edges.description: CEP135 contacts the A-microtubule and joins the WRAP73/helical network to the central filament in the proximal linker.

evidence.notes: Figures 3B and 5; the unidentified AHE network also contributes to attachment and is not omitted as if CEP135 acted alone.

edges.subject: c_side_interface
edges.description: The proximal C-link contacts the neighboring C-microtubule and is connected to the A-link by the central filament.

evidence.notes: Figure 3 and Results; transitional C-link protein identities are unresolved and are outside this graph.

datasets.platform: cryo-electron microscopy with single-particle reconstruction and model fitting
datasets.findings: Supports molecular assignments at the family level and preserves multiple unassigned protein chains. No global or local deposition copy number is promoted to whole-linker stoichiometry.
datasets.notes: Official entry, all 15 polymer entities and assembly 1 inspected. The entry identifies NCBITaxon 5911 and links the primary DOI/PMID. Only metadata and links are retained, not coordinates. The CEP135 SIFTS assignment and article Methods differ; see the open discussion.

evidence.notes: Cai et al. 2025. Official PMC12506977.1 metadata and checksum-verified JATS inspected. Main text, methods and figure captions read; Figures 1, 3, 5 and 6 inspected visually.
Bibliographic identity matches the official PMC metadata and PDB primary citation.
Official released model, exact primary citation, source organism, polymer entities and assembly inspected.

discussions.prompt: Distinguish the intertriplet A-C linker from the enclosing basal body and other basal-body modules.
discussions.rationale: A named, imaged multi-protein linkage is a distinct structure, not a single protein or synonym of the whole basal body.
discussions.notes: Ignored- and hidden-inclusive repository searches found no existing identity record. Complete GO searches for linker, triplet, intertriplet and centriole found no exact term. GO:0140535 is a broader is-a parent and GO:0036064 is parthood. Cartwheel, inner scaffold, transition fibers and Y-links remain distinct. The primary paper uses centriole as shorthand for the Tetrahymena ciliary basal body.

discussions.prompt: Resolve exact source-neutral groundings for WRAP73, CEP135, TBC1D31 and POC1 without using broader families or domains.
discussions.rationale: All four named classes have structural evidence but their inspected integrated annotations do not establish exact family equivalence.
discussions.notes: The live searches and accession annotations are recorded in each grounding note. Broad InterPro family summaries, including LLM-labeled descriptions, are not used as mechanistic evidence. All four remain REVIEWED_LABEL_ONLY.

discussions.prompt: Identify the unassigned helical elements and transitional C-link proteins, and determine form-specific assembly requirements.
discussions.rationale: The four-family list is incomplete and must not be interpreted as the universal composition of every A-C linker.
discussions.notes: The proximal form contains the POC1/TBC1D31 C-link and five unassigned AHEs. The transitional form retains WRAP73/CEP135, adds an unassigned AHE and replaces the C-side densities with unassigned beta-propellers and a microtubule-contacting domain. Figure 6C/D caption labels conflict with the panel titles, so form identity takes precedence over an ambiguous panel letter. A proposed distal form remains hypothetical. Essentialities and full copy numbers are unset; hierarchical layering is not temporal assembly evidence.

discussions.prompt: Reconcile TBC1D31 A/B aliases and CEP135 variant assignments before adding strain-paired protein examples.
discussions.rationale: Article text and deposition mappings disagree at finer granularity than the supported family-level components.
discussions.notes: Results assign Q23AD1 to A and Q23K58 to B, while Methods reverse them. Methods acknowledge indistinguishable CEP135 N termini and choose Q22AS4; current PDB SIFTS maps that entity to Q24GZ2. UniProt accessions describe SB210, whereas structural isolation uses SB715 and localization uses other strains. No exact paralogue/accession pairing or strain-specific protein example is asserted. Separately, verified POC1 is Q229Z6; the article's Q22Z96 is a different uncharacterized protein, not an alternative POC1.

discussions.prompt: Do not import all adjacent microtubule and junction material as A-C linker constituents.
discussions.rationale: A deposited structural model can include connected modules outside the structure's curated composition boundary.
discussions.notes: Microtubules are the bridged substrates here, not linker protein families. I7LY02 is assigned to inner-junction ladders and is not added to linker composition merely because it appears in PDB:9QZC. POC1 is included specifically because its C-terminal region participates in the proximal C-link. Unidentified chains and AHEs are retained as uncertainty, not fabricated components.

images.attribution: Bin Cai, Jingwei Xu, Erik H. Collet, Ellen Aarts, Leo Luo, Alexander Leitner, Takashi Ishikawa, Pedro Beltrao, Chad G. Pearson, Martin Pilhofer, et al.; CC BY, via PubMed Central
images.caption: Figure 1: Tetrahymena basal-body A-C linkers in situ and after isolation. A-C show segmented and denoised in-situ cryotomograms; F-G show isolated basal bodies with A-C linkers labeled. D is the isolation schematic and E is an SDS-PAGE gel, not microscopy. Scale bars: A, 200 nm; B-C and F-G, 100 nm.
images.notes: Fig. 1. from article version PMC12506977.1; exact licence version read from JATS and media md5 read from the PMC OA S3 metadata. Taxon supplied by the curator because PMC has no taxon field. Curator explicitly accepted the multi-panel figure. The entire multi-panel figure was visually inspected; source bytes are reproduced unchanged. Tomograms support structure identity, not individual protein identity or a mechanical perturbation assay. Source Methods describe DeepDeWedge denoising of the FIB-milled cell tomograms and segmentation of the denoised Figure 1A volume; this processing was performed by the source authors, not by this repository.

records.label: basal body A-tusk
records.definition: A microtubule-associated subassembly in the proximal region of a ciliary basal body, identified in Paramecium tetraurelia as a protruding density between A-microtubule protofilaments A8 and A9, adjacent to but distinguishable from the A-C linker.

curation_history.changes: Scaffolded by scripts/new_record.py

Added the native Paramecium A-tusk example, basal-body parthood, scoped axial-offset annotations, deposited triplet-map context and inspected CC BY figure. Distinguished adjacent linker proteins and processing intervals from A-tusk identity, composition and repeat length; retained molecular role and distribution as unresolved rather than inferring mechanisms or homology.

canonical_examples.note: Cryo-ET and subtomogram averaging of isolated basal bodies resolve the A-tusk in Figure 5B-D and Figure EV5C-E. Cortical units were isolated from d4-2 and Delta-CenBP1; the figures are not assigned to one strain. The proximal-region analysis used 11 tomograms containing 16 basal bodies with intact proximal regions.

physical_properties.context: Axial separation annotations in Paramecium tetraurelia Figure EV5E: the position of A-tusk 2 on one triplet lies 5.2 nm below the upper and 3.3 nm above the lower A-tusk 1 positions on the neighboring triplet. The original figure was visually inspected. These are two static, pairwise offsets in the depicted reconstruction, not means, uncertainty bounds, A-tusk dimensions, a universal axial repeat or an assembly time course. No replicate count or error estimate is supplied for these annotations.

datasets.title: Paramecium microtubule triplet from the start of the proximal region
datasets.description: Deposited whole-triplet structural context from the study defining the A-tusk. This is a proximal microtubule-triplet reconstruction with associated densities, not an isolated A-tusk map or a sequence-resolved A-tusk model.
datasets.notes: Native released-entry metadata verifies the title, taxon 5888, DOI and PMID:32954513. The paper lists EMD-10726 through EMD-10729 and describes combining global triplet and locally aligned A-C-linker maps to display adjacent triplets. EMD-10727 is the proximal A-C-linker-focused deposit; EMD-10726 and EMD-10728 have end-of-proximal-region titles. Sample-name fields repeat start-region wording, so entry titles distinguish the deposits. Only metadata and links are retained; no map volume was downloaded and no exact structure xref is asserted.

evidence.notes: Klena et al. 2020, PMID:32954513. Checksum-verified PMC7667884.1 Results, Paramecium preparation and A-C-linker averaging Methods, Figure 5, Figure EV5 and Data availability inspected. Both original figures were visually inspected; Figure 5 is hosted unchanged. Named segmented densities support morphological identity and placement, not a native protein assignment.

discussions.prompt: Keep the A-tusk distinct from the A-C linker and other basal-body densities.
discussions.rationale: A named morphological subassembly is not the entire basal body or an asserted protein.
discussions.notes: Hidden/ignored-inclusive repository searches and parsed identifiers, labels and synonyms across 871 prior records found no standalone A-tusk identity. Complete QuickGO queries tusk (0), A-tusk (730), centriole tusk (22) and basal body tusk (399) returned no exact term. Kind OTHER and parent GO:0005575 deliberately retain unresolved molecular classification. Basal body is parthood, not is-a. A-tusk, A-link trunk, ArmA, ArmB, triplet base, pinhead, D2-rod and tubulin protofilaments are not exact synonyms. Proximity to the A-C linker is not used to assert obligatory A-C-linker, cartwheel or pro-basal-body parthood.

discussions.prompt: Identify native A-tusk constituents and determine its specific biological role.
discussions.rationale: A segmented protrusion and a static spatial offset do not establish molecular membership or function.
discussions.notes: Direct molecular localization or a sequence-resolved model is needed before assigning components, stoichiometry or protein-family groundings. The inspected morphological evidence does not establish A-tusk-specific essentiality, assembly order, force transmission or mechanical stiffness. No function, trait or causal graph is asserted solely from the surrounding basal-body architecture.

discussions.prompt: Do not transfer neighboring A-C-linker protein assignments into A-tusk composition.
discussions.rationale: An assignment to a connected assembly in another species does not identify this density.
discussions.notes: The inspected Cai et al. 2025 Tetrahymena study assigns WRAP73, CEP135, TBC1D31 and POC1 to A-C-linker regions and leaves additional helical elements unassigned. Its JATS contains no A-tusk identification. These observations do not explicitly establish the identity or composition of the named Paramecium A-tusk. No linker protein or tubulin family is imported here as a constituent merely because it lies in the same broader reconstruction.

discussions.prompt: Distinguish neighboring-triplet offsets from a biological repeat or mechanical measurement.
discussions.rationale: Reconstruction sampling and adjacent-module annotations are not A-tusk dimensions.
discussions.notes: Figure EV5E labels two axial offsets, 5.2 and 3.3 nm, around one neighboring A-tusk position. Do not sum these into an independently measured A-tusk repeat. The Methods pick subvolumes every 8.5 nm; Figure 5 warns that this imposed a pinhead periodicity. The 8.4 +/- 0.2 nm value concerns the A-C linker, and 31.5 angstroms is reconstruction resolution. The approximately 35-nm label belongs to the triplet base; 6- and 9-degree changes concern triplet/linker orientation. None is an A-tusk length, stoichiometry or force measurement. The 1941 extracted subvolumes, split into 1042 proximal and 899 distal classes, are processing counts, not biological copy numbers.

discussions.prompt: Keep the directly supported example separate from cross-species linker comparisons.
discussions.rationale: A multipanel comparison does not establish the same named density in every illustrated taxon.
discussions.notes: Figure 5 and Figure EV5C-E directly label the Paramecium A-tusk. Figure EV5F-H compares A-C linkers from Paramecium, Chlamydomonas and Trichonympha; it is not used to assert broad A-tusk distribution, homologous protein composition or absence in other taxa. Only the single-species Figure 5 is hosted. The d4-2 and Delta-CenBP1 preparation strains are retained without assigning the image to one strain or interpreting it as a perturbation phenotype.

images.attribution: Nikolai Klena, Maeva Le Guennec, Anne‐Marie Tassin, Hugo van den Hoek, Philipp S Erdmann, Miroslava Schaffer, Stefan Geimer, Gabriel Aeschlimann, Lubomir Kovacik, Yashar Sadian, et al.; CC BY, via PubMed Central
images.caption: Paramecium proximal-triplet reconstructions. Panels B-D label the dark-teal A-tusk next to A-microtubule protofilaments A8 and A9, distinct from the lighter patterned A-C linker. Panel A shows the neighboring triplet base and pinhead; its approximately 35-nm annotation is not an A-tusk length. Panels E-F compare proximal-region triplet and linker orientations. These are segmented cryo-ET averages, not raw micrographs or sequence-resolved proteins.
images.notes: Original multipanel Figure 5 visually inspected and accepted without cropping or modification. JATS links this figure to g010.jpg, not g005.jpg; article and media MD5 checksums were verified. Exact CC BY 4.0 licensing comes from JATS. All panels concern Paramecium and match the canonical example. The source hides the pinhead in panel B because its reconstruction was biased by the picking interval. Figure EV5 was also inspected for axial-offset annotations but is not hosted because its complete figure includes multiple taxa. Segmentation colors are not protein identities.

records.label: basal body B-C inner junction
records.definition: A proteinaceous junction network at the lumen-facing interface between the B- and C-tubules of a basal-body triplet microtubule, connecting the two tubules with region-dependent composition.

curation_history.changes: Scaffolded by scripts/new_record.py

Added region-bounded B-C junction components, two species examples, proximal structural contacts, verified EMDB datasets and density preview. Preserved unassigned core/WD40 identities, model-fitting limits, strain provenance, cross-species uncertainty and conflicting reported repeat/dataset labels.
added 1 verified UniProtKB protein_example(s).

components.label: POC1 family protein
components.grounding_notes: The live POC1 family search returns IPR050505, combining WDR55 and POC1; IPR020472 is a WD40 repeat. Neither denotes this exact class. Native UniProt Q229Z6 is a reviewed POC1 reference from SB210, not a strain-paired example for the structural experiments. Its domain and repeat annotations are not promoted to a whole-protein family.
components.role: Its N-terminal WD40 domain bridges B08 and C10 in the proximal Tetrahymena junction. The C-terminal region continues into the neighboring A-C linker. This membership is not assigned to the compositionally distinct core B-C junction.

evidence.notes: Figure 2D-F combines predicted-model fitting with loss of the corresponding WD40 density in complete-triplet subclasses of poc1 deletion material. Figure S4B-D distinguishes the core junction, whose bridging density remains without Poc1.
Figure 4A-B and Results trace the POC1 C-link helix to its N-terminal B08/C10 bridge. This establishes shared participation in connected modules, not identity of the B-C junction and A-C linker.

protein_examples.role: Representative reviewed UniProtKB entry for gene POC1, which UniProt lists under the primary name TTHERM_01308010, in Tetrahymena thermophila SB210. Identifier for the component's declared gene symbol; it is not itself evidence that the protein is part of this structure.

evidence.notes: Pearson CG et al. 2009, ‘Basal body stability and ciliogenesis requires the conserved component Poc1.’, J Cell Biol. ECO:0000269 experimental evidence cited by UniProt for the 'Cytoplasm, cytoskeleton, cilium basal body' localisation of Q229Z6.

components.label: alpha-helical inner-junction ladder protein
components.grounding_notes: The source assigns I7LY02, an unreviewed SB210 reference at TTHERM_00682980. UniProt lists no InterPro or Pfam cross-reference and the native integrated InterPro endpoint returned HTTP 204. No exact source-neutral family is asserted. The PDB entity's SWIM-type name is not a verified family or activity. Cai's structural isolation uses SB715, so no strain-paired protein example is added.
components.role: Forms an alpha-helical ladder connecting B07 and C10 in the proximal Tetrahymena B-C junction. It is distinct from the additional unassigned WD40 density between successive POC1 molecules.

evidence.notes: Figure 4A-C and Results assign the ladder using an MS-derived library of predicted models and density fitting. RCSB 9QZC entity 8 maps the study's ladder model to I7LY02. This is not an I7LY02 knockout, biochemical binding assay or essentiality test.

canonical_examples.note: Cryo-ET of isolated basal bodies resolves different proximal and core B-C networks, with wild-type and poc1-deletion comparisons. Methods list B2086 and SB1969 backgrounds; this is a species-level example, not a pairing with SB210 reference sequences.

Cryo-ET of nucleo-flagellar apparatus from cc849, cw10 mt-, resolves a B-C junction network. The main average combines proximal mother-basal-body segments and attached procentrioles; separate averages reveal maturity-related differences. MIP9-11 are density labels, not verified equivalents of the Tetrahymena molecular assignments.

functions.label: luminal B-C tubule connection
functions.description: Connects the B- and C-tubules along the lumen-facing triplet interface. The Tetrahymena core junction also provides an interface for attachment of the separate inner scaffold.

evidence.notes: Figure 2D and Figure S4B-D show proximal and core bridging networks and distinguish the core junction from its scaffold attachment. This structural function is not a measured force threshold or a junction-specific explanation of all poc1 mutant defects.
Results and Figure 2C describe a network of MIP densities at the Chlamydomonas B-C inner junction without assigning their gene products.

causal_graphs.scope_notes: Edges describe contacts inferred from density and fitted models, not direct binding assays or temporal assembly order. They apply to the proximal form, not the distinct core architecture or an inferred Chlamydomonas protein crosswalk.

evidence.notes: Ruehle et al. 2024. Official PMC11094743.1 JATS checksum verified; proximal/core and mutant Results, relevant Discussion, Methods and captions inspected. Figures 2 and S4 visually checked. Molecular fitting and perturbation evidence are distinguished; no verbatim snippets are asserted.

Cai et al. 2025. Official PMC12506977.1 JATS checksum verified; junction Results, relevant isolation/model-building Methods and data availability read, and Figure 4 visually inspected. Structural isolation uses SB715; model assignments are MS-guided predicted-model fits.

Li et al. 2019. Official PMC6384029.1 JATS checksum verified; relevant architecture, MIP and assembly Results, Methods and MIP9 author response read. Figure 2 and its supplement 12 visually checked. Main averages combine mother-basal-body proximal segments with attached procentrioles.
Li et al. 2025 provides the earlier unassigned inner-ladder observation and an explicitly retained B-C dataset-label conflict. It is not the source for the later I7LY02 molecular assignment.

discussions.prompt: Distinguish the B-C inner junction from connected basal-body modules.
discussions.rationale: This is a named proteinaceous junction network within a triplet, not one protein.
discussions.notes: Hidden- and ignored-inclusive label, synonym, slug and citation searches found only adjacent records and provenance, not this identity. Complete inner-junction and triplet GO searches, and all cellular-component candidates from the basal-body search, found no exact B-C term. GO:0160113 denotes an axonemal doublet A-B junction, not this structure. The outer B-C junction, A-B inner junction, intertriplet A-C linker, inner scaffold and whole triplet are distinct. GO:0140535 is broader is-a; GO:0036064 is parthood.

discussions.prompt: Resolve exact POC1 and alpha-helical inner-junction ladder family groundings.
discussions.rationale: A repeat, domain or combined family does not denote an exact component class.
discussions.notes: Both components remain REVIEWED_LABEL_ONLY for the documented reasons. POC1 Q229Z6 is a reviewed SB210 reference; I7LY02 is unreviewed. Neither is paired to B2086, SB1969 or SB715 as an experimental protein example. The paper's limited detectable I7LY02 homology outside Ciliophora is not evidence that the structure is absent in other taxa.

discussions.prompt: Identify the additional proximal WD40 protein and the core B-C bridging proteins.
discussions.rationale: The named proximal classes are not a complete or universal junction composition.
discussions.notes: Cai et al. leave the WD40 density between POC1 copies unassigned; TBC1D31A is only a hypothesis based on proximity and is not added as a component. Ruehle et al. find a distinct bulky core junction without POC1-like density; its bridge persists in complete poc1-deletion triplets even when the separate scaffold attachment is lost. Proximal I7LY02 placement is not transferred to these core densities.

discussions.prompt: Reconcile the earlier unassigned ladder with newer molecular evidence.
discussions.rationale: Molecular uncertainty must follow the source chronology.
discussions.notes: Li et al. 2025 left the proximal B-C ladder identity open. Cai et al. later assigned I7LY02 by MS-guided model fitting, represented here with that qualification. The same paper assigns a separate I7LY02 array at the A-B junction; sharing a protein does not merge the two junction records.

discussions.prompt: Resolve Chlamydomonas MIP9-11 identities and reconcile the reported MIP9 repeat.
discussions.rationale: Density labels and geometric similarity are not cross-species protein identities.
discussions.notes: Li et al. 2019 assign MIP9 as likely non-tubulin because a canonical protofilament model deviates from its density; the author response and Figure 2 supplement 12 do not identify a gene product. MIP9-11 are not equated to Tetrahymena POC1 or I7LY02. Results describe a 4-nm MIP9 periodicity, while Table 1 lists 8 nm; no repeat measurement is asserted here pending reconciliation. Proximal mother-basal-body and procentriole averages differ, so the pooled map is not immature-only or a universal architecture.

discussions.prompt: Keep neighboring linkers, scaffolds and axonemal proteins outside junction composition.
discussions.rationale: A composite map includes material beyond the curated structural boundary.
discussions.notes: Tubulins are bridged substrates here, not extra junction families. Fam161A/Poc16 core localization is not a molecular assignment to the B-C bridge. TBC1D31-like A-C-linker proteins and axonemal FAP/PACRG assemblies are not imported merely because they are adjacent or occupy similar sites. POC1 is included specifically for its directly supported proximal B-C membership.

discussions.prompt: Avoid converting heterogeneous static reconstructions into a temporal assembly mechanism.
discussions.rationale: Poc1 loss affects multiple structures and specimen isolation can destabilize triplets.
discussions.notes: Complete-triplet mutant subclasses support local density comparisons, not uniform absence of the entire junction. Percentages of subtomogram classes are not organism prevalence. The 2019 assembly model and 2024 disassembly interpretation derive from static classes, with preparation-induced lability acknowledged. No junction-specific force threshold, whole-junction stoichiometry, broad taxonomic distribution or assembly essentiality is asserted. Reconstruction window lengths and map resolutions are not biological dimensions.

discussions.prompt: Handle the conflicting regional label for EMD-46438 without silently choosing one.
discussions.rationale: Native archive titles and article tables do not always agree.
discussions.notes: Li et al. 2025 Table 2 calls EMD-46438 core B-C, whereas native EMDB metadata says proximal B-C; the Methods also state that B-C junctions were excluded from the detailed study. This record instead links independently verified, region-consistent 2024 and Cai 2025 reconstructions. The conflict is retained rather than asserted to be resolved biologically.

records.label: basal body C-tubule hook
records.definition: A hook-shaped proteinaceous linker at the external B-C interface of a basal-body microtubule triplet. In the distal half of isolated Chlamydomonas reinhardtii basal bodies, hook densities occupy the C1 position, extend across the outer surfaces of C2-C4, and recur along the triplet axis.
