records.label: basal body cartwheel
records.definition: A proteinaceous hub-and-spoke assembly at the proximal region of a microbial ciliary basal body or pro-basal body. Its central hub bears nine radially arranged spokes that connect toward the surrounding microtubules; the hub and spokes extend longitudinally as a stacked scaffold.

curation_history.changes: Scaffolded by scripts/new_record.py

Added source-scoped cartwheel identity, constituents and protein examples, three microbial examples, native measurements and an inspected CC BY 4.0 figure. Documented grounding, model and deposition boundaries and the unread 2026 full-text follow-up.

components.label: SAS-6
components.grounding_notes: Native InterPro search returned SAS-6 domains and a domain superfamily, not an exact whole-protein family. These are not asserted as equivalent to SAS-6; the source-specific accession is retained below.
components.role: Structural constituent of the central hub and radial spokes. Recombinant Chlamydomonas SAS-6 forms ring-based assemblies, but this does not establish complete native composition or a fixed copy number per cartwheel.

evidence.notes: Native localization and in-vitro reconstitution with full-length CrSAS-6 and a Bld10 C-terminal fragment support cartwheel membership. The truncated SAS-6 assembly assay is not a census of native subunits.

protein_examples.role: Chlamydomonas SAS-6; the native UniProt entry retains its submitted name and CrSAS-6 gene symbol. This is a TrEMBL entry, not reviewed Swiss-Prot.

evidence.notes: Native JSON confirms accession, organism, gene symbol and entry status; its sequence reference is the original Chlamydomonas SAS-6 study.

components.label: Bld10/Cep135
components.grounding_notes: Native InterPro IPR051877 includes both CEP135 and TSGA10, as independently confirmed by reviewed human UniProt entries. Its scope is broader than Bld10/Cep135. The matched Pfam entries describe domains, not an exact whole-protein family.
components.role: Cartwheel-associated structural protein localized to radial fibers in Chlamydomonas. Its C-terminal fragment supports organized core-cartwheel reconstitution with full-length SAS-6; this does not assign the complete protein to a single density or establish universal cartwheel essentiality.

evidence.notes: Immunogold localization places Bld10 on cartwheel radial fibers in basal bodies and pro-basal bodies. The null mutant lacks recognizable basal bodies, so its phenotype is not a cartwheel-specific loss assay.
Full-length SAS-6 together with Bld10 residues 1061-1641 produces organized hub-and-spoke arrays in vitro. Fragment sufficiency does not establish the full native cartwheel proteome.
Native UniProt JSON verifies the accession, recommended name, BLD10 gene symbol, taxon and Swiss-Prot status.

canonical_examples.note: In-situ cryo-FIB/cryo-ET of mat3-4 cells resolves cartwheels in mature basal bodies and pro-basal bodies. This is a native cellular sample, not a recombinant cartwheel reconstitution.

Cartwheels characterized by cryo-ET and subtomogram averaging of isolated cortical units from d4-2 and delta-CenBP1 strains. The example does not assert identical cartwheel length or spoke-fusion geometry across species.

Isolated basal bodies from NEG cells differentiated into flagellates. Cartwheel periodicities were measured in undamaged regions because specimen preparation often compressed the basal bodies; this is not an assertion that amoeboid cells retain a cartwheel.

functions.label: ciliary basal body organization
functions.description: Provides a central radial scaffold linking the hub toward the surrounding microtubules in the proximal basal-body region. This structural role does not imply that the cartwheel alone determines microtubule number or that its absence abolishes every form of basal-body assembly.

evidence.notes: Native reconstructions resolve the hub, spokes and peripheral connections. Static architecture does not establish a growth time course.

physical_properties.context: Central-hub diameter in isolated Chlamydomonas reinhardtii pro-basal bodies, Figure 1 of Guichard et al. 2017; reported value and error, n=10 measurements from five tomograms. The caption does not specify the error statistic. This is not the full spoke-to-spoke cartwheel diameter.

Axial central-hub density spacing in mature Chlamydomonas reinhardtii basal bodies imaged in situ in Klena et al. 2020, Figure 1; mean and SD, n=30 distances. Not a universal ring-pair repeat or whole cartwheel length.

Axial spacing of cartwheel inner densities in the mature Chlamydomonas reinhardtii in-situ sample, Figure 1; mean and SD, n=18 distances. Inner-density occupancy is not uniform throughout every cartwheel.

discussions.prompt: Distinguish a cartwheel record from its basal-body parent and neighbors.
discussions.rationale: A named hub-and-spoke subassembly is not a single protein or an entire basal body.
discussions.notes: Hidden/ignored-inclusive searches found cartwheel as a component of the existing ciliary basal body record, not as a standalone record. Complete QuickGO cartwheel and centriole-cartwheel searches found no exact cellular component identity. GO:0032991 supplies the broader protein-containing complex class; basal body and pro-basal body are parthood, not is-a. The record centers on the hub and spokes, including their native peripheral specializations. Pinhead, triplet base, A-C linker, inner scaffold and microtubule wall are not synonyms. The 2017 core-cartwheel term excludes pinhead and microtubules and is narrower than the broader cartwheel usage.

discussions.prompt: Find exact taxon-agnostic groundings for SAS-6 and Bld10/Cep135.
discussions.rationale: Domain matches and a broader paralog family are not whole-family equivalents.
discussions.notes: Native InterPro searches and the two UniProt entries were inspected on 2026-10-04. SAS-6 matches are domains or domain superfamilies. IPR051877 includes both reviewed human CEP135 and TSGA10 entries. Components remain REVIEWED_LABEL_ONLY; organism-specific examples retain native names and distinct reviewed/unreviewed statuses. No cross-species essentiality or whole-cartwheel stoichiometry is asserted.

discussions.prompt: Keep reconstruction periodicities and reconstitution models scoped.
discussions.rationale: Native ring organization, artificial arrays and model fits are different kinds of evidence.
discussions.notes: Klena et al. resolve closely spaced hub rings and taxon-specific spoke merging; low-pass filtering can obscure paired rings. The 2017 truncated SAS-6 arrays include eightfold assemblies, and inferred preferential ring-pair addition comes from height distributions rather than a direct time course. Neither experiment supplies a universal copy number or kinetic assembly graph. SAS-5 and Bld10 assignments to particular additional densities remain hypotheses; no SAS-5 component or sequence identity for the cartwheel inner density is asserted here.

discussions.prompt: Assess the full 2026 Trichonympha cartwheel study before adding its molecular model or deposits.
discussions.rationale: Metadata and an abstract do not support an audited native model.
discussions.notes: The published DOI and PMID:42709820 were verified, and the bioRxiv API links the author preprint to this publication. Publisher/full-text routes were unsuccessful and the preprint XML returned HTTP 429 after backoff on 2026-10-04. Full Results and Methods have not been inspected. Its molecular assignments, repeat interpretation, model stoichiometry and specimen taxon are not curated here. Existing numerical fields remain explicitly tied to the 2017 or 2020 Chlamydomonas experiments, not a universal architecture.

evidence.notes: Metadata and abstract inspected only; follow-up source, not evidence for an asserted molecular claim in this record.

discussions.prompt: Do not label neighboring triplet deposits as cartwheel maps.

No isolated cartwheel deposit is identified by those entry descriptions, so they are not added as exact xrefs or cartwheel-specific datasets. records.label: basal body cartwheel inner density
records.definition: A morphologically distinct subassembly within the lumen of a microbial basal-body cartwheel hub, observed as a central electron-dense unit separate from the surrounding hub rings and radial spokes. Such units can repeat along the cartwheel axis, with nonuniform occupancy.

curation_history.changes: Scaffolded by scripts/new_record.py

Added four native microbial CID examples, scoped axial spacings, distinct reconstruction classes and an inspected unmodified CC BY figure. Declined unsupported hub-protein and speculative host Poc1B assignments and documented the unread newer full-text boundary.

canonical_examples.note: In-situ cryo-FIB/cryo-ET of mat3-4 cells resolves CIDs within the hubs of mature basal bodies and pro-basal bodies. Figure 1 distinguishes the inner densities from the surrounding hub. The Results paragraph discussing the Figure 3 reconstruction also reports raw regions without CID, citing Appendix Figure S4D.

Cryo-ET of isolated cortical units and cartwheel averaging resolve CIDs in Figures 2 and 3. Preparation used d4-2 and Delta-CenBP1 strains; the cited figure is not assigned to one strain. These are native specimens, not recombinant SAS-6 rings.

Basal bodies isolated from NEG cells differentiated into flagellates show CIDs in Figure 2 and Figure EV2. Periodicities were assessed in undamaged regions because preparation often compressed the basal bodies. This does not assert CID presence in the amoeboid stage.

Purified basal bodies from flagellates extracted from Reticulitermes speratus hindguts were examined by cryo-ET and subtomogram averaging. Figure 2F-J and Figure EV1 describe 55% and 45% subvolume classes that can occur within one basal body, not separate taxa or population prevalence estimates.

physical_properties.context: Axial spacing between CIDs in mature Chlamydomonas reinhardtii basal bodies imaged in situ in mat3-4 cells; Klena Figure 1, plotted in panel H of the original graphic. Mean and SD, n=18 measured distances, not 18 cells or protein copies. This is not CID diameter, hub-ring spacing, or a universal repeat.

Axial CID spacing in Chlamydomonas reinhardtii pro-basal bodies in the same in-situ mat3-4 study; Klena Figure 1. Mean and SD, n=5 measured distances. Mature and pro-basal-body measurements are separate observations, not a time course or a demonstrated developmental change.

Axial spacing between CID elements in the Trichonympha agilis 55% central-cartwheel subvolume class, Nazarov Figure 2H. Reported mean and error; the caption does not name the error statistic. N=9 denotes 2D measurements from the subtomogram average, not independent cells. The 55% is a reconstruction-class fraction, not biological occupancy.

Distance between two CID elements in the Trichonympha agilis 45% central-cartwheel class, Nazarov Figure EV1C; N=1 2D measurement from the subtomogram average, with no error estimate. An intervening single hub unit lacks a neighboring CID. This is not a species-wide mean or a second universal repeat.

discussions.prompt: Keep the named inner-density subassembly distinct from the cartwheel hub and its proteins.
discussions.rationale: A density-defined cellular subassembly is not a protein assignment, and the CID abbreviation has been used at two levels of granularity.
discussions.notes: Hidden/ignored-inclusive searches and parsed identities, labels and synonyms across 872 prior records found no standalone CID record. Complete QuickGO searches for cartwheel inner density (229 hits), cartwheel inner ring (273), CID (0), and filamentous cartwheel (46) returned no exact term. This record follows Klena's convention of one whole central CID, rather than each of the nine connected densities in the older usage. It is part of the cartwheel, not an is-a cartwheel or SAS-6 ring. Kind OTHER and broad GO:0005575 retain unresolved molecular classification; cartwheel, central hub, spokes and microtubule lumen are not exact synonyms.

discussions.prompt: Identify native microbial CID constituents and test CID-specific biological roles.
discussions.rationale: Morphological contacts and structural models do not demonstrate a protein identity, necessity, or causal mechanism.
discussions.notes: The inspected 2020 studies propose roles in hub-ring organization, symmetry, stability or polarity but do not establish CID-specific perturbation mechanisms. No protein components, stoichiometry, essentiality, GO function, trait link or causal graph is inferred from proximity to the hub. Direct molecular localization and structure-specific functional evidence are needed.

discussions.prompt: Do not transfer SAS-6 hub assignments or speculative fly Poc1B assignments into microbial CID composition.
discussions.rationale: A surrounding hub protein and a proposed analogous host structure do not identify this microbial subassembly.
discussions.notes: SAS-6 ring fitting describes the surrounding hub, not a CID sequence assignment. The inspected 2019 Poc1B study explicitly speculates that the atypical Drosophila sperm PCL tubule represents CID and that Poc1B might contribute to human CID. Its Discussion 4.2 does not directly localize Poc1B to the microbial CIDs represented here. No Poc1B, SAS-6 or Bld10 family is imported merely from neighboring architecture or analogy.

discussions.prompt: Resolve whether discrete CID and filamentous CID share molecular identity or homology.
discussions.rationale: A similar location does not establish equivalence of discontinuous central units and a continuous axial filament.
discussions.notes: Nazarov describes discrete CIDs in Trichonympha and a continuous filamentous cartwheel inner density, fCID, in Teranympha mirabilis. The source calls their relationship potential and leaves molecular nature unresolved. fCID is not an exact synonym, component assignment or additional canonical example of this record. Its reported diameter is not transferred to discrete CID.

discussions.prompt: Reconcile class- and reference-frame-specific CID polarity without imposing universal occupancy.
discussions.rationale: Different sample preparations, resolution limits and geometric reference axes can produce distinct observations.
discussions.notes: Klena did not resolve the asymmetric CID localization reported by Nazarov and notes possible resolution or species differences. Nazarov describes distal placement relative to the hub; its Figure EV1D instead describes proximal placement relative to the spoke-density axis in the 45% class, while the main text also discusses distal spoke-relative placement. The directional wording is retained as unresolved, not collapsed into a universal displacement. Both studies show regions or hub levels without CID, so a mean axial spacing is not obligatory occupancy at every ring pair.

discussions.prompt: Inspect the full 2026 Trichonympha study before extending molecular or mechanistic claims.
discussions.rationale: An abstract and deposited hub model cannot substitute for Results and Methods or identify an unmodeled density.
discussions.notes: PMID:42709820 metadata and abstract were inspected, including the abstract's description of asymmetric CID densities and possible polarity/stability roles. Publisher and author-preprint full-text routes were unsuccessful on 2026-10-04; full Results and Methods remain uninspected. Native RCSB entry and polymer-entity metadata for PDB:9ZMK identify only SAS-6, not a CID protein. The deposited eight-chain hub model is not CID stoichiometry. No 2026 numerical, compositional or causal assertion is imported here; the measured properties remain tied to the inspected 2020 experiments.

discussions.prompt: Keep CID spacing, hub architecture, reconstruction processing and taxonomic scope separate.
discussions.rationale: Image labels, symmetry processing and measurement counts are not interchangeable with molecular or population evidence.
discussions.notes: Klena Figure 1 distinguishes approximately 4-nm hub spacing from approximately 8.7-nm CID spacing; neither is a CID diameter or protein copy number. Nazarov's N denotes 2D measurements from averaged maps. Subvolume fractions, imposed rotations and reconstruction resolution are not biological replicates, population prevalence or native dimensions. Examples are specific observed microbial preparations, not universal clade distributions. Only the single-species Chlamydomonas Figure 1 is hosted unchanged; its panel lettering follows the graphic because the JATS caption letters are inconsistent. Symmetrized panels are processed observations, not unprocessed tomograms or independent evidence of ninefold symmetry.

records.label: basal body D2-rod
records.definition: A longitudinal subassembly at the periphery of a microbial ciliary basal-body or pro-basal-body cartwheel, linking the outer radial-spoke ends along the cartwheel axis. In characterized Chlamydomonas and Paramecium regions it is distinguishable from the pinhead and extends into the proximal cartwheel segment beyond the microtubule wall.

curation_history.changes: Scaffolded by scripts/new_record.py

Added D2-rod cartwheel parthood, native Chlamydomonas and Paramecium evidence, scoped radial-position measurement and inspected CC BY figure. Distinguished D1, pinhead, reconstituted arrays and proposed human CPAP localization from native microbial D2 composition; retained molecular and dataset boundaries without unsupported components or causal claims.

canonical_examples.note: Ninefold-symmetrized cryo-ET of isolated CW-15 pro-basal bodies resolves peripheral D2 densities in the core cartwheel. Figure 1 includes a proximal segment lacking pinhead and microtubules. This is native isolated material, distinct from the paper's recombinant arrays.

Cryo-ET and symmetrized cartwheel views resolve longitudinal D2 connections in Figure EV3 and Figure 3. Methods describe cortical units isolated from d4-2 and Delta-CenBP1; these figures are not assigned to one strain. No Chlamydomonas numerical measurement is transferred here.

functions.label: ciliary basal body organization
functions.description: Connects peripheral radial-spoke ends along the cartwheel axis in the characterized Chlamydomonas and Paramecium proximal regions. This observed arrangement does not establish a stiffness, a growth mechanism, or D2-specific essentiality.

evidence.notes: The proximal-extension Results name the vertical D2 connections as D2-rod. Figure EV3 distinguishes the D2-rod from the pinhead, including in the protruding cartwheel segment; Figure 3 resolves D1-to-D2 radial connections.

physical_properties.context: Radial distance from the hub margin to the D2 density in isolated Chlamydomonas reinhardtii CW-15 pro-basal bodies, Guichard et al. 2017 Figure 1f; reported value and error, n=13 measurements from five tomograms. The caption does not specify the error statistic. Methods selected spokes ending in visible D1 and/or D2 densities for these distance measurements. This is a position relative to the hub edge, not the hub center, rod length, diameter, axial repeat or molecule count.

evidence.notes: Klena et al. 2020, PMID:32954513. Checksum-verified PMC7667884.1 Results, species preparation, cartwheel averaging Methods, Figure EV3 and Data availability inspected. The original mixed-species EV3 figure was visually inspected but is not hosted here. Chlamydomonas in-situ mat3-4 mature and pro-basal-body views distinguish D2-rod from pinhead and microtubule wall.

Guichard et al. 2017, PMID:28332496. Checksum-verified PMC5376648.1 native and reconstitution Results, Discussion, isolation, cryo-ET and measurement Methods, Figure 1 and Data availability inspected. The original Figure 1 was visually inspected. Native D2 morphology is distinguished from recombinant core-cartwheel sufficiency.

discussions.prompt: Distinguish the D2-rod from the cartwheel and its neighboring densities.
discussions.rationale: A named peripheral subassembly is not the entire cartwheel or a single asserted protein.
discussions.notes: Hidden/ignored-inclusive repository searches and parsed identifier, label and synonym checks found no standalone D2-rod record before creation. Complete QuickGO queries D2 rod (49 results), cartwheel D2 (15) and centriole D2 (37) found no exact cellular-component identity. Bacterial flagellar rods and cyclin-D2 complexes are different entities. The cartwheel is parthood, not is-a. D1, the hub, cartwheel inner density, pinhead and triplet base are not exact synonyms. D2 density is related terminology for the peripheral cross-sectional feature, not an asserted exact synonym for a complete longitudinal rod. OTHER and the broad GO:0005575 parent retain unresolved molecular classification without asserting a proven multiprotein composition or filament architecture.

discussions.prompt: Identify the native microbial D2-rod constituents and a narrower molecular class.
discussions.rationale: Morphology and coassembly do not assign a complete native proteome to a resolved density.
discussions.notes: Direct molecular localization or a sequence-resolved D2-rod model is needed before adding components, stoichiometry, family groundings or D2-specific essentiality. Neither the native 2017 cross sections nor the 2020 longitudinal reconstructions provide those assignments.

discussions.prompt: Keep core-cartwheel reconstitution and human localization models separate from microbial D2 composition.
discussions.rationale: Membership in a broader assembly or a proposed counterpart is not a native D2-specific assignment.
discussions.notes: Full-length CrSAS-6 plus Bld10 residues 1061-1641 forms core-cartwheel-like arrays with D1- and D2-like peripheral densities in the 2017 assay. CrSAS-6_NL arrays retain D1 but lack D2. These results do not identify which protein forms the native D2-rod; the explicit SAS-6 assignment to D1 is not transferred to D2. The inspected 2024 human U-ExM study proposes CPAP as a D2 constituent from localization and prior fibril formation. That human model does not establish microbial D2 membership. No SAS-6, Bld10/Cep135, CPAP, pinhead protein or tubulin component is asserted here solely from these neighboring or model-system observations.

discussions.prompt: Keep radial position, axial organization and assembly models distinct.
discussions.rationale: Processing symmetry and adjacent structural repeats do not supply a molecular count or D2 growth rate.
discussions.notes: The 45.6-nm Figure 1f measurement is a hub-margin-to-D2 distance. The roughly 25-nm spacing in the 2020 cartwheel analysis concerns D1 merged-spoke units, not a demonstrated D2-rod repeat. Ninefold symmetrization improves contrast and is not a count of D2 protein molecules. The 2020 Paramecium Results and Methods give different cartwheel averaging counts (8 tomograms/235 boxes versus 7 tomograms/232 retained subvolumes); neither is promoted to biological stoichiometry or used for the 2017 measurement. Spatial extension without visible pinhead is not a time-resolved assembly sequence. No mechanical modulus, causal graph, broad clade distribution or motility trait is asserted.

discussions.prompt: Do not substitute neighboring maps for a D2-rod-specific deposit.
discussions.rationale: Sharing an article does not establish structural equivalence or sufficient map coverage.
discussions.notes: The 2017 Data availability statement points to the paper and its supplementary material. The 2020 paper lists EMD-10726 through EMD-10729; native released-entry titles describe A-C-linker or microtubule-triplet reconstructions, not an isolated D2-rod map. They are not added as exact xrefs or D2-specific datasets. This is a bounded decision about those deposits, not a claim that no relevant dataset exists elsewhere. The single-species 2017 Figure 1 supplies the hosted native D2 visual evidence; 2020 EV3 supplies the inspected longitudinal context but contains two taxa.

records.label: basal body filamentous cartwheel inner density
records.definition: An apparently continuous filamentous subassembly extending longitudinally within the lumen of a microbial basal-body cartwheel hub. It is morphologically distinguishable from the surrounding hub rings and spokes and from discontinuous cartwheel inner-density units.

curation_history.changes: Scaffolded by scripts/new_record.py

Added native morphology-defined fCID identity, scoped Teranympha specimen and approximate diameter, distinct EMDB classes and an inspected unmodified CC BY figure. Preserved specimen-assignment and deposition-name caveats, reconstruction processing, and unresolved composition, function and CID homology.

canonical_examples.note: Native basal bodies from hindgut flagellates of Reticulitermes speratus were examined by cryo-ET and subtomogram averaging. Preparation began with mixed Trichonympha agilis and Teranympha mirabilis cells, with a sedimentation step enriching the latter. Whole-cell morphology distinguished resin-embedded species; purified cryo-ET basal bodies were assigned using fCID presence or absence. This retains the source's morphology-based attribution, not an independent molecular identification. Figure 4 resolves fCID in both 64% and 36% cartwheel subvolume classes, which can coexist within one basal body.

physical_properties.context: Approximate diameter of the filamentous cartwheel inner density in purified Teranympha mirabilis basal bodies, Figure 4F-G and the corresponding Results. The value is reported for both 64% and 36% central-cartwheel reconstruction classes. No sample count or error statistic is supplied for this diameter. It is not the approximately 23-nm hub diameter, an axial hub/spoke spacing, or a measurement of discrete CID.

The sample and supramolecule free-text names instead say Teranympha agilis; this discrepancy is retained, not adopted as the organism identity. The paper and structured organism field support the curated taxon. Percentages are classified subvolumes, not species prevalence. evidence.notes: Nazarov et al. 2020, PMID:32954505. Checksum-verified PMC7667878.1 dedicated Teranympha Results, conserved-architecture Discussion, Figure 4 and EV3 captions, specimen preparation, cryo-ET acquisition and subtomogram processing Methods inspected. Original Figure 4 visually inspected. Supports a named continuous inner filament, not its molecular composition or proven function.

discussions.prompt: Keep the continuous inner filament distinct from the cartwheel hub and discrete CID.
discussions.rationale: A named morphological subassembly is not a single protein or an entire cartwheel.
discussions.notes: Hidden/ignored-inclusive alias, slug, DOI and PMID searches and parsed identities across 873 prior records found no standalone fCID record; the existing CID record explicitly excludes it. Searches also included FLS as a possible older name lead without adopting it as an asserted synonym. Complete native GO queries for filamentous cartwheel inner density (275 hits), fCID (0), and Teranympha cartwheel (0) found no exact term. FILAMENT describes the observed form without asserting a protein family. GO:0110165 requires granularity above a protein complex, which is not established for this molecularly unassigned entity; broad GO:0005575 is retained. The cartwheel is part_of, not is-a. Hub rings, spokes, microtubule wall and discrete CID are not synonyms.

discussions.prompt: Identify native fCID constituents and test filament-specific biological roles.
discussions.rationale: Morphology and proximity do not identify molecules or demonstrate necessity.
discussions.notes: The inspected primary study leaves molecular nature unresolved. Its modeled SAS-6 rings concern the surrounding hub, not a sequence assignment to fCID. No component family, protein accession, stoichiometry, essentiality, GO function, trait link or causal graph is inferred. Direct localization and filament-specific perturbations would be needed before importing these claims.

discussions.prompt: Do not transfer SAS-6 hub-ring fitting to the luminal filament.
discussions.rationale: The filament and the protein-containing hub are separate structures in the source maps.
discussions.notes: The paper fits CrSAS-6 ring models to hub densities and studies recombinant cartwheel-like arrays. Neither identifies fCID composition. SAS-6 is therefore not added as a filament constituent merely because its rings surround fCID; no surrounding pinhead, linker or microtubule protein is borrowed from Figure 4H-K.

discussions.prompt: Resolve the molecular relationship to discrete CID and the filament's connections and helicity.
discussions.rationale: Similar position and appearance do not establish homology, molecular equivalence or dynamics.
discussions.notes: The Discussion contrasts continuous Teranympha fCID with discontinuous Trichonympha CID and leaves shared molecular identity or evolutionary history unresolved. It describes small possible links in the 36% class and leaves other contacts and helical organization open. Figure 4 notes off-center positions as suggestive of flexibility, not a measured mechanical property. No fixed helical pitch, handedness, elasticity or conserved CID-like polarity is asserted. Related densities in other taxa are leads, not canonical examples here.

discussions.prompt: Preserve morphology-based specimen attribution and reconstruction processing boundaries.
discussions.rationale: Classified subvolumes and imposed symmetry are not independent organisms or molecular evidence.
discussions.notes: The source distinguishes intact resin-embedded species by whole-cell morphology and isolated cryo-ET basal bodies by fCID presence. This is not a molecular taxon assay or an unbiased prevalence survey. Central-cartwheel maps used C9 symmetry; later re-centered sector analysis relaxed symmetry to C1. The Results also report fCID in raw tomograms (Appendix Figure S1E) and non-symmetrized spoke-centered averages (Figure EV2I-P); those source statements were read, but these supplemental graphics were not visually inspected for this record. The 64% and 36% classes are not independent taxa and can coexist within one basal body. No native ninefold filament symmetry is inferred from processed maps.

discussions.prompt: Reconcile the free-text sample names in EMD-10922 and EMD-10923 with their structured taxonomy.
discussions.rationale: A mismatched sample name must not silently create a different organism assertion.
discussions.notes: Both native entries have Teranympha mirabilis in their titles and natural_source organism fields, with NCBI taxon 285686 and the verified Nazarov DOI/PMID. Their sample and supramolecule names instead say Teranympha agilis. The paper and native taxonomy support Teranympha mirabilis. The datasets retain the discrepancy and class distinctions; no third-party metadata was edited.

discussions.prompt: Keep filament dimensions separate from surrounding hub and spoke measurements.
discussions.rationale: The same multipanel figure contains several structures with different measured quantities.
discussions.notes: Only the approximate 7-nm filament diameter is curated as a physical property. Hub diameters, hub/spoke periodicities, whole cartwheel-bearing-region lengths and map resolution are not filament dimensions. Neither a sample count nor an error statistic for the diameter is supplied in Figure 4. The original single-species CC BY 4.0 Figure 4 is hosted unchanged; panel labels and 10-nm scale bars were visually checked. Segmentation colors are illustrative, not molecular boundaries, and the H-K peripheral maps are context rather than evidence of filament composition.

records.label: basal body inner scaffold
records.definition: A proteinaceous meshwork lining the lumen-facing surface of the central basal-body wall and interconnecting neighboring triplet microtubules through multiple attachment sites.

curation_history.changes: Scaffolded by scripts/new_record.py

Added bounded Tetrahymena inner-scaffold composition, structural-contact graph, EMDB datasets and licensed density preview; preserved unknown molecular assignments, assay scope and family-grounding uncertainty.
added 2 verified UniProtKB protein_example(s).

components.label: POC1 family protein
components.grounding_notes: InterPro IPR050505 combines WDR55 and POC1 and is broader than this class. IPR020472 is a WD40 repeat, not an exact POC1 family. The inspected POC1 accession Q229Z6 and family searches do not justify either as exact identity.
components.role: Anchors the scaffold at the central-core A-B inner junction. Its WD40 domain contacts an unidentified stem protein connecting toward the scaffold. This role does not assign Poc1 to the central-core B-C junction.

evidence.notes: Figures 5D-E and 6C combine model fitting and loss of the corresponding density in poc1 deletion material. Scaffold density is nearly absent in the mutant; initial assembly versus subsequent maintenance is not separated.

protein_examples.role: Representative reviewed UniProtKB entry for gene POC1, which UniProt lists under the primary name TTHERM_01308010, in Tetrahymena thermophila SB210. Identifier for the component's declared gene symbol; it is not itself evidence that the protein is part of this structure.

evidence.notes: Pearson CG et al. 2009, ‘Basal body stability and ciliogenesis requires the conserved component Poc1.’, J Cell Biol. ECO:0000269 experimental evidence cited by UniProt for the 'Cytoplasm, cytoskeleton, cilium basal body' localisation of Q229Z6.

components.label: FAM161A family protein
components.grounding_notes: The paper identifies a Tetrahymena Fam161A homolog at TTHERM_00052590. Its unreviewed SB210 UniProt entry Q23CT1 matches IPR019579, Protein FAM161A/B, and IPR051655, FAM161. These combined or broader families do not establish an exact FAM161A-only grounding. No strain-paired protein example is inferred.
components.role: Inner-scaffold-associated constituent supported by endogenous-tag localization at the basal-body core and reduced basal-body signal after Poc1 loss. Its exact position within the scaffold and direct binding partners in Tetrahymena remain unassigned; additional distal localization is present.

evidence.notes: Results and Figures 5A, 6A and S5 support the homolog assignment and localization. Unlike Poc1, Fam161A has no assigned molecular cryo-ET density here. Human-protein interaction results cited by the article are not direct evidence of a Tetrahymena Poc1-Fam161A contact.

protein_examples.role: Representative unreviewed (TrEMBL) UniProtKB entry for gene FAM161A, which UniProt lists under the primary name TTHERM_00052590, in Tetrahymena thermophila SB210. Identifier for the component's declared gene symbol; it is not itself evidence that the protein is part of this structure.

evidence.notes: UniProtKB unreviewed (TrEMBL) entry Q23CT1 for gene FAM161A in Tetrahymena thermophila SB210. Establishes the accession and gene identity only; the component's membership in this structure rests on the record's own sources.

canonical_examples.note: Cryotomography of isolated wild-type and poc1-deletion basal bodies resolves the central-core scaffold and its attachments. Endogenous Fam161A tagging and fluorescence imaging provide complementary localization evidence. Methods list B2086 and SB1969 backgrounds; this example is species-level, not an asserted strain-specific pairing with SB210 reference sequences.

functions.label: intertriplet cohesion
functions.description: Provides luminal connections between neighboring basal-body triplet microtubules in the central core. In the studied Tetrahymena material, backfitted reconstructions support stacked rings rather than a universal helical geometry.

evidence.notes: Figure 5B-C and Figure S4E support the intertriplet meshwork and ring arrangement. This structural function does not assert a measured force threshold or selective scaffold-dependent rescue of basal-body shape.

causal_graphs.title: Poc1 anchors a luminal intertriplet scaffold
causal_graphs.description: Structural contacts and a separately bounded localization dependency in the Tetrahymena basal-body central core.
causal_graphs.scope_notes: Contact edges describe fitted cryo-ET density, not temporal assembly order. The fluorescence edge describes basal-body Fam161A signal, not a direct Poc1-Fam161A interaction or an exclusively scaffold-specific measurement. Poc1 deletion affects multiple basal-body modules, so this graph does not attribute the entire mechanical phenotype to scaffold loss.

discussions.prompt: Distinguish the inner scaffold from adjacent basal-body structures.
discussions.rationale: The imaged intertriplet meshwork is a physical entity, not a single protein or the whole basal body.
discussions.notes: Hidden- and ignored-inclusive repository searches found no existing identity record. Complete GO searches for scaffold, centriole and intertriplet found no exact cellular-component term. GO:0140180 is a molecular function, not this structure. GO:0140535 is a broader is-a parent; GO:0036064 is parthood. The proximal A-C linker, cartwheel, pinhead and transition-zone Y-links are distinct. Inner junctions form attachment interfaces, not scaffold synonyms.

discussions.prompt: Resolve exact POC1 and FAM161A family groundings without substituting broader families.
discussions.rationale: A combined family or domain is not an exact identity for a narrower component class.
discussions.notes: Both components remain REVIEWED_LABEL_ONLY. The inspected Fam161A homolog accession describes SB210, whereas endogenous tagging uses other backgrounds. No strain-paired protein example or unverified A/B orthology is asserted.

discussions.prompt: Identify the stem and other attachment proteins and locate Fam161A within the scaffold.
discussions.rationale: The two named classes are not a complete composition or a molecular model of every scaffold density.
discussions.notes: Fam161A localization supports scaffold association but does not identify a particular density or direct Tetrahymena Poc1 contact. A03 and B-C attachment identities remain unresolved. Poc1-knockout material loses most scaffold density, including in complete-triplet subclasses, but a reduced A03 density remains. Assembly requirements, stoichiometry and attachment redundancy need further experiments; essentialities are UNKNOWN.

discussions.prompt: Do not import nearby proteins or human scaffold composition as demonstrated Tetrahymena constituents.
discussions.rationale: Colocalization and evidence from another organism do not by themselves establish the same molecular placement.
discussions.notes: Poc16/WDR90 colocalizes in the core but its predicted shape does not fit the Poc1-containing A-B junction density; the paper does not assign it to this scaffold. Human POC5 and Centrin2 assignments and human Poc1B-Fam161A binding are not copied as Tetrahymena evidence. Microtubules are attachment substrates, not additional scaffold protein families. Unidentified densities remain open questions rather than invented components.

discussions.prompt: Keep mechanical interpretations and geometric measurements within their assay scope.
discussions.rationale: Poc1 loss affects multiple modules, and preparation-induced deformation is not a direct in-cell force measurement.
discussions.notes: Stacked rings are supported in the studied Tetrahymena material, not a universal scaffold geometry. Isolated mutant flattening can reflect grid preparation. High-temperature phenotypes do not isolate a scaffold-only mechanism. The wild-type Fam161A temperature comparison in Figure 6A has p = 0.0560 and is not treated as a significant decrease. U-ExM scale bars refer to acquired expanded images, not expansion-corrected biological size.

records.label: basal body pinhead
records.definition: A proteinaceous subassembly on the luminal face of the A-tubule in the proximal region of a microbial ciliary basal body or pro-basal body, forming the peripheral connection toward the cartwheel spokes. In Chlamydomonas reinhardtii it has a bent pinbody and two pinfeet attached to protofilament A3.

curation_history.changes: Scaffolded by scripts/new_record.py

Added pinhead architecture, Chlamydomonas example, 8-nm repeat, scoped Bld10 membership, native EMDB dataset and inspected CC BY figure. Kept density assignments and inaccessible full-text follow-up explicit; no universal composition or assembly chronology asserted.

components.label: Bld10/Cep135
components.grounding_notes: Native InterPro IPR051877 includes both CEP135 and TSGA10, as confirmed by reviewed human UniProt entries Q66GS9 and Q9BZW7. It is broader than Bld10/Cep135; PF30381 and PF30378 are domain matches, not exact whole-protein family equivalents.
components.role: Cartwheel spoke-tip constituent in Chlamydomonas, supported by the primary report of immuno-EM localization and truncation morphology. This is not a sequence assignment to PinB, PinF1 or PinF2 in the subtomogram average, nor a claim that Bld10 is confined to the pinhead.

evidence.notes: The inspected primary abstract reports Bld10 as a major spoke-tip component based on immuno-EM and truncated-protein morphology. Only the abstract was accessible; full Results, Methods and figures were not inspected. Detailed mutant measurements are not curated here.
Native UniProt JSON verifies accession, recommended name, gene, taxon and Swiss-Prot status; it is not independent pinhead imaging.
Membership is supported at the inspected primary-abstract level, not by a residue-resolved model.

canonical_examples.note: Cryo-ET and local subtomogram classification of isolated nuclear-flagellar apparatuses resolve pinheads in pro-basal bodies and the proximal region of mother basal bodies. This is not an assertion of pinhead occupancy along the entire basal-body length.

functions.label: ciliary basal body organization
functions.description: Forms the peripheral structural connection between cartwheel spokes and the A-tubule wall in the characterized Chlamydomonas proximal region. This observed connection does not by itself establish a force response, a length-control mechanism or an assembly time course.

evidence.notes: Results and Figures 1 and 2 resolve the connection and the A3-associated pinbody/pinfeet morphology.

physical_properties.context: Axial pinhead repeat in the Chlamydomonas proximal mother-basal-body and pro-basal-body reconstruction, Li et al. 2019 Figure 2D. Each pair of pinfeet associates with an alpha/beta-tubulin dimer on A3. This is not the length of a pinhead or a repeat generalized to other species.

datasets.title: Chlamydomonas pinhead with associated partial A-tubule
datasets.description: Local subtomogram average of the pinhead and attached A-tubule region, identified as structure 5 in Table 3 of Li et al. 2019.
datasets.notes: Released EMDB metadata explicitly identifies the pinhead-associated map, taxon 3055, strain CC849 and the primary DOI/PMID. Its 4763 subtomograms and 23.1-angstrom resolution are reconstruction provenance, not biological counts or dimensions. The map includes tubulin and is not an exact xref for the pinhead alone. No map volume is hosted.

evidence.notes: Li et al. 2019, PMID:30741631. Checksum-verified PMC6384029.1 JATS pinhead Results, Discussion, reconstruction and periodicity-control Methods, Table 3 and Figure 2 inspected. The original Figure 2 was visually inspected; no sequence assignment follows from its densities.

Hiraki et al. 2007, PMID:17900905. Primary abstract inspected through Europe PMC; publisher PDF and full-text routes were inaccessible on 2026-10-04. Only the abstract-supported Bld10 spoke-tip membership is used.

discussions.prompt: Distinguish the pinhead from its cartwheel and microtubule neighbors.
discussions.rationale: A named peripheral assembly is neither an entire basal body nor a single protein.
discussions.notes: Hidden/ignored-inclusive repository searches and parsed identity/synonym checks found mentions but no standalone record. Complete QuickGO searches for pinhead, pinfoot, pinbody, centriole pinhead and cartwheel spoke tip found no exact cellular-component identity. Axonemal radial-spoke terms denote a different assembly. GO:0032991 is a broader class; basal body and pro-basal body are parthood. PinB and PinF1/PinF2 are morphological regions, not identified protein families. The hub, spokes, D2-rod, triplet base, A-C linker, inner scaffold and tubulin wall are not exact synonyms. The record does not impose an obligate cartwheel parthood relation on every pinhead-containing region.

discussions.prompt: Resolve the pinhead proteome and exact Bld10/Cep135 family grounding.
discussions.rationale: Localization and domain matches do not assign all resolved densities or a complete proteome.
discussions.notes: Bld10 membership is retained at the explicitly stated primary-abstract level. Obtain lawful full text of Hiraki 2007 and Noga 2022 before curating domain-specific locations or mutant dimensions. PMC/publisher/Europe PMC full-text routes for Noga were unsuccessful; the PSI DORA item psi:45372 marks its deposited PDF restricted to the intranet, and no restricted file was requested. Its public abstract concerns inter-triplet crosslinks and does not make those links exact pinhead synonyms. Bld10 remains REVIEWED_LABEL_ONLY because IPR051877 also includes TSGA10. Other constituents, stoichiometry and pinhead-specific essentiality remain unresolved.

discussions.prompt: Avoid transferring cartwheel and triplet identities into the pinhead.
discussions.rationale: Being part of the same basal body does not establish membership in every subassembly.
discussions.notes: SAS-6 is discussed as a spoke constituent, but the inspected 2019 map does not identify SAS-6 in PinB or either foot; no SAS-6 pinhead component is asserted. Alpha/beta tubulin supplies the adjoining A3 lattice and is not listed as pinhead composition. The 2020 Bld10 assignment to the triplet base is expressly hypothetical and is not transferred here as a density-resolved model.

discussions.prompt: Keep repeat measurements separate from map dimensions and assembly hypotheses.
discussions.rationale: Static reconstruction, image processing and proposed mechanics answer different questions.
discussions.notes: Li et al. tested segment length, overlap, masking, initial reference and mother/pro-basal-body sampling when assessing the 8-nm pinhead repeat. The 19-nm final reconstruction window and 23.1-angstrom resolution are not biological lengths. Pinhead-tip low resolution is consistent with flexibility, not a measured spring constant. Iris-like twist classes, spoke strain, length control and the five-step triplet assembly scheme are interpretations of static data, not a direct time course. No kinetic causal graph or motility trait is asserted. The 2020 Paramecium analysis warns that initial 8.5-nm picking biased its pinhead reconstruction; no repeat from that map is substituted for the explicitly Chlamydomonas-scoped 2019 measurement.

records.label: basal body triplet base
records.definition: A linker in the proximal region of a microbial ciliary basal body that connects the pinhead to the A-C linker. In Paramecium tetraurelia reconstructions it extends to the ArmB region of the A-C linker.

curation_history.changes: Scaffolded by scripts/new_record.py

Added directly imaged triplet-base connectivity, two species examples, approximate Paramecium span, scoped EMDB provenance and inspected CC BY figure. Retained molecular identity, periodicity and mechanics as unresolved; no hypothesized protein membership or broad distribution asserted.

canonical_examples.note: Ninefold-symmetrized cryo-ET cross sections and a focused subtomogram average resolve the pinhead-to-A-C-linker connection. Methods describe cortical units isolated from d4-2 and Delta-CenBP1; Figure 5 is not assigned to one strain. The proximal-region analysis used 11 uncompressed tomograms containing 16 centrioles with intact proximal regions.
In situ cryo-ET of FIB-milled mat3-4 cells and ninefold-symmetrized cross sections show the link in Figure 4. The Paramecium focused-map measurement is not transferred to this species.

functions.label: ciliary basal body organization
functions.description: Provides a structural connection between the pinhead and A-C linker in the imaged proximal region. This is an observed spatial arrangement, not proof of a mechanical stiffness, essentiality or assembly time course.

evidence.notes: Figures 4 and 5 and the accompanying Results identify the connecting density; the Paramecium average locates its A-C-linker contact on ArmB.

physical_properties.context: Approximate pinhead-to-A-C-linker span annotated as about 35 nm in the Paramecium tetraurelia proximal-triplet reconstruction, Figure 5A, and described in the Discussion. No replicate distribution or uncertainty is reported for this annotation. It is not an axial repeat or a universal length.

datasets.title: Paramecium microtubule triplet from the start of the proximal region
datasets.description: Public proximal-triplet reconstruction from the study that visualizes the triplet-base connection. The deposited entity includes the microtubule wall and neighboring densities, not an isolated triplet base.
datasets.notes: Native released EMDB metadata verifies the start-of-proximal-region title, taxon 5888, DOI and PMID:32954513. The paper lists EMD-10726 through EMD-10729 in Data availability. EMD-10728 denotes the distal comparison; EMD-10726 and EMD-10727 denote A-C-linker-focused maps. Their sample-name fields repeat start-region wording despite different entry titles, so titles are used to distinguish these deposits. No exact structure xref or hosted map volume is asserted.

evidence.notes: Klena et al. 2020, PMID:32954513. Checksum-verified PMC7667884.1 JATS Results, Discussion, species preparation and A-C-linker averaging Methods, Figure 5 and Data availability inspected. Figure 5 was visually inspected; its low-threshold triplet-base density is not a sequence-resolved model.

discussions.prompt: Keep the triplet base distinct from adjacent basal-body modules.
discussions.rationale: A named linker is not the entire cartwheel, pinhead or A-C linker.
discussions.notes: Hidden/ignored-inclusive repository searches and parsed record identity/synonym checks found mentions but no standalone record. Complete QuickGO searches for triplet base (119 results) and centriole triplet base (141 results) found no exact cellular-component term. The ontology root GO:0005575 is retained only as a deliberately broad class pending molecular classification; OTHER avoids asserting a proven multiprotein composition or filament architecture. GO:0110165 would assert granularity above a protein complex, which is also unresolved. Basal body is parthood, not is-a. No obligatory cartwheel or pro-basal-body parthood is inferred. D2-rod, A-tusk, pinhead, ArmB, cartwheel spokes and the A-C linker are not exact synonyms or separately identified triplet-base components.

discussions.prompt: Resolve triplet-base molecular composition and a narrower structure class.
discussions.rationale: A proposed coiled-coil assignment is not a demonstrated molecular identity.
discussions.notes: Klena 2020 explicitly leaves molecular nature unknown and hypothesizes Bld10/Cep135 membership from length, appearance and prior localization. The inspected Cai 2025 Tetrahymena Discussion still describes the C-terminal CEP135 triplet-base assignment as proposed; its direct N-terminal CEP135 assignment is to the A-link, not this density. Consequently no Bld10/Cep135, SAS-6, tubulin or A-C-linker protein is asserted as composition here. Seek direct localization or sequence-resolved triplet-base evidence before assigning components, stoichiometry or protein-family grounding.

discussions.prompt: Separate observed connectivity from periodicity and mechanical hypotheses.
discussions.rationale: Low density and static axial differences do not uniquely specify occupancy, flexibility or chronology.
discussions.notes: The focused Paramecium map required a low contour threshold to show the triplet base. The source offers flexibility or incomplete occupancy as alternatives and could not reliably recover triplet-base or pinhead longitudinal periodicities. The 8.5-nm initial picking interval and 8.4-nm A-C-linker repeat are not triplet-base repeats. The predicted 133-nm CEP135 coiled-coil length is not a measured linker length. A-C linker density persists farther distally when the pinhead/triplet-base connection is weak or absent, so the structures are not interchangeable. The proposed cohesion/stability function and replacement by other densities are not direct force measurements or time-resolved assembly evidence. No causal graph, motility trait or broad taxonomic-distribution claim is asserted.

records.label: basal ring of apical complex
records.definition: An electron dense ring at the most posterior position of the apical complex, from which the subpellicular microtubules originate; formed during an invasive life cycle stage of an apicomplexan parasite.

curation_history.changes: Scaffolded by scripts/new_record.py

Added exact GO basal-ring synonyms, GO apical-complex parthood, Toxoplasma gondii scope, Hu 2006 and GO evidence, a nonmechanistic basal-ring topology graph, and curation discussions for unresolved constituents and the anterior/posterior polar-ring boundary.

Addressed #2247: Separated the active basal-ring topology from preconoidal-ring synonym conflation and qualified conoid-relative position for extrusion. The GO/source conflict and original rationale remain explicit.

synonyms.synonym_text: lower polar ring of apical complex
posterior polar ring of apical complex

taxonomic_distribution.note: Toxoplasma tachyzoites have a lower polar ring at the origin of the subpellicular microtubules. The conoid extends and retracts relative to this ring.

canonical_examples.note: Apicomplexan model in which the conoid fibers, polar rings, intraconoid microtubules and subpellicular microtubules of the apical complex were resolved as distinct cytoskeletal elements.

functions.label: subpellicular microtubule origin
functions.description: The basal ring of the apical complex marks the origin of the subpellicular microtubules; it is distinct from the preconoidal rings at the conoid tip.

evidence.notes: Gene Ontology defines the basal ring of the apical complex by the origin of the subpellicular microtubules.
Hu et al. 2006 distinguish the polar ring from which the 22 subpellicular microtubules originate from the distal preconoidal rings.
Gene Ontology cellular-component term for the basal ring of the apical complex.
Gene Ontology models the basal ring of the apical complex as part of the apicomplexan apical complex.
Hu et al. 2006, Cytoskeletal Components of an Invasion Machine--the Apical Complex of Toxoplasma gondii, PLOS Pathogens.
Hu, Roos and Murray 2002, A novel polymer of tubulin forms the conoid of Toxoplasma gondii. Figure 1 supports state-dependent conoid/ring topology.

causal_graphs.title: The lower polar ring marks the origin of subpellicular microtubules
causal_graphs.description: The lower polar ring marks the origin of Toxoplasma subpellicular microtubules. Its posterior position relative to the conoid is shown for the extruded conoid, not asserted for every conoid state.
causal_graphs.scope_notes: Mature topology, not a protein inventory or microtubule-nucleation mechanism. The posterior-to-conoid edge applies when the conoid is extruded; the conoid lies within the surrounding microtubule scaffold when retracted.

edges.subject: basal_ring_of_apical_complex
edges.description: The basal ring is a cytoskeletal substructure of the apicomplexan apical complex.

evidence.notes: Gene Ontology places the basal ring of the apical complex under the apical-complex cellular-component term.

edges.subject: basal_ring_of_apical_complex
edges.description: When the conoid is extruded, the lower SPMT-origin polar ring lies posterior to the conoid; the ring does not follow the retracting conoid.

evidence.notes: Figure 1 and Results distinguish the moving anterior ring/conoid from the lower polar ring during extension and retraction.
Introduction and Figure 1 distinguish the distal preconoidal rings from the SPMT-origin polar ring.

edges.subject: subpellicular_microtubule
edges.description: Subpellicular microtubules originate from the basal ring of the apical complex.

evidence.notes: Gene Ontology defines the basal ring by the origin of the subpellicular microtubules.

discussions.prompt: Resolve exact basal-ring resident proteins and their source-neutral family groundings.
discussions.rationale: This first basal-ring record captures the GO-delimited lower polar ring and its subpellicular-microtubule origin topology. It leaves protein components out until direct evidence places candidate proteins in the mature basal ring and an exact taxon-neutral family scope can be reviewed.

evidence.notes: Hu et al. 2006 localized candidate proteins to several Toxoplasma apical-cytoskeleton subcompartments.

discussions.prompt: Keep the basal or posterior polar ring distinct from the anterior polar ring of the apical complex.
discussions.rationale: GO:0020032 denotes the lower/posterior/preconoidal ring from which subpellicular microtubules originate, whereas GO:0020031 denotes the anterior polar ring from which conoid fibers originate. The two terms therefore represent adjacent but separate apical-complex rings.

evidence.notes: Gene Ontology lists lower, posterior and preconoidal ring exact synonyms for GO:0020032.
Gene Ontology identifies the anterior polar ring of the apical complex as a distinct term.

discussions.prompt: Separate the GO synonym conflict from the demonstrated basal-ring anatomy.
discussions.rationale: The original discussion faithfully recorded a GO:0020032 exact synonym, preconoidal ring of apical complex. Hu 2006 instead places preconoidal rings at the distal conoid tip and the SPMT-origin polar ring at the base. Hu 2002 distinguishes the moving anterior ring/conoid from the lower ring. Thus the GO synonym conflicts with the primary anatomy and cannot establish biological equivalence.
discussions.resolution_note: Remove the active preconoidal synonym and equivalent anatomical wording while preserving the original discussion, source attribution and dates as historical rationale. Retain GO:0020032 for the SPMT-origin ring and qualify its conoid-relative position by extrusion. Do not equate this one GO ring with all layers of the modern multilayer APR.

evidence.notes: Current authority still lists the conflicting preconoidal exact synonym; this local interpretation does not silently alter the source.
Introduction and Figure 1 explicitly separate distal preconoidal rings from the SPMT-origin polar ring.
Figure 1 distinguishes extended and retracted conoid states.

records.label: cellular bud neck septin collar
records.definition: A tubular structure with flared ends, shaped like an hourglass and composed of highly ordered arrays of septin filaments, that forms at the bud neck of a dividing cell. In S. cerevisiae, this structure is located at the bud neck throughout most of the cell cycle and the septins are fixed within the structure, not exchanging with soluble septins. This septin structure acts as a scaffold for other proteins that function at the bud neck.

These observations distinguish normal triplet architecture from malformed basal-body formation but do not establish complete loss of all triplet material in every functional ciliary basal body. Assembly essentiality remains UNKNOWN, not a claim of universal dispensability.

Loss of the central part is not demonstrated removal of every cartwheel or spoke-tip component. These results support a role in normal organization without establishing an absolute whole-substructure formation requirement; assembly essentiality remains UNKNOWN. Full experimental text of the 2007 source was not inspected.

records.label: cryptophyte cortical centrin network
records.definition: A peripheral centrin-positive cytoskeletal network observed in cryptophyte cells by ultrastructure expansion microscopy. It forms a regular hexagonal mesh in Rhinomonas nottbeckii and shows variable network patterns among Rhodomonas isolates. The assembly is distinct from basal-body-associated centrin structures and from the periplast itself.

GO:0020038 subpellicular network requires a mechanically stable pellicle-associated structure surrounding microtubules, not established here. The cryptophyte network is not equated to ciliate infraciliary lattices, periplast plates, nuclear baskets or flagellar rootlets. OTHER kind avoids asserting a single filament or a resolved multiprotein-complex composition.

records.label: equatorial microtubule organizing center
records.definition: A microtubule organizing center formed by a band of gamma-tubulin that is recruited to a circumferential band of F-actin at the midpoint of a cell and which nucleates microtubules from the cell division site at the end of mitosis.

discussions.prompt: Distinguish the equatorial assembly from other MTOCs and its microtubule output.
discussions.rationale: Parsed identifiers, labels and synonyms from all 903 pre-existing records and hidden/ignored-inclusive name, accession and citation searches found no duplicate identity. GO:0000923 exactly names this center. GO:0005815 is its parent and GO:0032153 its division-site whole. GO:1990295 has-part this center but names the larger post-anaphase array; that class-level existential is not inverted into universal eMTOC part-of PAA. MULTIPROTEIN_COMPLEX describes the resident nucleation assembly, not a single purified stoichiometric complex.

discussions.prompt: Keep ring context, spindle-pole scaffolds and output microtubules separate from the core.
discussions.rationale: F-actin and Myp2 supply upstream contractile-ring docking context. Their recruitment dependencies do not make the entire contractile ring an eMTOC component. Sid4/Cdc11 targeting evidence in the 2010 paper concerns spindle poles, not this equatorial assembly. Alpha/beta tubulin and Ase1 occur in the nucleated array rather than establishing core eMTOC membership. Mto1/Myp2 offset and dosage results limit a simple direct-coassembly model without excluding indirect association.

discussions.prompt: Find exact source-neutral whole-protein mappings for four label-only classes.
discussions.rationale: Complete InterPro matches were inspected for Mto1 O94488, Mto2 Q9USP7, Alp7 Q9URY2 and Rsp1 O13601. Domains and superfamilies are not whole-protein family equivalents. Rsp1 has a broad family annotation, but no exact mapping to the narrower class is adopted. Mto2's empty API response is not absence of homologs; divergent fungal homologs are discussed in the 2015 primary study. Alp14 uses the verified XMAP215 family, not a TOG domain.

discussions.prompt: Separate assembly, recruitment, activity and maintenance phenotypes.
discussions.rationale: Mto2 deletion can leave faint Alp4 recruitment, very limited nucleation or an early array that fails to persist. A failure to detect equatorial gamma-tubulin in another assay is not proof of zero molecules. Alp7/Mia1 mutants retain initial equatorial markers despite maintenance defects. The accessible Rsp1 abstract reports persistent asters in loss-of-function mutants, not demonstrated assembly in the complete absence of Rsp1. Rsp1 assembly essentiality therefore remains UNKNOWN, separately from its supported turnover role. Unknown assembly essentiality remains UNKNOWN for the other classes; no cell-viability phenotype is substituted for assembly necessity. Review update 2026-10-11: direct inspection of the 2006 equatorial Results and Figure 5C-E confirms residual equatorial assembly in mia1-deletion cells. Alp7 assembly essentiality is therefore now DISPENSABLE under the tested S. pombe conditions, superseding its earlier UNKNOWN classification; sustained nucleation-site use remains defective. The other unresolved essentiality values, including Rsp1 UNKNOWN, are unchanged.

discussions.prompt: Do not transfer interphase or engineered-system mechanisms to the equator.
discussions.rationale: Alp7 and Alp14 equatorial localization is direct evidence, but bonsai construct nucleation frequencies, interphase satellite dwell times and forced GBP recruitment are not native eMTOC measurements. The 2025 Klp2/Rsp1/Ssa1 study resolves a microtubule-lattice pathway; it does not directly establish the same reaction at an equatorial center. Klp2 and Ssa1 are therefore not imported as universal eMTOC members. Mto2 phosphorylation quantification in the 2015 paper excluded eMTOC-bearing cells. No equator-specific phosphoregulation graph or native copy number is inferred.

discussions.prompt: Resolve the molecular disassembly reaction at equatorial centers.
discussions.rationale: The rsp1 loss-of-function phenotype supports turnover dependence. Satellite redistribution and chaperone-based breakup remain models in the accessible 2004 account; the 2025 lattice experiments do not by themselves close this site-specific gap.

discussions.prompt: Keep inferred ring mechanics distinct from universal cytokinesis requirements.
discussions.rationale: The 2023 selective mto1-427 perturbation changes inferred contractile-ring stiffness without a measurable cytokinesis or anchoring defect under its tested conditions. Stiffness estimation assumes unchanged initial tension; mutant recoil did not plateau, limiting fitted parameters. Earlier anchoring experiments used cytokinesis delay or actin perturbation. Those contexts are retained rather than declaring a universal requirement or an unexplained contradiction. Array counts and offsets are not universal eMTOC dimensions.

discussions.prompt: Preserve organism, source-access and measurement limits.
discussions.rationale: Only S. pombe is a canonical example. Protein accessions identify the reference strain, not every experimental stock. The 2004 Rsp1 paper and 2006 Mia1 paper were not read in full; two 2005 papers were accessible as indexed primary Results, not complete Methods. No unverified trait, exact Complex Portal equivalent, direct structural dataset, exhaustive composition or fixed copy number is supplied. The native GO definition is an identity definition, not an independent new quantitative experiment. Review update 2026-10-11: both 2005 studies were subsequently read through primary PMC HTML, including full main Results, Discussion and Methods. The 2006 paper was assessed through its equatorial Results section, main Methods, Discussion, abstract and Figure 5, not all Results or separate supplements/movies. The 2004 Rsp1 study remains abstract-only. Earlier access statements above describe the initial curation, not current access availability.

components.label: FAZ1 repetitive filament protein

evidence.notes: Vaughan et al. 2008 identified FAZ1 as a repetitive T. brucei FAZ filament protein and tested its requirement for FAZ filament structure and function. In procyclic T. brucei, FAZ1 RNAi left aberrant FAZ-like structures and other filament markers despite attachment and cytokinesis defects. Because knockdown does not establish complete protein absence, these results leave assembly essentiality UNKNOWN; they support a requirement for normal filament organization, not an absolute block of FAZ formation.

discussions.prompt: Keep the whole meiotic array distinct from its organizer, constituent filaments and neighboring structures.
discussions.rationale: Parsed checks over 907 records and whole-repository searches including ignored and hidden files found only prior read-ahead notes, not an existing HAA record. GO:0032117 is exact; GO:0005818 is its native is-a parent and GO:0030981 its native part-of target. No extra HAA part-of meiotic-spindle claim is inferred from ancestor relations. OTHER denotes a multi-filament system, not one microtubule, the nuclear-movement process, the telomere bouquet, the SPB or the rMTOC. Native GO wording that microtubules emanate from the SPB is retained, while the 2012 ultrastructure resolves their organization near but distinct from the SPB core.

discussions.prompt: Separate the array polymer inventory from the organizing-center composition.
discussions.rationale: The initial constituent inventory covers alpha/beta-tubulin polymer classes. The 2012 study localizes Hrs1 and gamma tubulin to the rMTOC and tests Hrs1-dependent organization. These proteins are not automatically asserted to be array-lattice constituents; the center remains external assembly context in the graph. Whole-SPB, nuclear-envelope and bouquet membership is not inferred from spatial proximity or recruitment dependence. This boundary does not deny a physical connection to the array minus ends. A separate source-defined rMTOC record and more detailed membership evidence can refine the representation later.

discussions.prompt: Extend array-associated machinery and isoform coverage only with direct membership and role evidence.
discussions.rationale: This is a bounded polymer inventory, not a complete HAA proteome. The Atb2 reference sequence is not the experimental strain. Beta-tubulin class composition does not justify an Nda3 example without an inspected isoform-specific experiment. Dynein-dynactin participates in movement, but its detailed array-resident composition and assembly essentiality need separate primary-source review before adding machinery rows. Unpublished observations about dynein-assisted radial rearrangement and suggested Hrs1/NudE similarity in the 2012 Discussion are not treated as verified family or component assignments.

discussions.prompt: Resolve the physical minus-end attachment and nucleation mechanisms within the organizing region.
discussions.rationale: Ultrastructure, immunolocalization and Hrs1 perturbations establish radial organization but not a purified molecular bridge or sufficiency of an isolated nucleation complex. Yeast-two-hybrid interactions with Kms1 and Alp4 do not establish complete native binding geometry. Gamma-tubulin enrichment is not a census of a fixed ring stoichiometry. Distances and microtubule counts in selected tomograms are assay-specific and are not imported as universal HAA dimensions.

discussions.prompt: Keep Hrs1 downregulation and meiotic transition phenotypes source-bounded.
discussions.rationale: Hrs1 degradation and phosphorylation jointly downregulate the radial organizing system near meiosis I. Stabilized nonphosphorylatable Hrs1 can delay bipolar spindle formation; this is not a universal complete block, and outcomes depend on temperature and the spindle checkpoint. Phosphomimetic effects do not prove that every identified phosphorylation has the same native role. Ectopic Hrs1 produces HAA-like arrays in vegetative cells but does not turn every such cell into a native meiotic HAA exemplar. The later spindle is not the HAA, and disappearance of array signal is not direct proof that every tubulin subunit is degraded.

discussions.prompt: Preserve experimental, access and imaging limits.
discussions.rationale: Only S. pombe is an organism exemplar; no clade prevalence, fixed whole-array copy number, trait or pathway relation is inferred. Homothallic live-cell imaging and synchronized engineered pat1 mat-Pc diploid EM experiments are distinct. Main Figure 2 text/captions specify 80 minutes for immuno-EM, whereas supplemental methods and the deletion-control caption specify 120 minutes; no single universal sampling time is assigned. Tomography used high-pressure freezing followed by freeze substitution and resin sections, not vitreous cryo-ET. The 2005 source is abstract-only; the 2012 main text, strain table and supplemental methods were read, but movies, raw data and most supplemental image panels remain uninspected. Figure 4 is unchanged CC BY 3.0 material and mixes live-cell images with biochemical and schematic panels; no dimension is inferred from its unquantified scale bars.

records.label: interphase SIN signaling complex
records.definition: A SIN signaling complex associated with the old spindle pole body during interphase in an inhibitory configuration. In Schizosaccharomyces pombe, the Byr4-Cdc16 GAP inhibits the Spg1 GTPase. Dma1-dependent ubiquitination of the Sid4 scaffold antagonizes Plo1 recruitment in G2 and during a mitotic checkpoint arrest.

records.label: meiotic actomyosin contractile ring
records.definition: A cytoskeletal structure composed of actin filaments, myosin, and myosin-associated proteins that forms beneath the plasma membrane of many cells, including animal cells and yeast cells, in a plane perpendicular to the axis of the meiotic spindle, i.e. the cell division plane. Ring contraction is associated with centripetal growth of the membrane that divides the cytoplasm of the two future daughter cells. In animal cells, the meiotic contractile ring is located inside the plasma membrane at the location of the cleavage furrow. In fungal cells, the meiotic contractile ring forms beneath the plasma membrane of the prospore envelope in preparation for completing cytokinesis.

records.label: mitotic actomyosin contractile ring
records.definition: A cytoskeletal structure composed of actin filaments, myosin, and myosin-associated proteins that forms beneath the plasma membrane of many cells, including animal cells and yeast cells, in a plane perpendicular to the axis of the mitotic spindle, i.e. the cell division plane. Ring contraction is associated with centripetal growth of the membrane that divides the cytoplasm of the two future daughter cells. In animal cells, the mitotic contractile ring is located inside the plasma membrane at the location of the cleavage furrow. In Saccharomyces cerevisiae, Myo1 localizes to a ring at the future bud site before bud emergence; actin joins this ring at the mother-bud neck near the end of anaphase to form the cytokinetic actomyosin ring.

discussions.prompt: This is the corpus's first minted identifier — is the scheme right?
discussions.rationale: GO has no cellular-component term for MreB or for a bacterial actin cytoskeleton, so docs/CURATION.md requires minting with the nearest broader term as a parent. The local part is a lowercase slug of the label rather than a counter, because a slug needs no allocator and reads in a URL; the cost is that it looks stale if the preferred label ever changes, which is acceptable since identifiers are never renamed.

discussions.prompt: The filament guides the elongasome, and the schema has no relation that says so.

It was briefly recorded as xrefs: [cellstructuremech:elongasome], but the schema defines xrefs as true equivalence and the two are not equivalent, so the claim was false as written and removed (#119). Until a relation exists, the link lives in the RodZ component role and in this discussion.

discussions.prompt: Bound archaeal homology separately from occurrence of this MreB filament system.

Homology alone does not establish the occurrence or prevalence of the bacterial filament system defined in this record. Archaeal actin-like Ta0583 polymerization is a distinct experimental observation, not proof of this MreB-elongasome system.

evidence.snippet: MreB depletion results in loss of rod-like shape and rounding (Kruse et al., 2005), and there are no E. coli mutants or growth conditions known to restore rod-like shape in the absence of MreB.
evidence.notes: Verbatim from the open-access full text (PMC5846203). Supports REQUIRED_FOR rather than CONFERS: the shape is lost without MreB, and nothing restores it, but MreB alone does not produce a rod.

evidence.snippet: Many rod-like and curved bacterial species require MreB to elongate, although there are exceptions such as the Actinobacteria and Rhizobiales that lack MreB altogether.
evidence.notes: The same source bounds the claim: rod shape can be achieved without MreB in some lineages, so the requirement is not universal across bacteria.

evidence.snippet: MreB both senses and changes cell shape, thereby generating a self-organizing feedback system for shape maintenance.
evidence.notes: Verbatim from the open-access full text (PMC5846203). MODULATES rather than CONFERS: the filament is described as sensing and adjusting shape, not dictating it.
