discussions.prompt: Keep the whole array distinct from its organizing center and other microtubule networks.
discussions.rationale: Parsed checks over 906 existing records and hidden/ignored-inclusive name, accession and citation searches found no whole-array duplicate. GO:1990295 exactly denotes the array, with parent GO:0110165, part-of GO:0015630 and has-part GO:0000923. The has-part existential is not inverted into universal center part-of array. OTHER describes the multi-filament system, not a single filament or fixed stoichiometric complex. ePAA and lPAA are equatorial and longitudinal portions, not early/late arrays or exact whole-array synonyms. Spindle, interphase arrays, individual microtubules and microtubule ends remain distinct.

discussions.prompt: Distinguish array constituents, the nucleating subassembly and external ring context.
discussions.rationale: Alpha/beta tubulin and resident Ase1 belong to the array. Its organizing center is included at subassembly level, without duplicating every center protein. Myp2 and F-actin are upstream ring context; recruitment dependence alone does not make the whole ring a PAA constituent. Mto1/Myp2 spatial offsets and dosage responses constrain simple direct coassembly without excluding indirect association. Unknown tubulin or center assembly essentiality is not replaced by a cell-viability phenotype. Ase1 deletion leaves an altered array, so this constituent is DISPENSABLE for assembly.

discussions.prompt: Extend PAA-specific composition only after checking localization and assembly evidence.
discussions.rationale: This is not an exhaustive protein inventory. Mal3 is used as a plus-tip reporter in supplementary Figure S2, which has not been directly inspected; no Mal3 class is added from that lead alone. A beta-tubulin family assignment is not an isoform-specific localization assay, so no Nda3 protein example is supplied. InterPro families define classes, not universal PAA residence of every family member. Direct PAA-specific evidence is needed before adding other motors or microtubule-associated proteins.

discussions.prompt: Resolve the physical PAA-nuclear-envelope interface and transmitted forces.
discussions.rationale: Contact imaging, envelope deformation and selective perturbations support a mechanical basket interpretation, but do not identify a purified interface or calibrated forces. Protection from septal cutting, DNA-damage avoidance and precise inheritance benefits remain hypotheses; no nuclei were cut by the ring after PAA loss under the reported conditions. Later newborn-cell simulations model interphase microtubules and growth, not PAA. MBC affects multiple networks and can leave residual PAA signal.

discussions.prompt: Keep inferred effective stiffness separate from direct measurements and universal cytokinesis requirements.
discussions.rationale: Ablations used rings approximately 20-50 percent constricted, single-plane imaging and recoil fits. Interpreting increased recoil as reduced effective stiffness assumes unchanged initial tension. Mutant recoil often failed to plateau or moved out of plane; fitted amplitudes and timescales are lower bounds. Selective mto1-427 PAA impairment did not measurably alter anchoring, constriction or cytokinetic timing under the tested conditions. Complete mto1 deletion affects additional networks and cannot establish a PAA-only healing or timing defect. These experiments do not exclude stress-specific roles.

discussions.prompt: Preserve taxon, source-access and quantitative limits.
discussions.rationale: Only S. pombe is a canonical example; reference-sequence taxon 284812 does not identify every experimental stock. Main Results, Discussion and Methods of the two 2023 papers and Results/Discussion of the 2010 targeting paper were read. Separate strain supplements, actual movies, raw data and inline equation graphics remain uninspected. No clade-wide prevalence, fixed whole-array copy number, universal dimension, exact Complex Portal composition, trait link or pathway relation is inferred. The hosted figure is the unchanged CC BY 4.0 original; restricted-license imagery from the nuclear-position study is not hosted.

records.label: quiescent cell microtubule bundle
records.definition: A stable antiparallel cytoplasmic microtubule bundle assembled during nutrient-exhaustion-induced quiescence in fission yeast, characterized in Schizosaccharomyces pombe. It contains closely packed microtubules, is usually associated with the spindle pole body, and is distinct from the nuclear microtubule array of quiescent budding yeast.

discussions.prompt: Separate efficient polarity recovery from longevity or immediate tubulin-store release.

records.label: quiescent nuclear microtubule bundle
records.definition: A stable monopolar bundle of parallel nuclear microtubules formed during glucose-exhaustion-induced quiescence, characterized in Saccharomyces cerevisiae. The bundle extends from the nuclear face of the spindle pole body and reorganizes kinetochore and centromere distribution; it is distinct from the antiparallel cytoplasmic quiescent-cell bundle of fission yeast.

functions.label: Quiescent nuclear reorganization
functions.description: The nuclear array supports relocation of kinetochore-centromere clusters away from the SPB and displacement of the nucleolus.

evidence.notes: Kinetochore and centromere localization, plus no-array mutants, associate array formation with nuclear reorganization; chromosomes and nucleolus are not treated as bundle constituents.

functions.label: Support of quiescent survival and recovery
functions.description: Bundle formation contributes to survival and subsequent colony formation in the tested glucose-exhaustion conditions.

evidence.notes: Array-defective mutants lose viability and regrowth capacity; pleiotropic effects limit a uniquely bundle-specific causal claim.

Early nocodazole prevents formation and impairs survival/regrowth, whereas late treatment of stabilized bundles does not have the same effect. This narrows but does not eliminate off-target explanations.

edges.subject: glucose_exhaustion
edges.description: Carbon exhaustion triggers the transition from dynamic nuclear microtubules to a persistent bundle.

evidence.notes: Figure 1 and Results identify sequential establishment, growth and stabilization phases; exact timing depends on culture conditions.

edges.subject: kinetochore_attachment
edges.description: Functional attachment is required early for normal bundle formation, but late Ndc80 inactivation does not dismantle an established bundle.

evidence.notes: Figure 3 and supplement 1 compare early and late ndc80-1 restrictive-temperature treatments.

causal_graphs.title: Regulated disassembly on quiescence exit
causal_graphs.scope_notes: Exit from glucose-exhaustion-induced quiescence; timing and deletion evidence do not identify a molecular checkpoint. Kip3 and She1 are external regulators, not inferred stable residents.

edges.subject: refeeding
edges.description: Refeeding triggers progressive shortening of the nuclear array; translation inhibition delays efficient disassembly.

evidence.notes: Quiescence-exit experiments compare glucose alone and cycloheximide treatment.

edges.subject: kip3
edges.description: Kip3 supports timely onset of disassembly, without a detected change in the subsequent shortening rate in its deletion.

evidence.notes: Figure 5 distinguishes delayed onset from post-onset depolymerization kinetics; Kip3 is resynthesized on exit.

edges.subject: she1
edges.description: She1 contributes to efficient disassembly in the tested KIP3-deficient background.

evidence.notes: Figure 5 compares kip3 and kip3 she1 deletions. The native spindle-associated She1 accession is P38200, not MYO4's historical SHE1 alias P32492.

edges.subject: disassembly
edges.description: Completion of bundle loss precedes SPB separation; delayed disassembly is associated with delayed separation.

evidence.notes: Figure 5 tracks bundle disappearance and SPB separation in wild type and mutants. The combined deletion also delays separation without delaying overall proliferation; this is not proof of a specific molecular checkpoint.

discussions.prompt: Keep the nuclear Q-nMT identity separate from generic nuclear microtubules and cytoplasmic Q-MT.
discussions.notes: Hidden- and ignored-inclusive identity, synonym and citation searches, plus a parsed identity scan, found no existing record. OAK GO alias searches and native GO definitions do not supply an exact Q-nMT term. GO:0099070 is broader; GO:0005880 is a constituent filament. The parallel monopolar nuclear array is not the antiparallel cytoplasmic S. pombe bundle or a bipolar mitotic spindle. OTHER denotes the whole array. Bare nuclear microtubule array is not adopted as an exact synonym.

discussions.prompt: Separate bundle composition from its nucleation site and attached chromosomal assemblies.
discussions.notes: The SPB nucleates the array but is not its containing structure. Tub4/Spc97/Spc72 mark the nucleation site. All six kinetochore subcomplexes have array-associated localization in 2013; Dad2 and Nuf2 mark attachments in 2024. These are retained as interacting chromosome-bound machinery rather than asserted stoichiometric building blocks of the microtubule bundle. Centromeric Cse4/chromosomes and the displaced nucleolus are likewise not bundle components. Slk19 is included because its own direct bundle-end localization and perturbation are documented.

discussions.prompt: Do not turn genetic requirements or expression into residence.
discussions.notes: Dynein and dynactin are detected on the cytoplasmic SPB face in 2013, not inside the nuclear array. Cik1 requirement, monopolin Mam1/Lrs4/Hrr25/Csm1 expression and deletion phenotypes, Spo13 effects, and tubulin-folding factors do not alone establish Q-nMT residence. Ipl1 activity is required early, but Ipl1 and Nbl1 were not detected in quiescence; the whole CPC is not imported from Bir1/Sli15 localization. Kip3 and She1 exit phenotypes are modeled as regulatory evidence, not stable-component evidence. She1 P38200 is distinct from the MYO4/SHE1 homonym P32492.

discussions.prompt: Keep assay sensitivity and individual deletion effects explicit.
discussions.notes: Kar3 was not detected in 2013 but later detected with 3GFP in 2024. Cin8 localization is faint and channel controls are shown in Figure 4 supplement 1B. Cin8 and Kip1 share a family but have distinct phenotypes; family-wide necessity is not tested. Short residual bundles after several deletions preclude an unqualified assembly-essential claim.

discussions.prompt: Resolve stabilization without upgrading models into measured mechanisms.
discussions.notes: Nocodazole resistance, low tubulin turnover and stability after laser severing bound stability to these assays. Survival/regrowth effects are supported but perturbations also act beyond this array. Proposed tubulin storage, a molecular SPB-separation checkpoint and homology with primary cilia are not asserted as demonstrated functions.

records.label: radial microtubule organizing center
records.definition: A transient, Hrs1/Mcp6-dependent, gamma-tubulin-enriched amorphous microtubule-organizing assembly at the cytoplasmic side of the spindle pole body during Schizosaccharomyces pombe meiotic prophase, distinct from the spindle pole body core, that organizes the radial microtubule array used in horsetail nuclear movement.

components.label: Hrs1/Mcp6-like meiotic organizing protein
components.grounding_notes: Native InterPro combined matches for reviewed Hrs1/Mcp6 Q10336 returned HTTP204 on 2026-10-08. UniProt supplies no exact integrated InterPro family; its SUPFAM Tropomyosin match is not an exact Hrs1 grounding. The primary paper treats NudE similarity as a hypothesis. This narrow source-neutral class does not assert membership of all coiled-coil, NudE or tropomyosin proteins.
components.role: Localized constituent required for the recognizable meiotic rMTOC in S. pombe. A structural-scaffold role is supported as a model; a purified molecular bridge and its stoichiometry are not resolved.

protein_examples.role: Reference-sequence exemplar for the species-level localization experiment; the reference stock is not asserted to be the engineered experimental strain (also declared as synonym hrs1, mug3).

evidence.notes: Figures 1-2 and the deletion control show Hrs1 enrichment in the organizing region and loss of that region without Hrs1. Experiments use synchronized pat1 mat-Pc diploids, not an asserted 972h- experimental stock.
Native reviewed accession, recommended protein name, gene and reference taxon verified on 2026-10-08. Experimental membership is established by the primary study, not by sequence annotation alone.

Immunogold labeling places Hrs1 in the faintly electron-dense, ribosome-excluding region outside the SPB core. hrs1 deletion removes this recognizable region and normal radial geometry while retaining some nonradial SPB-associated microtubules. Essentiality concerns rMTOC formation, not cell viability or all microtubule polymerization.

components.label: Gamma tubulin
components.role: Gamma-tubulin class enriched in the radial organizing region; local enrichment does not specify a complete ring complex or demonstrate sufficiency for rMTOC assembly.

protein_examples.role: Reference-sequence exemplar for the species-level localization experiment; the reference stock is not asserted to be the engineered experimental strain (also declared as synonym tug1).

evidence.notes: Figure 3 detects S. pombe gamma tubulin in the rMTOC with GTU88 immunogold labeling; the signal becomes more dispersed around the SPB in hrs1 deletion. Native InterPro matches for the reference protein include Gamma tubulin IPR002454 as a family, not merely a domain.
Native reviewed accession, recommended protein name, gene and reference taxon verified on 2026-10-08. Experimental membership is established by the primary study, not by sequence annotation alone.

Results section 2.3 and Figure 3 establish gamma-tubulin enrichment in the rMTOC. This study does not separately test whether gamma-tubulin removal abolishes the amorphous scaffold, so assembly essentiality is left UNKNOWN.

canonical_examples.note: Meiotic-prophase ultrastructure in synchronized h-/h- pat1.114/pat1.114 mat-Pc diploids: KT2486 with wild-type hrs1 and KT2919 with hrs1 deletion (supplemental Table S1). Homothallic live-cell transition experiments are separate. No clade prevalence or experimental identity with the UniProt reference stock is inferred.

functions.label: horsetail-astral microtubule organization
functions.description: Organizes the radial microtubule array during S. pombe meiotic prophase by concentrating organizing material near the SPB and spatially arranging predominantly capped microtubule ends.

evidence.notes: Tomography, immunolocalization and hrs1 deletion connect the rMTOC to radial geometry. They do not establish purified nucleation sufficiency or a fixed number of microtubules per center.
Native GO label and definition verified on 2026-10-08; the term denotes the biological process, not the center identity.

edges.subject: hrs1
edges.description: Hrs1 is required for the recognizable amorphous radial center.

evidence.notes: Figures 1-2 and deletion controls show loss of the organizing region and radial arrangement in hrs1-deleted cells; residual nonradial microtubules do not contradict this assembly dependence.

edges.subject: hrs1
edges.description: Hrs1 supports concentration of gamma tubulin in the rMTOC region.

evidence.notes: Figure 3 compares enriched wild-type labeling with more dispersed gamma-tubulin labeling around the SPB after hrs1 deletion. The experiment does not establish direct Hrs1-gamma-tubulin binding.

edges.subject: gamma
edges.description: Gamma tubulin is an enriched constituent of the radial center.

evidence.notes: Figure 3 serial-section immunogold localization supports membership; this edge records localization, not a gamma-tubulin assembly-dependency or sufficiency experiment.

edges.subject: rmtoc
edges.description: The radial center arranges microtubule minus ends outside the SPB core.

evidence.notes: Figure 1 tomography places predominantly capped ends in the organizing region, with varied orientations; hrs1 deletion removes normal radial geometry. Not every end was resolved as capped.

edges.subject: ends
edges.description: Spatial minus-end organization establishes the radial array geometry.

evidence.notes: The wild-type and hrs1-deletion tomograms distinguish radial from residual nonradial SPB-associated microtubules. This is not a complete account of how pre-existing interphase polymers rearrange.

edges.subject: haa
edges.description: The radial array provides the microtubule system used in horsetail movement.

evidence.notes: Main Introduction and Results describe radial-array function and live-cell behavior; the array acts with dynein-dynactin and is not itself the motor or proof of recombination outcomes.
Exact GO array definition includes facilitation of horsetail nuclear movement.

discussions.prompt: Keep the radial center distinct from the SPB and output array.
discussions.rationale: Whole-repository searches included hidden/ignored files and parsed identities across 908 records. Earlier HAA/PAA context is not a separate rMTOC record. Native GO label/alias searches with positive HAA/MTOC controls found no exact rMTOC identity, so a local identifier is minted with GO:0005815 as an is-a parent. The source resolves an amorphous assembly near but distinct from the SPB core. GO:0035974 denotes the whole meiotic SPB and GO:0032117 the output array, neither an equivalent. MULTIPROTEIN_COMPLEX denotes an assembly, not a claim of fixed stoichiometry or membrane enclosure. No SPB, nuclear-envelope or HAA parthood is asserted solely from proximity.

discussions.prompt: Do not turn neighboring proteins and interaction leads into a complete inventory.
discussions.rationale: The initial inventory covers directly localized Hrs1 and gamma-tubulin classes. Kms1/Kms2 are membrane/SPB interaction context; Alp4 and Mto1 interactions are leads for broader nucleation machinery. Neither yeast-two-hybrid interaction nor an older whole-SPB annotation establishes every partner as a localized constituent of the 2012-defined amorphous region. These proteins are not imported here as a complete ring, and their omission is a bounded curation decision, not a claim of absence. Alpha/beta polymers are the associated output array, not automatically the center matrix.

discussions.prompt: Resolve the native molecular bridge, complete composition and nucleation mechanism.
discussions.rationale: Hrs1 localization and deletion establish membership and assembly dependence, but the detailed scaffold/bridge geometry is proposed. Gamma-tubulin enrichment does not establish a purified nucleation reaction, fixed ring stoichiometry or the necessity of gamma tubulin for forming the amorphous matrix. Dynein-assisted rearrangement includes unpublished observations, and the paper explicitly leaves conversion from interphase arrays unresolved. No distances or counts from selected tomograms are promoted to universal center dimensions.

evidence.notes: Primary source and its stated limitations.

discussions.prompt: Retain the experimental limits of rMTOC downregulation.
discussions.rationale: Hrs1 degradation and phosphorylation jointly downregulate the organizing system near meiosis I. Stabilized nonphosphorylatable Hrs1 delays bipolar spindle formation under specified temperature/checkpoint conditions; it does not universally block separation. Individual phosphosite functions and the responsible kinases/E3 enzymes remain unresolved. Proposed holding of duplicated SPBs is not a purified mechanical measurement. Vegetative overexpression aggregates and HAA-like output are not automatically normal meiotic rMTOCs, and phosphorylation is not proof of destruction of every constituent.

discussions.prompt: Keep specimen, imaging and source-access scope explicit.
discussions.rationale: Only S. pombe is a canonical organism exemplar, with no inferred clade frequency. Reference proteins from taxon284812 are not asserted to be the engineered KT2486/KT2919 experimental stocks. EM used high-pressure freezing, freeze substitution and resin sections, not vitreous cryo-ET. Main immuno-EM text/captions specify 80 minutes whereas supplemental immunolabeling methods specify 120 minutes; no single universal sampling time is assigned. Figure 3 includes TEM sections and interpretive 3D models, and contrasts wild-type hrs1 with deletion. The original image is unchanged CC BY 3.0 material; 100 nm bars are image provenance, not a curated whole-center dimension. Main text, captions and supplemental pages13-22 were read, but movies, raw data and most supplemental panels were not inspected.

images.caption: Gamma-tubulin localization at the S. pombe radial organizing center. A shows immunogold-labeled TEM serial sections of synchronized meiotic cells with wild-type hrs1; B-C model those labels and the ribosome-excluding amorphous region. D shows hrs1-deletion sections and E their model, with more dispersed gamma-tubulin labels and nonradial microtubules. In the models, yellow marks gamma-tubulin labels, green microtubules and blue the SPB; C highlights the amorphous region. Bars are 100 nm. Model surfaces are interpretations, not additional micrographs.

discussions.prompt: Do not infer architecture or absolute necessity from reporter localization.
discussions.notes: Alp4 is one gamma-TuC reporter, not a whole-complex accession. No ring geometry, small-complex copy number, exhaustive subunit list or fixed telocentrosome stoichiometry is established here. Kms1 and Mto1 support normal recruitment, but reduced or residual signals are not encoded as complete absence. Dlc1 has a stage-dependent contribution independent of Dhc1; Dhc1 is dispensable for Alp4 recruitment but important for clustering. Resident motors remain constituents without being assigned universal assembly necessity.

discussions.prompt: Separate the nucleation-center core from upstream chromosome tethers and external motor systems.
discussions.notes: Bqt1/Bqt2, Rap1 and Taz1 supply the chromosome-to-envelope context or markers and are not separately imported into this core nucleation-center composition; this does not assert their absence from the telomere environment. Kinesins Cut7, Tea2, Klp5/Klp6 and Pkl1/Klp2 affect clustering but lack obvious telocentrosomal localization in the defining study, so genetic effects alone do not make them resident components. Sid4 is explicitly absent from telocentrosomal foci. Mto2, all dynactin subunits, all gamma-TuC subunits and alpha/beta tubulin are not imported merely from related-complex membership or from nucleated microtubules.

discussions.prompt: Resolve the physical motor arrangement without promoting a proposed model to fact.
discussions.notes: Minus-end-directed telomere movement and contributions from multiple motors are observed. Oligomerized dynein/kinesin-14 cross-linking of telocentrosomal and SPB microtubules, direct motor-specific telomere transport, and the exact maintenance action of Dlc1 remain proposed mechanisms in Figure 5C. The graphs encode recruitment dependencies and supported outputs only.

discussions.prompt: Keep partial ectopic assembly separate from physiological meiotic telocentrosomes.
discussions.notes: The 2025 study ectopically expresses Bqt1/Bqt2 in Rabl-deficient haploid mitotic cells. Sad1, Kms1, Mto1 and Alp4 recruit to telomeres, but Dhc1 is not detected and the complete bouquet does not form. Kms1 loss suppresses telomere migration and some growth defects in that engineered context. These observations do not demonstrate a normal mitotic organelle, prove dynein is the only missing factor, or contradict the 2013 physiological meiotic scope.

discussions.prompt: Distinguish the named spool assembly from tubulin proteins and broader cytoskeletal structures.
discussions.rationale: A shape-bearing subcellular structure requires its own identity without promoting a broader ontology class or a hypothetical homology to equivalence.
discussions.notes: Hidden- and ignored-inclusive repository searches for labels, aliases, DOI, PMID and preprint DOI found no existing spool record. QuickGO spool search returned zero terms. Generic tubulin and microtubule hits do not denote this assembly. GO:0005622 is the broad parent; microtubule cytoskeleton is a part_of relation. OTHER kind avoids claiming a resolved single-filament lattice or bundle topology. Tubulin ring is not an exact synonym for all ring-shaped tubulin structures. The membrane nuclear net, cortical array, flagellar apparatus and apical centrin ring are not asserted to be this entity. No desmose equivalence or parthood is asserted.

evidence.notes: Figure 2D-E names the tubulin or microtubule spools; desmose association is speculative.

discussions.prompt: Resolve the spool's filament topology, tubulin subtype composition and assembly mechanism.
discussions.rationale: Immunolocalization and an apparent connection cannot establish the complete lattice, gene inventory or assembly dependencies.
discussions.notes: The authors describe an apparent extension from a single microtubule. This is not treated as a counted one-microtubule stoichiometry, closed ring topology, standard protofilament number or direct reconstruction of a complete molecular lattice. Tubulin-family grounding is not a claim that every family member is present. No gene-specific accession, subunit count or causal assembly graph is asserted.

evidence.notes: Microtubule-array Results and Figure 2D-E establish morphology and tubulin labeling.

discussions.prompt: Keep neighboring cortical centrin, DNA and flagellar modification signals separate from spool composition.
discussions.rationale: A multi-channel or multi-panel view does not make every labeled material a constituent of the highlighted structure.
discussions.notes: DNA supplies nuclear context, not a demonstrated spool constituent. Cortical centrin is described separately and is not assigned to the spool merely because it appears in the same cells or video. Figure 2F-G examines flagellar and cortical tubulin modifications; it does not establish a spool-specific modification inventory. The structure is not assigned centrin, DNA, flagellar proteins or modifying enzymes on that basis. This is an evidence boundary, not a claim of biological absence.

evidence.notes: The microtubule and centrin Results and Figure 2 separate these structures and signals.

discussions.prompt: Establish physiological function, cell-cycle dynamics and taxonomic prevalence with targeted tests.
discussions.rationale: A fixed-cell survey and a hypothesis about neighboring structures do not demonstrate force transmission, swimming performance or division requirements.
discussions.notes: The survey reports spools among sampled Kareniaceae, including Karenia, Karlodinium and Takayama. This is not universal family prevalence or an absence claim for unsampled or insufficiently labeled taxa. Mechanical reinforcement, high-shear swimming, nuclear-envelope dynamics and desmose-mediated basal-body linkage remain hypotheses. No asserted function, associated trait, essentiality, universal two-spool count or causal graph is inferred from them.

evidence.notes: Dinoflagellate survey and Discussion explicitly propose future time-course experiments to clarify spool formation and function.

discussions.prompt: Reconcile expansion-factor handling before asserting native-cell dimensions from the figure.
discussions.rationale: Conflicting scale statements must not be silently converted into a precise biological measurement.
discussions.notes: Figure 2's legend describes 5 micrometre scale bars adjusted for expansion, whereas Image analysis Methods says scale bars are not adjusted. Figure 2E reports perinuclear and posterior diameter summaries for measured spools, not universal dimensions. No physical_properties or scale-derived measurements are asserted. The hosted publisher Figure 2 is unmodified; D-E are the spool panels, while other panels contain other structures or taxa. It is fixed-cell expansion fluorescence, not live imaging, electron microscopy or a direct native-size image.

evidence.notes: Figure 2 legend and STAR Methods, Image analysis, were read together; the scale-bar discrepancy remains unresolved.

RCC3511 is separately listed as Biecheleriopsis adriatica in the key resources. The combined filename therefore does not establish strain equivalence or spool occurrence in Biecheleriopsis. records.label: photosystem I
records.definition: A photosystem that contains an iron-sulfur reaction center associated with accessory pigments and electron carriers. In cyanobacteria and chloroplasts, photosystem I functions as a light-dependent plastocyanin-ferredoxin oxidoreductase, transferring electrons from plastocyanin to ferredoxin; in photosynthetic bacteria that have only a single type I photosystem, such as the green sulfur bacteria, electrons can go either to ferredoxin (Fd) -> NAD+ or to menaquinone (MK) -> Cytb/FeS -> Cytc555 -> photosystem I (cyclic photophosphorylation).

records.label: proton-transporting ATP synthase complex
records.definition: The rotary motor enzyme that makes ATP from ADP and phosphate using the ion motive force across the membrane. It has two coupled sectors: a membrane-embedded Fo, whose c-ring turns as protons cross it, and a soluble F1 (alpha3beta3gammadeltaepsilon), whose catalytic beta subunits are driven through their conformational cycle by the rotating gamma subunit.

components.label: F1 catalytic head (alpha3beta3)
components.stoichiometry: three alpha and three beta subunits, alternating
components.role: Carries the three catalytic sites; ATP is made as each beta subunit passes through its conformational cycle.

evidence.notes: Kuehlbrandt 2019 describes the alpha3beta3 head and its three catalytic sites.
Walker 2013 reviews the same sector composition, and the variable c-ring stoichiometry across species.

records.label: coccosphere
records.definition: An external cell covering of a coccolithophore assembled from individual mineralized scales called coccoliths. Its organization varies among taxa and cell states; the covering is distinct from a single coccolith and from the intracellular vesicle in which a coccolith forms.

functions.description: In tested Coccolithus braarudii cultures, an intact coccosphere supports separation of daughter cells. Disruption of the covering during Ge or HEDP treatment is associated with persistent cell pairs after completed cytokinesis; this is not asserted for every coccolithophore or calcification perturbation.

evidence.notes: Results and Figures 7-9 combine treatment time courses, time-lapse imaging, nuclear and membrane staining, and in situ decalcification controls. Low-Ca growth inhibition does not produce the same paired-cell phenotype. Possible additional treatment effects and the precise adhesion mechanism remain unresolved.

Xu, Hutchins and Gao (2018), PeerJ. Primary Methods, SEM architecture Results, Figure 2, count/geometry assumptions and assembly discussion read. Separates observed scale arrangement from simulated topology and hypothetical cellular control.

Walker et al. (2018), New Phytologist. Culture and perturbation Methods, time-lapse/fluorescence/SEM Methods, division and organic-layer Results, Figures 5-9 and Discussion read. Supports species- and treatment-scoped covering organization and daughter-separation observations.

Johns et al. (2023), Science Advances. Primary Results and culture/isolation/adsorption Methods read. Cells can acquire free coccoliths, and xenospheres can mix morphotypes or scales from different species; possession of an attached scale does not prove that its host produced it.
Verified external encapsulating structure is a broader cellular-component class for structures outside the plasma membrane surrounding the cell, not an exact coccosphere identity.

discussions.prompt: Keep the whole coccosphere distinct from an individual coccolith, its formation vesicle and the organic matrix alone.
discussions.rationale: A covering assembled from mineral scales, a scale and a membrane-bounded formation compartment have different physical boundaries.
discussions.notes: Whole-repository hidden/ignored-inclusive name, alias, parent and primary-reference searches found no duplicate covering record. QuickGO coccosphere and xenosphere searches returned zero; coccolithophore shell returned process and unrelated structure terms. GO:0030312 is broader, so the local identifier is minted. The coccosphere has_part cellstructuremech:coccolith; it is not a subclass of the scale or of the coccolith vesicle. ENVELOPE_LAYER denotes a non-membrane covering, not a claim of exactly one geometric layer. The entire mineral-scale covering is not equated with glycocalyx or with its organic matrix, and no unconditional vesicle parthood is asserted.

evidence.notes: SEM and geometric analysis distinguish individual plates from their complete arrangement.
Results distinguish the extracellular covering, intracellular coccolith formation and the organic layer exposed after decalcification.

discussions.prompt: Resolve the chemistry, distribution and assembly requirement of the coccosphere-associated organic matrix.
discussions.rationale: A patterned lectin-positive layer does not identify an exact polymer, protein or receptor, nor prove a universal composition.
discussions.notes: The matrix remains REVIEWED_LABEL_ONLY. Retention after decalcification helps distinguish it from the mineral plates but does not establish that either matrix or mineral is dispensable for normal assembly. No specific adhesive protein, exact polymer composition, fixed stoichiometry or universal essentiality is assigned.

evidence.notes: Figure 9 and the fluorescence Methods characterize extracellular lectin staining, not the exact matrix chemistry.

discussions.prompt: Resolve how layer definitions, coccolith geometry and cell state affect coccosphere architecture across taxa.
discussions.rationale: A topology model fitted to one strain does not determine universal plate counts, layer counts or cellular sensing machinery.
discussions.notes: The PeerJ study defines a layer operationally as fully interlocking plates covering the surface and estimates total plate numbers from visible plates. Other sources discuss extra plates or multiple layers using different conventions. No universal one-layer statement, minimum plate number, four-to-six-neighbor rule, whole-sphere diameter or geometry-sensing protein is asserted. Xenosphere and holococcosphere are narrower configurations, not exact synonyms for every coccosphere; model-based assembly explanations remain hypotheses.

evidence.notes: Methods explicitly state the counting assumption and layer definition; Conclusions leave actual sensing and regulation unresolved.
Discussion contrasts coccosphere organization among species and life-cycle states.

discussions.prompt: Distinguish species-specific daughter-separation effects from universal growth, protection or photosynthesis functions.
discussions.rationale: Different calcification perturbations and different species need not have the same cellular consequences.
discussions.notes: C. braarudii cells with disrupted coverings can complete an initial cytokinesis before remaining paired and failing subsequent divisions. Low-Ca treatment does not produce the same paired-cell phenotype; potential additional effects of Ge or HEDP are acknowledged. The source does not show that calcification directly supports photosynthesis under the tested conditions. No broad prevalence row, generalized cell-cycle block, universal antiviral or grazing protection, causal graph or unverified trait link is added.

evidence.notes: Division Results and Discussion retain species/treatment distinctions and do not equate impaired growth with failure of initial cytokinesis.

discussions.prompt: Do not infer that every coccolith in a covering was produced by the covered cell.
discussions.rationale: A structural part can be acquired from the surrounding medium rather than synthesized by its present host.
discussions.notes: Experiments distinguish calcified CCMP374 donor cells from naked recipients that adsorb isolated coccoliths, and natural xenospheres can contain mixed scales. The has_part link is structural, not a same-cell biosynthesis assertion. This evidence does not make every adsorbed coccolith a fully reconstructed coccosphere or justify a universal benefit of adsorption.

evidence.notes: Figures 1-3 and culture/adsorption Methods distinguish mixed-scale coverings, donor and recipient cells, and organic-material-dependent adsorption.

discussions.prompt: Do not import the intracellular division microtubule network as a constituent of the extracellular covering.
discussions.rationale: Concurrent cellular rearrangements do not establish shared structural membership.
discussions.notes: The source images an intracellular microtubule bundle during division separately from the extracellular coccosphere and organic layer. Tubulin is therefore not added as a coccosphere component. This boundary decision does not claim that the cytoskeleton has no role in division, trafficking or covering reorganization, or resolve the open matrix-chemistry question.

evidence.notes: Figure 6 and immunofluorescence Results localize the microtubule network within dividing cells; Figure 9 characterizes the extracellular organic layer.

records.definition: A cell septum which forms as part of the division site and functions in the compartmentalization of a cell into two daughter cells at division. A division septum spans a cell and does not allow exchange of organelles or cytoplasm between compartments.

records.label: dolipore septum
records.definition: A porous fungal cell septum in which the cross-wall swells around a central pore and the pore is capped on both sides by septal pore caps called parenthesomes.

datasets.title: Bactericidal Membrane Attack Complex formation initiates at the new pole of E. coli
datasets.description: Human immune protection against bacteria critically depends on activation of the complement system. The direct bacteriolytic activity of complement molecules against Gram-negative bacteria acts via the formation of Membrane Attack Complex (MAC) pores. Bactericidal MAC pores damage the bacterial outer membrane, leading to destabilization of the inner membrane. Although it is well-established that inner membrane damage is crucial for bacterial cell death, the critical event causing MAC-mediated inner membrane damage remains elusive. Here we questioned whether the bacterial cell envelope possesses vulnerable spots for MAC pores to insert. We followed the localization of MAC pores on E. coli over time using fluorescence microscopy and elucidate that MAC deposition initiates at the new bacterial pole, which induces inner membrane damage and halts bacterial division. MAC components C8 and C9 preferentially localize at new bacterial poles, while C3b localizes randomly on the bacterial surface. This suggests that preferential MAC localization is determined by one of the initial steps of MAC formation. These findings provide valuable information about the interplay between immune components and the Gram-negative cell envelope.

evidence.notes: Egan, Errington and Vollmer 2020 review peptidoglycan synthesis from cytoplasmic lipid-linked precursors through translocation to polymerisation.

edges.subject: seds_polymerases
edges.description: RodA and FtsW SEDS proteins polymerise exported Lipid II into glycan strands for sidewall and septal peptidoglycan assembly.

edges.subject: penicillin_binding_transpeptidases
edges.description: DD-transpeptidases create peptide bridges between neighboring glycan strands.

evidence.notes: Egan, Errington and Vollmer 2020 review transpeptidation during peptidoglycan synthesis and remodelling.

edges.subject: peptide_crosslinks
edges.description: Peptide crosslinks turn adjacent glycan chains into a single mesh-like sacculus.

evidence.notes: Vollmer, Blanot and de Pedro 2008 describe the bacterial sacculus as glycan strands crosslinked by short peptides.

edges.subject: peptidoglycan
edges.description: The closed, crosslinked sacculus is the stress-bearing layer that keeps internal turgor pressure from rupturing the cell.

evidence.notes: Vollmer, Blanot and de Pedro 2008 review how peptidoglycan architecture gives bacteria a protective, shape-maintaining wall.

functions.label: selective permeability barrier
functions.description: The plasma membrane separates cytoplasm from the external milieu while membrane proteins mediate controlled import, export, and ion movement.

functions.description: In bacteria and archaea, respiratory and ATP-synthase complexes in the cytoplasmic membrane use ion gradients across the membrane for energy conservation.

causal_graphs.title: Membrane lipids and proteins form a selective cell boundary
causal_graphs.description: Amphipathic lipids assemble into a plasma-membrane permeability boundary. Integral membrane proteins embedded in that boundary provide the selective transport and energy-linked activities that make the membrane functional.
causal_graphs.scope_notes: This graph captures the class-level lipid-boundary and integral-protein organization shared by microbial plasma membranes without choosing a bacterial, archaeal, or fungal lipid topology or biosynthesis pathway.

discussions.prompt: Avoid bilayer-only wording for the taxon-spanning plasma membrane record.

records.label: S-layer
records.definition: A paracrystalline monomolecular array of one or more (glyco)protein species that self-assemble on the outermost surface of the cell envelope, with oblique, square or hexagonal lattice symmetry. S-layers are common in Archaea, where they are often the sole wall component, and widespread but patchily distributed in Bacteria.

components.label: S-layer protein (SLP)
components.role: The lattice-forming subunit; self-assembles in vitro.

evidence.notes: Sleytr et al. 2014 review SLP self-assembly and lattice types. The review reports generally one protein/glycoprotein species with molecular masses of 40-170 kDa; this is subunit mass, not copies per lattice.

records.definition: A proteinaceous Bacillus thuringiensis inclusion body that accumulates Cry, Cyt, and related pesticidal crystal proteins as a parasporal crystalline deposit.

components.role: Strain-specific toxin protoxins that crystallize into the parasporal inclusion and can become active against susceptible cells after solubilization and proteolytic activation.

evidence.notes: Palma et al. 2014 review Bacillus thuringiensis parasporal crystalline inclusions as containing Cry and Cyt proteins, plus additional crystal proteins of varied known or unknown activities.

The Crossref-indexed abstract for Insell and Fitz-James 1985 reports that the Bacillus thuringiensis subsp. israelensis inclusion has two electron-microscopic lattice classes with distinct major polypeptides; the ASM article and PDF were blocked by Cloudflare during curation, so no verbatim snippets were copied.

records.label: plastoglobule
records.definition: A lipoprotein particle present in chloroplasts.

curation_history.changes: Scaffolded by scripts/new_record.py

Added chloroplast parthood, UniProt Subcellular Location xref, reviewed-label lipid core and monolayer components, Chlamydomonas taxonomic scope, a thylakoid lipid-remodeling function, record-level evidence, and a nonmechanistic plastoglobule-thylakoid graph.

Resolved #649 by adding the GO exact synonyms PG and plastoglobuli; resolved #650 by changing plastoglobule parthood to the immediate GO:0009570 chloroplast stroma compartment and adding GO:0009570 evidence.
#2321: Qualify plant versus algal topology, mark lipid exchange as proposed, and correct the GO composition attribution.

components.label: plastoglobule lipid core
components.grounding_notes: GO:0010287 lists non-polar lipids, prenylquinones, plastoquinone and tocopherols; no single source-neutral ChEBI identifier denotes that mixture. Carotenoids are discussed separately in the Rottet et al. 2015 review, not in this GO definition.
components.role: Hydrophobic lipid-rich interior that stores neutral lipids and prenyl lipids inside the chloroplast plastoglobule.

evidence.notes: GO:0010287 defines plastoglobules as lipoprotein particles rich in non-polar lipids and prenyl lipids.
Rottet, Besagni and Kessler 2015 review plastoglobules as thylakoid-associated lipid droplets involved in chloroplast lipid metabolism.

components.label: plastoglobule lipid monolayer
components.grounding_notes: Austin et al. 2006 resolved a half-unit lipid membrane continuous with the thylakoid outer leaflet in higher plants. Engel et al. 2015 observed apparently discontinuous Chlamydomonas plastoglobules with occasional punctate contacts, subject to tomogram resolution limits. GO:0034430 denotes a generic lipid-droplet monolayer, not a plastoglobule-specific boundary.
components.role: Lipid boundary surrounding the plastoglobule core; permanent thylakoid continuity is a higher-plant observation, not established for the algal example.

evidence.notes: Austin et al. 2006 used electron tomography and freeze-fracture imaging of higher-plant chloroplasts to resolve a half-unit membrane continuous with the thylakoid outer leaflet.

Engel et al. 2015 found Chlamydomonas plastoglobules apparently discontinuous from adjacent thylakoids, sometimes with punctate contacts; their tomograms did not resolve the two lipid-bilayer leaflets.

taxonomic_distribution.note: Plastoglobules are present in the Chlamydomonas reinhardtii chloroplast and were resolved by in situ cryo-electron tomography.

canonical_examples.note: Unicellular green alga whose native chloroplast architecture was imaged by cryo-focused ion beam milling and in situ cryo-electron tomography, revealing plastoglobules among thylakoid and pyrenoid subcompartments.

functions.label: thylakoid lipid remodeling
functions.description: Plastoglobules participate in chloroplast lipid metabolism and thylakoid remodeling. Exchange of lipid metabolites with thylakoids is a proposed model, not a directly established transport mechanism in the cited review or the Chlamydomonas example.

evidence.notes: Rottet, Besagni and Kessler 2015 review evidence that plastoglobules participate in thylakoid lipid remodeling.
Gene Ontology cellular-component term for plastoglobule.

Gene Ontology cellular-component term for chloroplast.

Engel et al. 2015 resolved the native Chlamydomonas reinhardtii chloroplast by in situ cryo-electron tomography.
Austin et al. 2006 reported permanent plastoglobule-thylakoid coupling in the higher-plant chloroplasts studied; this topology is not established as universal in algae.
Rottet, Besagni and Kessler 2015 reviewed plastoglobule roles in thylakoid lipid remodeling.

causal_graphs.title: Higher-plant plastoglobule architecture and proposed lipid exchange
causal_graphs.description: The higher-plant model places a lipid core within a monolayer continuous with the thylakoid outer leaflet. This architecture motivates a lipid-exchange hypothesis; it is not evidence for universal continuity or direct transport in algae.
causal_graphs.scope_notes: Higher-plant architecture from Austin et al. 2006 and a proposed lipid-remodeling model from Rottet et al. 2015. Engel et al. 2015 instead observed apparently discontinuous Chlamydomonas plastoglobules, with resolution caveats. No specific transport mechanism is established here.

evidence.notes: Austin et al. 2006 resolved plastoglobules as particles enclosed by a half-unit membrane.

edges.subject: plastoglobule_lipid_monolayer
edges.description: In the higher-plant chloroplasts examined by Austin et al. 2006, the plastoglobule half-unit membrane was continuous with the outer thylakoid leaflet.

evidence.notes: Austin et al. 2006 used electron tomography and freeze-fracture imaging of higher-plant chloroplasts to resolve a half-unit membrane continuous with the thylakoid outer leaflet.

edges.subject: plastoglobule
edges.description: Lipid supply and exchange during thylakoid remodeling are proposed roles; structural contact alone does not demonstrate metabolite movement.

evidence.notes: Rottet, Besagni and Kessler 2015 discuss a proposed lipid-supply and remodeling model alongside evidence for plastoglobule lipid metabolism.

components.label: polyhydroxyalkanoate polymer core
components.grounding_notes: CHEBI:53388 is exact for poly(hydroxybutyrate), a common PHB core polymer, but the GO:0070088 record covers PHA granules with multiple possible hydroxyalkanoate polymer chemistries.
components.role: Hydrophobic polyester storage material that forms the granule core and stores carbon plus reducing power.

evidence.notes: Kelly et al. 2024 describe Pseudomonas putida PHA as a polymeric carbon-rich storage material sequestered in carbonosomes.

Bresan et al. 2016 used fluorescent phospholipid-binding LactC2 probes in vivo, not a quantitative chemical-fraction analysis. Native producer granules lacked detectable probe labeling; rare labeling of isolated granules was interpreted as membrane contamination. Recombinant E. coli granules were a distinct context.

components.label: PHA synthases
components.grounding_notes: PHA synthases are grouped by granule-associated polymerization role here; exact family groundings differ between short-chain and medium-chain-length PHA systems and were left for a dedicated family-level curation pass.
components.role: Granule-associated polymerase enzymes that synthesize PHA polyester and remain attached to nascent granules.

evidence.notes: Pfeiffer and Jendrossek 2012 localized PHB synthase PhaC1 to nascent and mature PHB granules in Cupriavidus necator H16.

components.label: phasins
components.grounding_notes: Phasins are curated as a granule-surface protein class; no single InterPro, Pfam, or NCBIfam accession was chosen as exact for the heterogeneous phasins that decorate PHA granules across PHA-producing bacteria.
components.role: Amphipathic granule-surface proteins that bind the PHA core and influence granule size, number and surface coverage. A formation requirement for the heterogeneous phasin class is not established here; changes in granule size or number are not failure to form granules.

evidence.notes: Pfeiffer and Jendrossek 2012 localized multiple Cupriavidus necator H16 phasins to PHB granules. Single phaP6 or phaP7 deletions did not visibly alter granule formation, but do not establish dispensability of all phasins.

edges.subject: phasins
edges.description: Phasins bind to the PHA granule surface and are the major granule-associated surface proteins.

evidence.notes: Pfeiffer and Jendrossek 2012 localized multiple phasins to PHB granules in Cupriavidus necator H16.

edges.subject: polyhydroxyalkanoate_granule
edges.description: The assembled granule holds carbon and reducing power in polyester form for later mobilization.

evidence.notes: Kelly et al. 2024 describe Pseudomonas putida PHA as a polymeric carbon-rich storage material sequestered in carbonosomes.

discussions.prompt: Should a phospholipid monolayer be curated as a PHA granule component?
discussions.rationale: GO:0070088 still mentions a phospholipid monolayer from the older structural model, but Bresan et al. 2016 reported that purified PHA granules contain PHA and protein and no detectable phospholipids, so the monolayer is deliberately not curated as a component. Correction (2026-10-16): the earlier experiment description above was inaccurate. Bresan et al. used phospholipid-binding fluorescent probes in vivo; rare labeling of isolated granules was attributed to contamination, not a bulk chemical composition measurement. The native-producer results and recombinant E. coli observations must be distinguished.
discussions.resolution_note: Do not add a universal phospholipid-monolayer component on this evidence. The decision is bounded to the tested native producer systems and probe sensitivity; it does not assert that phospholipids can never associate with any recombinant or isolated PHA granule.

evidence.notes: Bresan et al. 2016 Results: native producer in vivo LactC2 assays; isolated granules had less than 1% fluorescent particles, interpreted as contamination; recombinant E. coli granules sometimes labeled.

discussions.prompt: Resolve exact broad groundings for PHA polymer cores, PHA synthases and phasins.
discussions.rationale: A curated ChEBI match was verified for poly(hydroxybutyrate), but the GO:0070088 record is broader than PHB; likewise, PHA synthase and phasin families are heterogeneous enough that exact family CURIEs need a separate InterPro/Pfam/NCBIfam pass.

discussions.prompt: How do bacterial polyphosphate granules relate to acidocalcisome-like membrane structures?

functions.description: Provides the membrane-bounded environment in which coccolith calcite crystals develop. This site-of-formation claim does not specify the molecular mechanism that sets crystal shape.

evidence.notes: Results and Figures 2-3 image membrane-enclosed coccoliths at different developmental stages in Calcidiscus leptoporus.
Figures 3-4 distinguish the calcite-forming compartment from the separate calcium-rich storage compartment in Emiliania huxleyi.

Avrahami et al. (2026), Journal of the American Chemical Society. Primary Results, Discussion, Conclusions, figure captions and supplementary culture/imaging Methods read. Membrane-crystal proximity varies with position and stage; mechanistic compartmentalization remains an interpretation of structural and elemental observations.

Sviben et al. (2016), Nature Communications. Primary microscopy Results, Discussion and culture Methods read. The calcium/phosphorus-rich storage compartment is distinct from the coccolith-vesicle/reticular-body system; apposition does not establish continuity or an identified transfer mechanism.
Verified broad intracellular membrane-bounded organelle parent, not an exact coccolith-vesicle identity.

discussions.prompt: Keep the coccolith-forming vesicle distinct from its mineral product and neighboring calcium store.
discussions.rationale: Similarity in calcium content or close membrane apposition does not make these entities equivalent.
discussions.notes: Hidden/ignored-inclusive repository searches found no duplicate label, alias or primary citation. QuickGO coccolith and coccolithogenesis searches returned zero hits; all 481 results of the broader coccolith-vesicle query were inspected without an exact label/definition match. GO:0043231 supplies a broad parent without imposing a spherical geometry. Neither a coccolith nor the extracellular coccosphere is a synonym for the vesicle. The reticular body is not asserted as an exact synonym. Golgi derivation does not by itself establish persistent Golgi parthood. The calcium/phosphorus storage compartment is not imported into this record.

evidence.notes: Introduction and Results distinguish mineral, surrounding membrane and extracellular coccoliths.
Figures 3 and 6 distinguish storage and calcification compartments.

discussions.prompt: Do not assign unidentified luminal particles to a full ATPase complex or import cargo scaffolds as vesicle-building proteins.
discussions.rationale: Ultrastructural resemblance is insufficient to choose a protein family or infer transport activity.
discussions.notes: The 2026 Figure 4 average of 716 membrane-associated particles is approximately half the height of the comparison ATPase and challenges a full-ATPase assignment. The particles are observed, but their identities and functions remain unresolved. No ATPase, ion transporter, cytoskeletal protein or guessed accession is asserted as a constituent. The organic base plate and calcite are treated here as the developing coccolith cargo rather than verified molecular building blocks of the vesicle boundary. Lack of detected cytoskeletal contact is not evidence of biological absence.

evidence.notes: Results and Figure 4 explicitly discuss limited structural resolution and uncertain particle identity.

discussions.prompt: Resolve molecular transport, membrane shaping, developmental dynamics and occurrence across additional species and life-cycle phases.
discussions.rationale: Near-native snapshots and elemental maps establish morphology but do not independently prove a general causal mechanism.
discussions.notes: Membrane-crystal proximity bands in Calcidiscus are not asserted as sealed suborganelles or a universal continuous physical mold. Proposed chemical subcompartments and local growth inhibition remain hypotheses; no causal graph or universal distance, concentration, stoichiometry or prevalence is asserted. The later Calcidiscus study detects luminal calcium, so the earlier Emiliania nondetection is not generalized as absence. Exact protein composition and how these observations extend to other coccolith types require further evidence.

evidence.notes: Discussion and Conclusions retain open questions about solutes, transporters, membrane proximity and organic macromolecules.
Discussion proposes calcium-transfer routes without identifying the relevant transport machinery.

records.label: endoplasmic reticulum

components.label: flattened IMC alveolar membranes
components.grounding_notes: The flattened vesicles that make up the apicomplexan inner membrane complex are the membranes of GO:0070258 itself; no narrower source-neutral lipid or membrane CURIE was curated for this first record.
components.role: Flattened double-membrane cisternae that lie beneath the parasite plasma membrane and form the membranous part of the apicomplexan pellicle.

evidence.notes: Ferreira et al. 2021 review the Plasmodium IMC as a double membrane organelle beneath the parasite plasma membrane.
Dearnley et al. 2012 resolved flattened subpellicular membrane compartments beneath the Plasmodium falciparum gametocyte plasma membrane.

components.label: alveolin subpellicular network
components.grounding_notes: Alveolins are an alveolate-specific, repeat-containing protein family on the cytoplasmic face of the inner membrane complex, but no exact family CURIE was curated for the first GO:0070258 record.
components.role: Peripheral membrane proteins that form a cytoskeletal network on the cytoplasmic face of the IMC.

evidence.notes: Ferreira et al. 2021 review alveolins as Alveolata-specific IMC proteins that form a subpellicular network at the IMC cytoplasmic face.
Kono et al. 2012 analysed Plasmodium alveolin proteins in inner-membrane-complex architecture across asexual and sexual malaria-parasite stages.

taxonomic_distribution.note: The inner membrane complex is a pellicle organelle of apicomplexan parasites, with stage-specific architecture in Plasmodium and lineage-specific functional differences.

canonical_examples.note: Human malaria parasite in which the IMC has been studied through asexual and sexual stages, including gametocyte subpellicular-membrane assembly.

functions.label: pellicle shape support
functions.description: The IMC and associated subpellicular proteins stabilize parasite morphology as part of the apicomplexan pellicle.

evidence.notes: Ferreira et al. 2021 review the Plasmodium IMC as a compartment that confers cell stability and shape.

functions.label: daughter-cell scaffolding
functions.description: The IMC provides a scaffold for apicomplexan daughter-cell formation during parasite replication.

evidence.notes: Kono et al. 2012 followed IMC architecture during asexual and sexual Plasmodium development.
Ferreira et al. 2021 review the IMC as an important scaffold during daughter-cell formation in Plasmodium spp.

functions.label: glideosome anchoring for motility
functions.description: The apicomplexan IMC anchors gliding-motility machinery used for parasite movement and host-cell invasion.

evidence.notes: Ferreira et al. 2021 review the IMC as the anchor for the actin-myosin glideosome that powers gliding motility and invasion.
Ferreira et al. 2021, The Dynamic Roles of the Inner Membrane Complex in the Multiple Stages of the Malaria Parasite, Frontiers in Cellular and Infection Microbiology.

discussions.resolution_note: Include Hsp78 and Ssc1 as associated machinery, not a fixed coat or invariant constituent set. records.label: microneme
records.definition: A small, elongated secretory organelle that forms part of the apical complex, located along the main axis of an apicomplexan parasite cell within the extreme apical region and at the periphery under the inner membrane complex. Micronemal proteins function during parasite attachment and penetration into the target cell.

components.label: phagocytic vesicle lipid bilayer
components.role: Lipid-bilayer material that forms the phagocytic vesicle membrane boundary around ingested particulate cargo.

evidence.notes: GO:0030670 identifies the phagocytic vesicle membrane surrounding a phagocytic vesicle.

components.grounding_notes: GO:0030670 and UniProt SL-0205 identify the whole phagocytic vesicle membrane; no separate source-neutral CURIE was curated for the generic lipid constituent of that membrane.

taxonomic_distribution.note: Dictyostelium discoideum phagosomes have membranes that are progressively remodeled after particle uptake.

canonical_examples.note: Amoebozoan model whose purified latex-bead phagosome membranes were profiled across a maturation time course.

functions.label: phagosome maturation
functions.description: The phagocytic vesicle membrane is progressively remodeled as newly formed phagosomes mature toward late digestive compartments.

evidence.notes: GO:0090382 defines phagosome maturation as cellular rearrangement of phagosome constituent parts after early phagosome formation.
Gotthardt et al. 2002 dissected Dictyostelium phagosome maturation into temporally distinct membrane-trafficking phases.

causal_graphs.title: Phagocytic vesicle membrane topology

causal_graphs.scope_notes: The graph captures the phagocytic vesicle membrane boundary without asserting specific Rab, V-ATPase, protease, or actin recruitment mechanisms.

records.label: photosynthetic membrane
records.definition: A membrane enriched in complexes formed of reaction centers, accessory pigments and electron carriers, in which photosynthetic reactions take place.

curation_history.changes: Scaffolded by scripts/new_record.py

components.grounding_notes: No exact source-neutral CURIE for the lipid matrix shared by cyanobacterial thylakoids and purple-bacterial chromatophores was verified in this pass.
components.role: Membrane lipid matrix that embeds photosynthetic pigment-protein complexes and separates aqueous phases so light-driven electron flow can build an electrochemical proton gradient.

evidence.notes: GO defines photosynthetic membranes as membranes in which photosynthetic reactions take place.

Feniouk et al. 2002 assayed light-driven ATP synthesis across sealed Rhodobacter capsulatus chromatophore vesicle membranes.

components.label: photosynthetic reaction center complexes
components.grounding_notes: Reaction-center complexes span oxygenic photosystem I/II and anoxygenic bacterial reaction-center antenna cores; no single exact GO cellular-component term was curated for the whole set.
components.role: Pigment-protein complexes that carry the primary photochemistry of photosynthesis by converting excitation energy into charge separation within the membrane.

evidence.notes: GO includes reaction centers in the definition of a photosynthetic membrane.
Perez-Boerema et al. 2024 review photosystem I and photosystem II reaction centers as major thylakoid membrane complexes.
Bahatyrova et al. 2004 imaged dimeric reaction-center LH1-PufX core complexes in native purple-bacterial photosynthetic membranes.

taxonomic_distribution.note: Most cyanobacteria use thylakoid photosynthetic membranes for oxygenic light reactions; Gloeobacter-like lineages are the major exception because they photosynthesize at the plasma membrane.
Photosynthetic membranes occur in phototrophic bacterial clades, including cyanobacterial thylakoids and the chromatophore membranes of purple photosynthetic bacteria.

canonical_examples.note: Cyanobacterial model whose thylakoid photosynthetic membranes have been used to map native photosystem organization.
Purple photosynthetic bacterium whose native chromatophore photosynthetic membrane architecture was resolved by atomic force microscopy.

evidence.notes: GO defines photosynthetic membranes as the membrane site where photosynthetic reactions take place.
Perez-Boerema et al. 2024 review the thylakoid membrane electron-transport chain.
Comayras et al. 2005 analyzed quinone-linked cyclic electron transport in Rhodobacter chromatophore membranes.

causal_graphs.title: Photosynthetic membranes couple light absorption to membrane electron flow
causal_graphs.description: Light-harvesting complexes, reaction-center complexes, quinone carriers and quinol-oxidizing cytochrome complexes are embedded in or associated with a photosynthetic lipid bilayer, enabling light reactions that drive photosynthetic electron transport and proton-gradient formation.
causal_graphs.scope_notes: The graph records the shared membrane-level light-reaction architecture without modeling oxygenic PSII-to-PSI linear transport, purple-bacterial cyclic RC-LH1/bc1 transport, phycobilisome rod and core organization, chlorosome baseplates, soluble carriers or ATP synthase coupling in detail.

edges.subject: antenna_pigments
edges.description: Accessory pigments are held in protein-pigment antenna complexes that tune absorption and excitation transfer.

evidence.notes: GO defines light-harvesting complexes as protein-pigment complexes.
Sui 2021 reviewed phycobilin chromophores attached to phycobiliproteins in phycobilisome antennae.

edges.subject: light_harvesting_complexes
edges.description: Light-harvesting complexes broaden spectral capture and route excitation energy toward reaction-center photochemistry.

evidence.notes: GO defines light-harvesting complexes by radiant-energy harvest and transfer to reaction centers.
Bahatyrova et al. 2004 imaged LH2 antennae around purple-bacterial RC-LH1-PufX cores.

edges.subject: reaction_centers
edges.description: Reaction-center complexes are integral membrane constituents of photosynthetic membranes.

evidence.notes: GO defines photosynthetic membranes by their enrichment in reaction centers.
Casella et al. 2017 mapped photosystems in native Synechocystis thylakoid membranes.

edges.subject: reaction_centers
edges.description: Light-excited reaction centers reduce membrane-associated quinone or electron carriers that relay redox equivalents through the photosynthetic chain.

evidence.notes: Perez-Boerema et al. 2024 review plastoquinone reduction by thylakoid PSII.
Comayras et al. 2005 analyzed quinone exchange between RC-LH1-PufX cores and cytochrome bc1.

edges.subject: electron_carriers
edges.description: Reduced quinones diffuse within photosynthetic membranes to quinol-oxidizing cytochrome complexes.

evidence.notes: Perez-Boerema et al. 2024 place cytochrome b6f downstream of plastoquinol in the thylakoid chain.
Comayras et al. 2005 modeled quinone traffic to cytochrome bc1 in Rhodobacter chromatophores.

edges.subject: cytochrome_complexes
edges.description: Cytochrome complexes connect quinol oxidation to proton translocation across the photosynthetic membrane.

evidence.notes: Perez-Boerema et al. 2024 describe cytochrome b6f as a proton-gradient-generating thylakoid complex.
Feniouk et al. 2002 measured proton-motive-force driven ATP synthesis across chromatophore membranes.

edges.subject: photosynthetic_membrane
edges.description: The photosynthetic membrane organizes reaction centers, quinone carriers and cytochrome complexes for membrane-localized photosynthetic electron transport.

evidence.notes: GO defines photosynthetic membranes as the membrane site of photosynthetic reactions.
Perez-Boerema et al. 2024 review thylakoid electron transport.

discussions.prompt: Resolve how far to project membrane parthood for LH2 rings, phycobilisomes and chlorosome baseplates before adding lineage-specific antenna rows under photosynthetic membranes.
discussions.rationale: Purple-bacterial LH2 complexes are integral chromatophore membrane complexes, whereas cyanobacterial phycobilisomes and green-bacterial chlorosome antennae can be peripherally attached to a photosynthetic membrane or baseplate rather than embedded in the bilayer itself.

evidence.notes: Bahatyrova et al. 2004 imaged integral LH2 complexes in purple-bacterial chromatophore membranes.
Sui 2021 reviewed phycobilisomes as large antennae associated with cyanobacterial thylakoid membranes.
Nielsen et al. 2016 resolved the CsmA chlorosome baseplate that couples chlorosomes to membrane reaction centers.

discussions.prompt: Keep ATP synthases out of this broad photosynthetic-membrane definition unless a child membrane record explicitly includes them as part of the same curated membrane system.
discussions.rationale: Thylakoid and chromatophore membranes both maintain proton motive force for ATP synthesis, but GO:0034357 is defined by reaction centers, accessory pigments and electron carriers rather than by the downstream ATP synthase.

evidence.notes: GO defines a photosynthetic membrane without naming ATP synthase as a defining component.
Feniouk et al. 2002 show that chromatophore vesicle membranes can drive ATP synthase without establishing ATP synthase as part of the GO:0034357 parent class.

records.label: rhoptry
records.definition: A large, club-shaped secretory organelle that forms part of the apical complex of an apicomplexan parasite, and consists of a bulbous body and a narrow electron-dense neck that extends through the conoid at the apical tip of the parasite. The rhoptry necks serve as ducts through which the contents of the rhoptries are secreted after attachment to the host has been completed and at the commencement of invasion. Rhoptry proteins function in the biogenesis and host organellar association of the parasitophorous vacuole.

records.label: bacterial microcompartment
records.definition: A bacterial protein-shelled organelle in which a selectively permeable polyhedral shell encapsulates pathway enzymes to segregate segments of metabolism from the cytosol.

curation_history.changes: Scaffolded by scripts/new_record.py

Added BMC synonymy, organelle parentage, generic BMC-H/BMC-T/BMC-P shell and lumen-cargo components, bacterial taxonomic scope, a Haliangium ochraceum shell example, encapsulation and permeability functions, core evidence, and a protein-shell encapsulation graph.
Resolved issue #209 by changing metabolosome from BROAD_SYNONYM to NARROW_SYNONYM because metabolosomes are the catabolic subset of bacterial microcompartments.

components.label: BMC-H facet shell proteins
components.grounding_notes: BMC-H proteins are single Pfam00936-domain shell proteins, but the Pfam family also includes tandem-domain BMC-T proteins, so no exact family CURIE was curated.
components.role: Hexameric single-domain shell proteins that tile the polyhedral shell facets around the encapsulated enzyme cargo.

evidence.notes: Kerfeld et al. 2018 review BMC-H proteins as hexameric shell tiles that form microcompartment facets.
Sutter et al. 2017 resolved BMC-H proteins in an intact Haliangium ochraceum BMC shell.

components.label: BMC-T gated shell proteins
components.grounding_notes: BMC-T proteins contain fused BMC domains with varied gating and redox specializations; no exact source-neutral family CURIE for only BMC-T shell proteins was curated.
components.role: Pseudohexameric tandem-domain shell proteins that can form trimers or double trimers and introduce larger gated pores.

evidence.notes: Kerfeld et al. 2018 review BMC-T proteins as pseudohexameric tandem-domain shell proteins with gated pores in some BMCs.
Greber et al. 2019 used cryo-EM to analyze BMC-T interactions in the Haliangium ochraceum shell.

components.label: BMC-P vertex shell proteins
components.grounding_notes: The BMV/Pfam03319 family covers BMC vertex proteins across carboxysomes and metabolosomes but does not by itself denote a single lineage-neutral assembled vertex component.
components.role: Pentameric shell proteins that cap polyhedral vertices and help close the proteinaceous organelle shell.

evidence.notes: Kerfeld et al. 2018 review BMC-P proteins as pentamers placed at the vertices of BMC shells.
Sutter et al. 2017 extracted the BMC-P vertex protein structure from the intact Haliangium ochraceum shell.

components.label: encapsulated lumen enzyme cargo
components.grounding_notes: BMC enzyme cargo differs by metabolic locus, so no exact family CURIE for the whole cargo class was curated.
components.role: Lineage- and locus-specific enzymes enclosed by the shell; their identities define carboxysome, propanediol, ethanolamine, and other BMC metabolic types.

evidence.notes: Kerfeld et al. 2018 review the different enzymes encapsulated by carboxysome and metabolosome BMCs.
Sutter et al. 2021 cataloged BMC locus diversity by combining shell proteins with adjacent signature enzymes and auxiliary genes.

taxonomic_distribution.note: Bacterial microcompartment loci are widespread but patchily distributed across bacterial genomes.

canonical_examples.note: The Haliangium ochraceum HO shell was used to solve an intact 6.5-MDa bacterial microcompartment shell structure.

functions.label: metabolic pathway encapsulation
functions.description: The protein shell spatially segregates enzyme cargo so BMCs can concentrate useful pathway intermediates or retain toxic and volatile ones.

evidence.notes: Kerfeld et al. 2018 review BMCs as organelles that encapsulate enzymes for autotrophic carbon fixation and heterotrophic substrate catabolism.

functions.label: selective metabolite permeability
functions.description: Small pores through BMC-H and BMC-T shell tiles control the movement of substrates, products, cofactors, and volatile intermediates across the shell.

evidence.notes: Greber et al. 2019 analyzed BMC-T pores in intact Haliangium shells and modeled them as a gated permeability route through the shell.
Kerfeld et al. 2018 review BMC shell proteins as selectively permeable pore-containing tiles.

discussions.prompt: Should the RuBisCO assembly chaperone RbcX (Q31N04) be a carboxysome component?

records.label: encapsulin nanocompartment
records.definition: A proteinaceous nanocompartment, 24 to 42 nm across, built from a single HK97-fold shell protein that self-assembles into an icosahedron. Cargo enzymes are packaged inside by a short targeting peptide that binds the shell interior; the commonest cargoes are ferritin-like iron-mineralising proteins and peroxidases.

components.label: encapsulin shell protein
components.stoichiometry: 60 subunits (T=1) or 180 (T=3), depending on the family
components.role: The single protein that forms the icosahedral shell; it shares the HK97 fold with bacteriophage capsids.

evidence.notes: Giessen 2016 describes the HK97-fold shell and its T=1 and T=3 assemblies.
The 2017 survey reports shell families across thousands of genomes.

components.role: Ferritin-like proteins, dye-decolourising peroxidases and others, drawn in by a C-terminal targeting peptide. The shell assembles without them, which is why they are dispensable to the structure.

The 2017 survey classifies encapsulin systems by their cargo.

causal_graphs.title: Targeting peptides load iron-mineralising cargo into the shell
causal_graphs.description: Encapsulin shell proteins self-assemble into HK97-fold icosahedra, and C-terminal targeting peptides load ferritin-like cargo proteins onto the shell interior. The enclosed cargo oxidises and mineralises iron inside the nanocompartment, storing iron away from the cytosol to buffer iron and oxidative stress.
