edges.subject: cargo
edges.description: C-terminal targeting peptides on cargo enzymes bind the shell interior and direct cargo loading.

evidence.notes: Sutter et al. 2008 identified conserved binding sites inside the shell for short C-terminal targeting peptides on oxidative-stress enzymes.
Altenburg et al. 2021 dissected hydrophobic and ionic interactions that govern targeting-peptide binding to Thermotoga maritima and Myxococcus xanthus encapsulin shells.

edges.subject: encapsulin_shell
edges.description: The closed shell packages ferritin-like enzymes and separates their iron chemistry from the surrounding cytosol.

evidence.notes: McHugh et al. 2014 showed that Myxococcus xanthus encapsulin shells are lined with ferritin-like adaptor proteins that nucleate iron-rich granules.

edges.subject: cargo
edges.description: Encapsulated ferritin-like cargo oxidises Fe2+ and drives ferric mineral deposition in the lumen.

evidence.notes: McHugh et al. 2014 linked ferritin-like encapsulin cargoes with iron sequestration inside the protein shell.

edges.subject: ferrous_iron
edges.description: Ferrous iron is converted into a sequestered iron-rich mineral core inside the nanocompartment.

evidence.notes: McHugh et al. 2014 observed dense iron-rich cores in native Myxococcus xanthus encapsulins.

edges.subject: ferric_mineral_core
edges.description: Internal mineralisation stores iron away from the cytosol and protects cells from iron starvation and oxidative stress.

evidence.notes: McHugh et al. 2014 tied the Myxococcus xanthus encapsulin system to iron storage and oxidative-stress protection.

causal_graphs.title: HK97-fold shells assemble around peptide-tagged cargo
causal_graphs.description: Type 1 encapsulin shell protomers form HK97-fold icosahedral cages. Short cargo targeting peptides bind pockets on the shell interior during assembly, producing a closed nanocompartment that selectively encloses enzyme cargo.

edges.subject: shell
edges.description: Encapsulin shell proteins adopt an HK97-like fold that is reused by many viral capsid proteins.

evidence.notes: Sutter et al. 2008 resolved the Thermotoga maritima encapsulin shell and found an HK97-like shell-protein fold.

edges.subject: hk97_protomer
edges.description: Shell protomers self-assemble into icosahedral cages that can form without cargo and package cargo when targeting peptides are present.

evidence.notes: McHugh et al. 2014 resolved the 180-subunit Myxococcus xanthus EncA shell and its ferritin-like cargo.
Giessen 2016 reviews T=1 and T=3 encapsulin shell architectures.

edges.subject: cargo
edges.description: Encapsulin cargo proteins carry terminal peptide tags that are sufficient to route native or heterologous proteins into the assembling shell.

evidence.notes: Cassidy-Amstutz et al. 2016 identified minimal peptide tags that load proteins into Thermotoga maritima encapsulins in vivo and in vitro.

edges.subject: targeting_peptide
edges.description: Hydrophobic and ionic contacts between targeting peptides and the shell interior determine shell binding strength and cargo-loading specificity.

evidence.notes: Altenburg et al. 2021 characterized and engineered targeting-peptide interactions with Thermotoga maritima and Myxococcus xanthus shell interiors.

edges.subject: interior_binding_pocket
edges.description: Binding sites on the inner shell surface capture targeting peptides and localize cargo enzymes into the nascent shell lumen.

evidence.notes: Sutter et al. 2008 identified conserved binding sites for targeting peptides on the inside of the Thermotoga maritima shell.

edges.subject: cargo_loaded_shell
edges.description: Completion of the shell leaves the targeted enzymes packaged inside the encapsulin lumen.

evidence.notes: McHugh et al. 2014 showed ferritin-like cargoes enclosed inside native Myxococcus xanthus encapsulin shells.

components.label: Eut BMC-domain shell proteins
components.role: Hexameric and pseudohexameric BMC-domain proteins that tile the facets and pores of the ethanolamine-utilization shell.
components.grounding_notes: EutS, EutM, EutL, and EutK carry BMC domains, but the generic BMC-domain families also cover carboxysome and other metabolosome shell proteins, so no exact ethanolamine-metabolosome shell family was curated.

evidence.notes: Kofoid et al. identified the Salmonella eut operon and its eutS, eutM, eutL, eutK, and eutN shell homologues.
Takenoya et al. solved E. coli EutL and EutM shell protein structures and assigned them to the ethanolamine-utilizing microcompartment shell.
Held et al. assembled EutS-only and EutSMNLK nanocompartments from Salmonella shell proteins in E. coli and confirmed BMC-like particles by TEM.

components.label: EutN BMC-P vertex shell protein
components.role: Pentameric BMV-family shell protein homologous to the pentamers that close bacterial microcompartment vertices.
components.grounding_notes: The BMV-domain family covers EutN and PduN but also broader carboxysome and glycyl-radical metabolosome vertex proteins; no exact family for EutN alone was curated.

taxonomic_distribution.note: Ethanolamine-utilization bacterial microcompartment loci are patchily distributed in bacterial genomes rather than universal.

canonical_examples.taxon_label: Salmonella enterica subsp. enterica serovar Typhimurium str. LT2
canonical_examples.note: Kofoid et al. mapped the 17-gene eut operon and Huseby and Roth dissected private cofactor recycling in the Salmonella Eut microcompartment.

functions.label: ethanolamine catabolic process
functions.description: Sequesters ethanolamine-catabolic chemistry in a protein shell so the cell can convert ethanolamine through acetaldehyde to acetyl-phosphate, acetyl-CoA, and ethanol.

evidence.notes: Huseby and Roth used Salmonella genetics to test how the Eut microcompartment routes ethanolamine catabolism and recycles private NAD and CoA pools.

functions.label: acetaldehyde and cofactor confinement
functions.description: Restricts acetaldehyde and large NAD/CoA cofactors from freely diffusing between the lumen and cytosol during ethanolamine breakdown.

evidence.notes: Genetic evidence supported retention and recycling of NAD and CoA within the Eut compartment and restricted diffusion of the acetaldehyde intermediate.
Kaval and Garsin review bacterial ethanolamine utilization, including eut loci and the Eut microcompartment in pathogens.
Kofoid et al. defined the 17-gene Salmonella eut operon and recognized five shell-protein homologues.
Huseby and Roth provide a mechanistic genetic model of ethanolamine catabolism and cofactor recycling within the Eut microcompartment.

causal_graphs.title: Eut shell proteins assemble a cargo-targeting compartment
causal_graphs.description: Eut BMC-domain and BMC-P shell proteins form the ethanolamine-utilization protein shell. Short targeting sequences on lumen enzymes bind the shell protein EutS, and EutQ modulates the number of EutSMNLK compartments in a recombinant assembly system.

edges.subject: eut_bmc_domain_shell_proteins
edges.description: EutS alone, and the EutSMNLK shell-protein set, can assemble BMC-like shells in a heterologous E. coli system.

evidence.notes: Held et al. observed EutS and EutSMNLK polyhedral bodies by TEM after recombinant expression in E. coli.

edges.subject: eutn_vertex_shell_protein
edges.description: EutN belongs to the vertex-protein lineage of bacterial microcompartment shell proteins and is pentameric in solution.

evidence.notes: Wheatley et al. found that EutN is predominantly pentameric in solution while studying BMC vertex proteins.

edges.subject: eutc_targeting_peptide
edges.description: The EutC N-terminal targeting peptide binds EutS, linking ethanolamine-catabolic cargo to the Eut shell.

evidence.notes: Fan et al. showed that EutC and EutE targeting sequences bind the EutS shell protein to mediate cargo encapsulation.

edges.subject: eutc_targeting_peptide
edges.description: An N-terminal EutC targeting sequence can route fused cargo to the lumen of recombinant Eut shells.

evidence.notes: Choudhary et al. used the 19-residue EutC targeting sequence to localize reporters to EutS and EutSMNLK compartments.

edges.subject: eutq
edges.description: EutQ interacts with EutM in vitro and can promote multiple EutSMNLK compartments in the recombinant assembly system.

evidence.notes: Held et al. found EutQ-EutM binding in pull-down assays and linked EutQ to multiple EutSMNLK compartment formation.

functions.label: 1,2-propanediol catabolic process

evidence.notes: Havemann et al. tied Pdu polyhedral bodies to coenzyme B12-dependent 1,2-propanediol degradation in Salmonella.

functions.label: propionaldehyde sequestration
functions.description: Keeps the reactive propionaldehyde intermediate inside the protein shell to limit DNA and cellular damage.

records.label: AP-2 adaptor complex
records.definition: A heterotetrameric AP-type membrane coat adaptor complex that consists of alpha, beta2, mu2 and sigma2 subunits, and links clathrin to the membrane surface of a vesicle, and the cargo receptors during receptor/clathrin mediated endocytosis. Vesicles with AP-2-containing coats are normally found primarily near the plasma membrane, on endocytic vesicles. In at least humans, the AP-2 complex can be heterogeneric due to the existence of multiple subunit isoforms encoded by different alpha genes (alphaA and alphaC).

records.label: AP-type membrane coat adaptor complex
records.definition: Any of several heterotetrameric complexes that link clathrin (or another coat-forming molecule, as hypothesized for AP-3 and AP-4) to a membrane surface; they are found on coated pits and coated vesicles, and mediate sorting of cargo proteins into vesicles. Each AP complex contains two large (a beta and one of either an alpha, gamma, delta, or epsilon) subunits (110-130 kDa), a medium (mu) subunit (approximately 50 kDa), and a small (sigma) subunit (15-20 kDa).

evidence.notes: GO:7770042 defines the bindosome complex as an archaeal membrane-associated complex consisting of sugar-binding proteins.

discussions.prompt: Should BasEF or BasABC be curated as constituents of the mature bindosome complex?
discussions.rationale: GO:7770042 identifies the bindosome as the assembled sugar-binding-protein complex. Zolghadr et al. showed that BasEF and BasABC are type-IV-pilin-like machinery required for functional surface localization of the sugar-binding proteins; BasEF was not required for formation of the extracted 400 and 600 kDa complexes themselves. The Bas system was therefore left out of the mature bindosome component list.

evidence.notes: The study separated the BasEF membrane complex from the high-molecular-mass sugar-binding-protein complexes.

discussions.prompt: Resolve whether SlaA or other S-layer material should be modeled as a bindosome constituent or as a neighboring envelope scaffold.
discussions.rationale: The 600 kDa S. solfataricus sugar-binding-protein complex co-purified with the main S-layer protein SlaA, whereas the 400 kDa complex contained GlcS and SSO3043 and the GO definition keeps the bindosome scoped to sugar-binding proteins. This pass therefore records the S-layer association without making SlaA a source-neutral bindosome subunit.

evidence.notes: Zolghadr et al. found SlaA in the larger extracted complex and interpreted the sugar-binding complexes as S-layer associated.

discussions.prompt: Keep Bni1, Aip5, the exocyst, and MAPK signaling proteins outside the first cellular-bud-tip polarisome component boundary.
discussions.rationale: GO:0000133 and later Saccharomyces polarisome studies implicate Bni1, Aip5, and other actin-assembly factors in the broader polarisome, but Sheu et al. 1998 directly support a Spa2/Pea2/Bud6 12S complex and discuss Bni1 only as a possible additional component. records.label: clathrin-coated pit
records.definition: A part of the endomembrane system in the form of an invagination of a membrane upon which a clathrin coat forms, and that can be converted by vesicle budding into a clathrin-coated vesicle. Coated pits form on the plasma membrane, where they are involved in receptor-mediated selective transport of many proteins and other macromolecules across the cell membrane, in the trans-Golgi network, and on some endosomes.

records.label: CORVET complex
records.definition: A multimeric protein complex that acts as an endosomal tethering complex (CORVET = class C core vacuole/endosome tethering) by cooperating with Rab GTPases to capture endosomal vesicles and trap them prior to the action of SNAREs; the complex is involved in endo-lysosomal biogenesis and required for transport between endosome and vacuole. The Saccharomyces cerevisiae complex contains Vps8p, Vps3p, Pep5p, Vps16p, Pep3p, and Vps33p.

canonical_examples.note: The paper studies procyclic cells: strain 29-13 for inducible RNAi and Lister 427 for endogenous tagging, with tagging also performed in RNAi lines. functions.label: regulation of TbPLK protein turnover
functions.description: WDR1 depletion slows the loss of TbPLK during a cycloheximide chase and increases its abundance in procyclic T. brucei. This supports a turnover-regulatory role for the named association, but does not establish direct covalent ubiquitination of TbPLK by a purified complex.

evidence.notes: Figure 6A-C measures abundance at 24/48 hours of RNAi and a 0-6-hour chase after 24 hours of induction. Figure 6D detects less polyubiquitinated material in TbPLK immunoprecipitates, but the Results explicitly leave its identity unresolved: TbPLK itself and/or associated proteins.

functions.label: support of bilobe duplication and flagellum attachment
functions.description: WDR1 RNAi impairs bilobe duplication, basal-body segregation and new flagellum-attachment-zone assembly, with detached flagella at 48 hours. These are perturbation-supported cellular outputs, not proof that every phenotype is mediated exclusively by direct TbPLK ubiquitination.

evidence.notes: Figures 4-5 show basal-body, bilobe, FAZ and attachment phenotypes after 48 hours of WDR1 RNAi. Figure 7 shows persistent phospho-Ser54 TbCentrin2 staining in late-cycle cells at 24 hours. TbPLK overexpression in S4 Figure phenocopies several effects, but is not a rescue or an epistasis test.

discussions.prompt: Separate CRL4WDR1 from generic Cul4 and other DDB1 complexes.
discussions.rationale: Shared cullin or receptor names do not establish equivalence.
discussions.notes: Parsed identities and synonyms across 876 prior records and whole-repository hidden/ignored-inclusive name, locus, DOI, PMID and candidate identifier searches found no existing record; prior mentions concern the Cullin-E boundary. Native GO queries for CRL4WDR1 and WDR1 found no entry. GO:0080008 is the broader Cul4-RING parent; GO:0031464/0031465 denote A/B subclasses, GO:0043494 denotes CLRC, and GO:0070912/0070913 denote different transcription-coupled repair heterodimers. Exact Complex Portal name and locus queries found no entry. WDR1 hits there denote predicted human complexes, not this assembly.

discussions.prompt: Keep the WDR1-specific assembly distinct from Cullin-E and broader Cullin-D isolates.
discussions.rationale: A scaffold identity is not the identity of all its receptor-specific complexes.
discussions.notes: The primary paper assigns WDR1 to TbCUL4/Tb927.3.1290 and reports no co-isolation with TbCUL1/Tb927.11.11430. The modern Table 1 calls these TbCul-D and TbCul-E respectively, despite its Discussion attributing the older PLK result to Cullin-E. Modern Cullin-D isolates contain DCAF proteins Tb927.11.3190 and Tb927.8.840 and Rbx1/Tb927.10.1810; they do not establish those as members of CRL4WDR1. Neither a Cul4A versus Cul4B assignment nor generic Cullin-D nuclear localization is imposed on this receptor-specific record.

discussions.prompt: Resolve exact component-family mappings and studied-strain protein examples.
discussions.rationale: Broad families and reference-genome annotations do not supply exact experimental examples.
discussions.notes: InterPro search and reference-protein entry pages were checked completely: IPR045093 and IPR050358 are broader families; WDR1 hits are other WDR proteins. UniProt exact-locus queries resolve unreviewed Q57XW2 and Q586I3 to the reference strain 927/4 GUTat10.1, not the studied Lister 427 or 29-13 cells; the WDR1 locus query returned no entry. These verified reference annotations are not entered as experimental protein_examples, and the reviewed-only automated adapter is not relaxed. The structured iModulonDB adapter lists 28 datasets without a matching Trypanosoma organism: not applicable, not negative biological evidence.

discussions.prompt: Do not convert captured client proteins or experimental markers into obligatory constituents.
discussions.rationale: Co-isolation and downstream readouts have different biological roles.
discussions.notes: TbPLK is recovered with the three tagged core proteins in Figure 3D, but the source interprets it as a recognized client. It is not asserted to be an invariant structural subunit. TbCentrin2, TbCentrin4, FAZ1, TbPSA6, antibodies, recombinant-expression hosts and APC/C are not constituents. Cdc27/APC/C depletion also affects TbPLK turnover, so CRL4WDR1 is not claimed as the sole pathway. Rbx1 and other DCAFs from broader Cullin-D isolates are excluded pending receptor-specific membership evidence.

discussions.prompt: Establish the complete catalytic assembly and direct covalent substrate reaction.
discussions.rationale: Co-immunoprecipitation and chase data do not identify all catalytic subunits or ubiquitinated proteins.
discussions.notes: The 2017 paper does not experimentally identify a RING subunit within the WDR1-specific assembly, resolve fixed stoichiometry or show purified CRL4WDR1 ubiquitinating TbPLK. Figure 6D leaves the polyubiquitinated species unresolved. Figure 8 is a model, not proof of the entire ubiquitination, turnover, phosphorylation and FAZ chain. TbPLK overexpression phenocopy does not establish exclusive mediation. Subunit assembly essentiality, physical dimensions and broad clade distribution remain unset.

discussions.prompt: Resolve localization and architecture of the assembled CRL4WDR1 particle.
discussions.rationale: Subunit immunofluorescence does not demonstrate colocalization of all constituents.
discussions.notes: Figure 2E-F localizes endogenous WDR1-3HA to the basal-body/bilobe region, with partial TbPLK overlap in G1 and reduced WDR1 signal later. It does not image the whole assembly. The unchanged multi-panel Figure 2 is hosted as explicitly bounded subunit-localization and interaction evidence under verified CC BY 4.0; A-D include schematics, yeast assays and biochemical blots. No organelle part_of relation or whole-complex atomic structure is inferred.

evidence.notes: The paper's own Cullin-E knockdown Results and Figure 6B-D provide DAPI counts and GRASP immunofluorescence. The function is bounded to these observations, not the paper's conflicted attribution of older WDR1/PLK work to Cullin-E.

PMID:28052114, native PMC5241021.1. The older Results and Figure 3 assign the WDR1-DDB1 association to TbCUL4, Tb927.3.1290, and report that TbCUL1, Tb927.11.11430, did not co-precipitate WDR1. discussions.prompt: Keep the Cullin-E association distinct from other cullins and TUSK.
discussions.rationale: A scaffold name or broader ligase class is not an exact complex identity.
discussions.notes: Whole-repository hidden/ignored-inclusive name, locus, alias, DOI, PMID and accession searches found only the prior unaccepted discovery lead; parsed identities and synonyms across 875 prior records found no match. Native GO Cullin-E, TbCul-E, CulE, TbCulE, exact-locus and cullin queries were inspected with complete returned pages. GO:0031461 is the verified broader cullin-RING ubiquitin ligase complex parent, not an exact identity. Exact Complex Portal queries found no entry. The modern letter-based naming avoids assumed orthology to mammalian CUL1. Old protein name TbCUL1 is not adopted as an exact complex synonym.

discussions.prompt: Resolve exact source-neutral families for the four component classes.
discussions.rationale: Broad domains or family matches cannot establish exact paralog membership.
discussions.notes: InterPro search scopes and declined broader matches are recorded per component. IPR051031 includes broader RING-box machinery; its unchecked LLM description is not experimental evidence. Protein examples are unset: source loci are retained only in evidence notes and no UniProt accession is guessed. Skp1.2 is not TUSK SkpZ. The kelch class represents four enriched proteins, not a tested invariant four-subunit cassette.

discussions.prompt: Exclude the older WDR1-DDB1-PLK mechanism from Cullin-E.
discussions.rationale: The newer paper's citation attribution conflicts with the cited primary identifiers.
discussions.notes: The older paper's TbCUL4 is Tb927.3.1290, corresponding to the newer Table 1 TbCul-D scaffold. It co-precipitates WDR1 and DDB1. The older TbCUL1 is Tb927.11.11430, corresponding to TbCul-E, and explicitly does not co-precipitate WDR1 in that experiment. The newer Discussion nevertheless attributes prior PLK-substrate evidence to Cullin-E. No WDR1, DDB1 or PLK constituent, substrate or causal edge is imported from that reference. This is a boundary decision, not a claim that all possible Cullin-E/PLK relationships have been disproved.

discussions.prompt: Establish simultaneous composition, localization and direct ligase substrates.
discussions.rationale: Affinity enrichment and RNAi abundance changes do not reconstruct a molecular mechanism.
discussions.notes: Table 1, Figure 2B and the checked S3 rows support association. They do not resolve copy number, direct pairwise contacts, kelch-subunit co-occupancy or assembly requirements. The RNAi outputs support the bounded function and NONMECHANISTIC graph, not direct ubiquitylation of KKT9 or other changed proteins. No organellar part_of, physical dimension, essential assembly subunit, broad phylogenetic assembly distribution or exact narrower GO function is inferred.

discussions.prompt: Keep uncertain enrichment hits and modifiers separate from established constituent classes.
discussions.rationale: Not every affinity-isolation hit is a stable structural constituent or client.
discussions.notes: The source notes Nedd8, RFC subunit 4, VPS13 and Tb927.6.4360 among Cullin-E co-isolates, while saying the physiological significance of most additional hits is unclear. Nedd8 is retained as modification context rather than an obligatory complex subunit. These hits, changed RNAi proteins, other cullin baits and other Rbx-like paralogs are not promoted to components or direct substrates.

discussions.prompt: Reconcile RNAi specimen detail, control counts and the duplicate Figure 7 locus.
discussions.rationale: Source-specific descriptions must not be silently harmonized.
discussions.notes: The isolation/tagging Methods specify procyclic Lister 427 cells; the RNAi subsection does not explicitly specify stage/strain, the qRT-PCR subsection names parental 2T1, and Figure 6A depicts bloodstream forms. No claim makes all experiments procyclic. Native PRIDE lists six wild-type isolation controls, versus seven in paper Methods and S3 (WT_1 through WT_7); Figure 2's caption uses n > 3. The record does not flatten these to one replicate count. Figure 7 labels both ESAG11 and VSG-related points with Tb927.1.4900; neither ambiguous assignment enters the graph. The reference database 927 release 42 is annotation context, not a cultured strain. The structured iModulonDB adapter lists 28 datasets without a matching Trypanosoma organism; it is not applicable, not negative biological evidence.

discussions.prompt: Obtain experimentally resolved imaging of the assembled Cullin-E complex.
discussions.rationale: Phenotype images and generic or predicted models do not locate or resolve this assembly.
discussions.notes: Original Figures 2, 6 and 7 were visually inspected and their native media checksums verified. They show enrichment, RNAi phenotypes and proteomic changes, not a resolved Cullin-E particle. Figure 6D marks Golgi and mitochondria, not Cullin-E. Figure 8 is a generic scheme based on a human Cullin1 complex, not an experimental structure of this complex. Native JATS establishes CC BY 4.0, but no figure is hosted or presented as a complex micrograph.

records.label: EMC complex

Added broad GO synonymy, membrane-complex parentage, ER-membrane parthood, Saccharomyces scope, an EMC-dependent membrane-insertion function, GO/DOI evidence, a nonmechanistic ER transmembrane-domain insertion graph, and an EMC subunit-boundary TODO.

Resolved #1167 by narrowing the insertion graph edge, resolved #1168 by adding top-level Sec61 GO evidence, and resolved #1169 by pairing Emc3/Kre27 and Emc5/Aim27 aliases in the subunit-boundary TODO.

records.label: epsilon DNA polymerase complex
records.definition: A heterotetrameric DNA polymerase complex that catalyzes processive DNA synthesis in the absence of PCNA, but is further stimulated in the presence of PCNA. The complex contains a large catalytic subunit and three small subunits, and is best characterized in Saccharomyces, in which the subunits are named Pol2p, Dpb2p, Dpb3p, and Dpb4p. Some evidence suggests that DNA polymerase epsilon is the leading strand polymerase; it is also involved in nucleotide-excision repair and mismatch repair.

records.label: ESCRT IV complex
records.definition: An ESCRT complex that has AAA-ATPase activity and is involved in ESCRT-mediated intralumenal vesicle formation and the final stages of cytokinesis. The complex catalyzes disassembly of the ESCRT III filament around the neck of the budding vesicle in an ATP-driven reaction, resulting in membrane scission and recycling of the ESCRT III components back to the cytosol. In yeast, it is formed by the AAA ATPase Vps4 and its cofactor Vta1.

records.label: GATOR1 complex
records.definition: A GTPase-activating protein (GAP) complex that regulates TORC1 signaling by interacting with the Rag GTPase. In human, the GATOR1 complex consists of DEPDC5, NPRL2, and NPRL3. In S. cerevisiae, this complex is referred to as SEACIT and contains the Iml1p, Npr2p, and Npr3p proteins.

records.label: Gemini of Cajal bodies
records.definition: Nuclear bodies frequently found near or associated with Cajal bodies (also called coiled bodies or CBs). Gemini of coiled bodies, or 'gems', are similar in size and shape to CBs, and often indistinguishable under the microscope. Unlike CBs, gems do not contain small nuclear ribonucleoproteins (snRNPs); they contain a protein called survivor of motor neurons (SMN) whose function relates to snRNP biogenesis. Gems are believed to assist CBs in snRNP biogenesis, and to play a role in the etiology of spinal muscular atrophy (SMA).

causal_graphs.title: INO80-C carries yeast chromatin remodeling
causal_graphs.description: In Saccharomyces cerevisiae, Ino80, Rvb1, Rvb2, Ies5, Ies3, Nhp10, Ies6, Ies1, Arp8, Arp4, Act1, Taf14, Ies2, Ies4 and Arp5 form the INO80-C chromatin-remodeling complex.
causal_graphs.scope_notes: The graph records the 15 INO80-C constituent classes and their connection to ATP-dependent chromatin remodeling without resolving the ordered assembly pathway or the nucleosome-engagement cycle.

discussions.prompt: Keep the chromosome assembly distinct from its formation process and tether subcomplexes.
discussions.notes: Ignored- and hidden-inclusive name, synonym, identity and citation searches plus parsed YAML identities found no existing bouquet record. GO:0045141 denotes meiotic telomere clustering, a biological process, not the structure. GO:0034993 and GO:1990612 denote smaller membrane linkers; neither is an exact identity. The bouquet is a protein-DNA assembly within the nucleus, containing nuclear chromosomes and their telomeric regions, not part of one chromosome or the whole SPB. It is distinct from the quiescent telomere hypercluster, ordinary interphase clusters, telomerase and the entire horsetail nucleus.

discussions.prompt: Find exact whole-protein family identifiers for Taz1, Bqt1, Bqt2, Csm4 and Kms1.
discussions.notes: Complete native InterPro protein responses were inspected. Taz1 has only domains/superfamilies, Kms1 an EF-hand superfamily; Bqt1, Bqt2 and Csm4 return HTTP 204 with no matches. UniProt supplies verified sequence exemplars. No isolated domain or guessed family is promoted to whole-protein identity.

discussions.prompt: Resolve the core-versus-accessory placement of Csm4 within the smaller t-LINC complex.
discussions.notes: The two 2020 studies agree that Csm4 associates with telomeres and Mps2 and is required for normal dynamics, but differ in their structural model: Fan et al. call Mps2-Mps3-Csm4 a heterotrimeric t-LINC, while Lee et al. favor Csm4 as an accessory regulator. Both place it at the assembled telomere-tether system, so it is retained as a bouquet constituent without deciding the smaller complex boundary. The proposed nonamer in Fan Figure 7 is not measured copy number and is not imported as stoichiometry.

discussions.prompt: Keep species-specific components and assembly requirements separate.
discussions.notes: These are component classes with explicitly paired sequence examples, not a claim that every bouquet contains every listed factor. Mps3 and Sad1 share the verified SUN family; Mps2 and Kms1 are not forced into one family. Depletion/deletion requirements in one organism do not establish record-wide universal essentiality, which remains UNKNOWN. The Kms1 recruitment experiment in 2025 is partial ectopic mitotic reconstitution; it is not presented as a normal meiotic localization assay.

discussions.prompt: Distinguish telomere tethers from drivers, general envelope anchors and downstream machinery.
discussions.notes: The composition list focuses on chromosome ends and their bouquet connector system. Bqt3/Bqt4 are general pre-existing envelope anchors discussed by the sources; their importance for encounter/attachment is not by itself bouquet-core occupancy. Myo2 binds the assembled budding-yeast tether and Myo1/Myo4 can label dispersed meiotic ends, but those movement assays do not establish specific residence in the clustered bouquet; external motors and entire actin/microtubule systems are therefore not listed as bouquet constituents. Cdc2/Cdc13 transiently accumulate at the telomere-SPB interface as signaling effectors; no fixed bouquet subunit status is inferred. Rec8 chromosome-axis, histone chromatin, Tub4/Sid4/Ppc89 SPB and envelope markers do not automatically import their entire complexes. The nucleus, SPB, telocentrosome and synaptonemal complex are not collapsed into the bouquet.

discussions.prompt: Identify the physiological release mechanism without equating correlation with causation.
discussions.notes: Rap1 phosphorylation increases through meiotic prophase, but the tested multi-site phosphomimetic and nonphosphorylatable mutants retain normal bouquet formation and dissociation. Rap1-DD337AA instead specifically disrupts Bqt1/2 binding and clustering. Induced Bqt1-AID destruction demonstrates maintenance dependence, not that auxin or the engineered degron is a natural disassembly pathway. The complete physiological trigger remains unresolved.

discussions.prompt: Avoid making clustering the unique cause of every mutant phenotype.
discussions.notes: Budding-yeast pairing/gene-conversion experiments perturb tethering and movement together; Mps2 also has independent SPB roles. Fission-yeast bqt1 mutants can still divide successfully in a subset of cells. The 2025 experiments show that retained Ndc80-SPB attachment inhibits meiotic entry/bouquet completion, while ectopic Bqt1/Bqt2 recruitment in mitosis is incomplete. Neither the mitotic reconstituted t-LINC nor a partial telocentrosome is itself the normal meiotic bouquet.

discussions.prompt: Preserve experimental taxon and measurement scope.
discussions.notes: Only the two directly characterized yeast species are canonical examples; no fungal prevalence or absence row is inferred. UniProt strain identities are sequence references, not exact SK1 or mating-stock assignments. Fission-yeast persistence through prophase and transient budding-yeast clustering are not assigned one universal duration. Fluorescent focus counts, spatial resolution, schematic models and culture-hour measurements do not supply molecular stoichiometry, dimensions or universal chromosome counts.

discussions.prompt: Identify which primary sources were read in full relevant sections and which were abstract-only.
discussions.notes: Current PMC OA native JATS was used for the five later papers cited here. The 2006 Cell publisher page returned 403 and Europe PMC supplied only a subscription-linked abstract. The bridge claim is explicitly abstract-level; no inaccessible Methods, figure or quantitative result is invented. Additional older leads PMC1885593 and PMC1569800 were absent from the current OA metadata bucket; that is a route-specific limit, not a claim that no full text exists.

records.label: membrane coat
records.definition: Any of several different proteinaceous coats that can associate with membranes. Membrane coats include those formed by clathrin plus an adaptor complex, the COPI and COPII complexes, and possibly others. They are found associated with membranes on many vesicles as well as other membrane features such as pits and perhaps tubules.

records.label: methionine-importing ABC transporter complex
records.definition: An ATP-binding cassette (ABC) transporter complex that is capable of methionine-importing activity. An example is the bacterial MetNIQ methionine transporter, that consists of the dimeric ATPase subunit MetN located at the cytoplasmic side of the plasma membrane and the dimeric transmembrane subunit MetI. MetQ is regarded as the periplasmic methionine-binding chaperon subunit, and is capable of transporting methionine from the periplasm into the cytoplasm in an ATP-dependent manner.

causal_graphs.title: CheA and CheW network receptor trimers into a hexagonal array
causal_graphs.description: Methyl-accepting chemotaxis proteins assemble as receptor trimers of dimers. CheA dimers and CheW couplers connect neighboring trimers through a baseplate of alternating CheA regulatory domains and CheW subunits, yielding the extended hexagonal array that supports cooperative chemotaxis signalling.

edges.subject: mcp
edges.description: Chemoreceptor dimers are organized as trimers of dimers at vertices of the lattice.

evidence.notes: Briegel et al. 2012 combined crystallography with cryo-electron tomography of native arrays to place receptor trimers of dimers at hexagonal lattice vertices.

edges.subject: chea
edges.description: One CheA dimer connects two receptor trimers as part of the core chemotaxis signaling unit.

evidence.notes: Li and Hazelbauer 2011 showed that purified core signaling complexes contained two receptor trimers of dimers and two CheW proteins for each CheA dimer.

edges.subject: chew
edges.description: CheW links receptor trimers to CheA and helps build the repeating core signaling unit.

evidence.notes: Li and Hazelbauer 2011 established the two-CheW stoichiometry of the two-trimer, one-CheA-dimer core unit.

edges.subject: receptor_trimer
edges.description: Receptor trimer vertices surround rings of alternating CheA P5 regulatory domains and CheW couplers.

evidence.notes: Briegel et al. 2012 modeled the receptor trimers surrounding alternating CheA/CheW rings in the cytoplasmic baseplate.

edges.subject: chea_chew_ring
edges.description: The CheA/CheW ring and associated receptor trimers define the repeated building block of the chemoreceptor array.

evidence.notes: Briegel, Li, Bilwes, Hughes, Jensen and Crane 2014 reviewed a sequential assembly model in which two receptor trimers, one CheA dimer, and two CheW monomers form the core functional unit before hexagons and the superlattice.

edges.subject: core_signaling_unit
edges.description: Core units share CheA/CheW linkers to produce the extended hexagonal chemotaxis array with conserved 12 nm spacing.

evidence.notes: Briegel et al. 2009 found a conserved hexagonal lattice spacing of about 12 nm in chemoreceptor arrays from diverse bacteria and archaea.
Briegel et al. 2012 showed that CheA dimerization domains link neighboring rings to form the extended stable array.

causal_graphs.title: Chemoeffector binding is amplified by the array and read out as phospho-CheY
causal_graphs.description: The array's function is gain: binding at one receptor reaches ~35 kinases, and the cluster's output is a phospho-CheY signal the flagellar motor reads. The edges stop where the cited source stops -- the CheA-to-CheY phosphotransfer step itself is not stated quotably here, and motor switching is a trait rather than part of this structure.

nodes.label: methyl accepting chemotaxis protein complex
nodes.description: The assembled array. The cited source calls it the chemosensory array or receptor cluster; the node carries the GO label its grounding defines.

nodes.label: flagellar motor reversal to clockwise rotation

edges.subject: chew
edges.description: CheW is what puts the kinase under receptor control.

evidence.snippet: Chemoreceptors form stable core signaling complexes with two cytoplasmic proteins, CheA, a histidine autokinase, and CheW, which couples CheA to receptor control.
evidence.notes: Verbatim from the open-access full text (PMC4417406).

edges.subject: chemoeffector
edges.description: One binding event reaches tens of kinases; this is the array's gain.

evidence.snippet: In the chemosensory array, attractant binding to a single receptor can regulate ~35 CheA kinase proteins [ 82 ].
evidence.notes: Verbatim. The ~35:1 ratio is the quantitative statement of why the array is a structure rather than a collection of receptors.

edges.subject: mcp
edges.description: Receptor conformation sets kinase activity over a 100-fold range.

evidence.snippet: MCP signaling complexes modulate CheA autophosphorylation activity over more than a 100-fold range, most likely through changes in receptor conformation or dynamic motions that allosterically regulate P1-P4' interactions and/or the kinase active site.
evidence.notes: Verbatim. The authors hedge the mechanism with 'most likely'; the 100-fold modulation itself is reported without hedge.

edges.subject: array
edges.description: Cooperativity converts a small concentration change into a large kinase activity change.

evidence.snippet: These receptors operate in cooperative arrays to produce large changes in the activity of a signaling kinase CheA in response to small changes in chemoeffector concentration.
evidence.notes: Verbatim from PMC4417406.

edges.subject: array
edges.description: The cluster's output signal, delivered in pulses.

evidence.snippet: These observations imply that a cell’s receptor cluster produces phospho-CheY signals in a pulsatile manner, consistent with essentially all-ON or all-OFF array behavior.
evidence.notes: Verbatim. Stated as an implication of the observations, not a direct measurement, and the edge is no stronger than that. The CheA-to-CheY phosphotransfer step is not stated quotably in this source, so it is not drawn as an edge.

edges.subject: chea
edges.description: Autophosphorylated CheA binds CheY and transfers its phosphoryl group to generate the phospho-CheY signal read by the flagellar motor.

evidence.notes: Stewart 1997 kinetically characterized CheA-to-CheY phosphotransfer as reversible CheY binding to phospho-CheA followed by rapid reversible phosphoryl transfer.

edges.subject: phospho_chey
edges.description: Phospho-CheY diffuses to the motor and is the clockwise signal.

evidence.snippet: The motor that was closer to the cell’s receptor cluster reversed first, followed by the second motor with a time lag determined by its distance from the first motor and consistent with the intracellular diffusion rate of phospho-CheY, the CW rotational signal.
evidence.notes: Verbatim. Motor reversal is included as the readout of this structure's output, not as part of the structure; the motility phenotype itself is the METPO:1000702 trait link.

discussions.prompt: The CheA-to-CheY phosphotransfer step is missing from the signalling graph because Parkinson et al. 2015 does not state it in a quotable sentence. Should a primary source for the phosphotransfer be added, or is the array's output adequately described by 'the receptor cluster produces phospho-CheY signals'?
discussions.rationale: The graph deliberately stops where the source stops. Drawing the step from background knowledge would be the defect #161 records.
discussions.resolution_note: Added an evidence-backed CheA-to-phospho-CheY edge from the Stewart 1997 kinetic characterization of CheA-to-CheY phosphotransfer.

Vps13-L1627S bypass restores foci despite ERMES loss, so ERMES is not an obligatory physical template.

ERMES perturbation and Vps13 bypass distinguish ERMES function from obligatory ERMES-complex presence; localization overlap does not prove direct binding.

functions.description: Supports formation and organization of mitochondrial crista junctions through cooperative Mic60-Mic19 assembly and membrane remodeling, within the larger MICOS machinery.

evidence.notes: Mic60 lipid-binding mutants in YPH499-derived yeast lose normal crista junctions and accumulate detached lamellar cristae; purified fungal Mic19 enhances Mic60-driven membrane deformation.

Mic60 oligomerization-interface and Mic60-Mic19 interaction-interface variants impair crista-junction formation in yeast. The complex is not asserted to be sufficient for native crista formation by itself.

Hessenberger et al. (2017), Regulated membrane remodeling by Mic60 controls formation of mitochondrial crista junctions. Full Results, Discussion, methods and Figure 4 inspected in checksum-verified PMC5460017 version 1.

The local complex is a type of inner mitochondrial membrane protein complex; this broader GO term is not its exact identity.
MICOS is the containing complex, not an is-a parent or synonym of the two-component subcomplex.

causal_graphs.title: Direct binding and cooperative membrane remodeling by fungal Mic60 and Mic19
causal_graphs.description: Purified fungal proteins establish direct interaction, Mic60-dependent lipid recruitment, Mic19-enhanced oligomerization and membrane tubulation.
causal_graphs.scope_notes: Biochemical edges concern Chaetomium thermophilum Mic60 soluble region lacking its N-terminal transmembrane anchor and purified Mic19 in Folch liposome assays. They are not a reconstruction of native yeast MICOS, a physiological membrane-leakage claim, or proof of an in situ diffusion barrier. Higher-order assembly is supported, but universal 4:4 stoichiometry is not asserted.

evidence.notes: Isothermal titration calorimetry and domain deletions establish direct binding; isolated Mic19 coiled-coil region does not bind Mic60.

edges.subject: mic60

evidence.notes: Liposome co-sedimentation detects Mic19 in the presence of Mic60; Mic19 alone does not bind the tested membranes.

edges.subject: mic19
edges.description: Mic19 binding promotes higher-order assembly of purified soluble Mic60.

evidence.notes: Hydrodynamic and cross-linking experiments support Mic19-induced oligomerization, with an inferred tetrameric Mic60 arrangement rather than a universal native copy count.

edges.subject: mic60
edges.description: The soluble Mic60 region binds and deforms model lipid membranes through its lipid-binding regions.

evidence.notes: Electron microscopy shows tubulation with purified Mic60; deletion of the amphipathic LBS1 region abolishes lipid binding and remodeling.

edges.subject: lipid_bound_complex
edges.description: Adding full Mic19 increases Mic60-dependent liposome tubulation and branching relative to Mic60 alone.

evidence.notes: Figure 3 reconstitution assays compare Mic60 alone with full Mic19 and Mic19 domain constructs. Full Mic19 stimulates membrane deformation; its domains have different effects on dye leakage.

discussions.prompt: Establish an exact taxon-agnostic Mic19 family grounding without treating DUF1690 membership as identity.
discussions.rationale: Reviewed yeast Mic19 cross-references a fungal DUF family, but the current family description does not establish equivalence to the complete Mic19 component class. CHCH-domain membership alone is also insufficient.

evidence.notes: The current InterPro family label is Protein of unknown function DUF1690 and its description names uncharacterized fungal proteins.
Direct experiments establish the Mic19 component independently of a database family assignment.

discussions.prompt: Determine the native microbial complex architecture and copy number, and directly test the proposed crista-junction strut and diffusion-barrier functions.
discussions.rationale: The 2022 structural model combines isolated fungal domains and engineered fusion constructs. The authors explicitly leave the molecular identity of yeast junction-spanning tomographic densities unresolved. Purified-protein oligomerization does not prove one universal native 4:4 assembly.

evidence.notes: Discussion and Figure 5 present an architectural model and testable barrier/strut hypotheses, not direct molecular identification of a native junction-spanning complex.

discussions.prompt: Keep the Mic60-Mic19 subcomplex distinct from full MICOS, MIB and experimental expression hosts.
discussions.rationale: Other MICOS subunits and outer-membrane partners occur in the surrounding machinery but are not constituent identities of this two-component subcomplex. Expression in Escherichia coli does not make the complex a bacterial structure.
discussions.resolution_note: Only Mic60 and Mic19 are components; MICOS is linked by part_of. Yeast YPH499 derivatives provide the canonical in vivo example. S288c accessions used for family lookup are not added as strain-matched protein examples, and recombinant fusion constructs are not treated as native stoichiometry.

evidence.notes: Methods distinguish fungal protein sequences, bacterial expression hosts, and YPH499-derived yeast experiments.
Structural and yeast experiments address the named Mic60-Mic19 subcomplex within MICOS.

Fis1/Mcr1 dependence differs from earlier steady-state measurements; no exclusive import route, fixed stoichiometry or directly observed exchange between MIM populations is asserted.

evidence.notes: Figure 2: import is impaired in mim1-deletion and mim1-23 mitochondria; imported His-Fis1 co-purifies Mim1 and Mim2. MIM assistance is not equivalent to absolute dependence.

evidence.notes: Figure 4C-D: mim1 perturbations reduce the intermediate, Sam35-HA antibody shift identifies SAM association, and a Sam50 POTRA deletion enhances both MIM-SAM association and Tom6 intermediate formation. Direct molecular handoff is inferred rather than visualized.

discussions.prompt: Distinguish MIM constituents from interacting import systems, substrates and functional substitutes.
discussions.rationale: TOM and SAM association, precursor binding and heterologous rescue do not establish additional constitutive MIM components.
discussions.resolution_note: Keep Mim1 and Mim2 as the two curated constituent families. Do not add TOM, SAM, Tom70, Tom5, Tom6, imported substrates or pATOM36 as MIM components. TOM13 is a historical Mim1 name, not proof of constitutive TOM membership. Do not equate MIM with the mitochondrial inner membrane, MIMAS, or a stable TOM-MIM-SAM supercomplex.

evidence.notes: Separate MIM populations and substrate-dependent Tom70 cooperation.
pATOM36 substitutes for selected yeast MIM functions but poorly rescues Ugo1 import; yeast MIM does not replace the pATOM36 DNA-inheritance function.

discussions.prompt: Resolve the assay-dependent differences in Fis1 and Mcr1 dependence on MIM.
discussions.rationale: The iScience study finds largely preserved mitochondrial levels of Fis1 and Mcr1 and only minor Fis1 mistargeting, whereas the later Cell Reports import assays detect MIM-dependent effects. Steady-state abundance, targeting fidelity and import kinetics are different readouts; these sources do not establish which experimental differences explain the contrast.

evidence.notes: Signal-anchored and tail-anchored Results and Discussion explicitly distinguish strong Msp1 dependence, moderate Gem1 dependence and largely independent Fis1/Mcr1 behavior.
Figures 1-2 report impaired precursor import in mim1-deletion and mim1-23 mitochondria.

discussions.prompt: Resolve native MIM stoichiometry and the proposed exchange between free, TOM-associated and SAM-associated populations.
discussions.rationale: Native-gel migration and complementation do not resolve an intact atomic structure or fixed copy number. Competition and altered association support a dynamic-exchange model without directly observing exchange. The hosted microscopy shows organelle morphology, not molecular MIM localization or structure.

evidence.notes: Discussion proposes redistribution among populations from association and competition experiments.
Figure 5 visualizes mito-GFP morphology in W303-derived deletion/rescue cells. Heterologous coexpression experiments support a two-protein machinery but not fixed native stoichiometry.

discussions.prompt: Distinguish MIMAS from other mitochondrial assemblies.
discussions.rationale: Similar mitochondrial-complex names do not establish equivalent identity.
discussions.notes: Parsed identities and synonyms across 877 prior records and hidden/ignored-inclusive whole-repository searches found no MIMAS record or prior primary citation. Native GO MIMAS search returned no entry; the complete multifunctional result contained two molecular-function terms, not a cellular component. Complex Portal exact-name searches returned no entry. GO:0098800 is an is-a parent; GO:0005743 is the containing membrane. INAC, MICOS, SAM and MIB denote different assemblies. discussions.prompt: Resolve complete membership and architecture.
discussions.rationale: The first record represents experimentally supported classes, not an exhaustive stoichiometry.
discussions.notes: Five classes are curated here. Psd1 enrichment and complexome correlation alone do not make every hit an invariant subunit. MIMAS-A and MIMAS-B migrate at apparent masses near 3.3 and 2.5 MDa; these are not exact particle masses or copy counts. Obtain resolved architecture and appropriately licensed imaging before adding dimensions or a structural image. Primary gels are not hosted under NC-ND terms.

records.label: NuA4 histone acetyltransferase complex
records.definition: A complex having histone acetylase activity on chromatin, as well as ATPase, DNA helicase and structural DNA binding activities. The complex is thought to be involved in double-strand DNA break repair. Subunits of the human complex include HTATIP/TIP60, TRRAP, RUVBL1, BUVBL2, beta-actin and BAF53/ACTL6A. In yeast, the complex has 13 subunits, including the catalytic subunit Esa1 (homologous to human Tip60).

records.label: pyrenoid
records.definition: A non-membrane-bounded organelle found within the chloroplasts of algae and hornworts; responsible for carbon dioxide fixation.

records.label: quiescent telomere hypercluster
records.definition: A nuclear assembly in which multiple chromosome ends and associated subtelomeric chromatin coalesce into fewer enlarged foci during quiescence, characterized in Saccharomyces cerevisiae and Schizosaccharomyces pombe. Nuclear position and assembly requirements depend on species, strain and starvation conditions.

curation_history.changes: Scaffolded by scripts/new_record.py

Added twelve component classes, nine verified protein examples, species-scoped mechanisms, three dataset links, one hosted and two link-only inspected figures, and explicit evidence conflicts and access limits.

components.label: telomere
components.role: Chromosome-end DNA brought together within the nuclear assembly.

evidence.notes: Taz1-marked chromosome ends form fewer, brighter foci on nitrogen starvation; this is not a claim that every chromosome end is individually resolved.

components.grounding_notes: Native SO telomere sequence-feature identity verified; the component denotes chromosome-end DNA, not the entire multi-chromosome hypercluster.

components.label: subtelomere
components.role: Subtelomeric DNA associated with the coalescing chromosome ends.

evidence.notes: Y-prime FISH and chromosome-contact mapping establish subtelomeric association; a Y-prime probe does not label every chromosome end equally.

components.grounding_notes: Native SO subtelomere definition verified; the sequence feature is adjacent to the telomere, not equivalent to the whole hypercluster.

components.label: nucleosome

evidence.notes: Histone H4 tail and K16 substitutions implicate nucleosomal chromatin in hypercluster formation. This is a chromatin-class assertion, not an isoform-specific localization or copy-number measurement.

components.grounding_notes: Native GO definition specifies DNA wound around a multisubunit histone core. Terminal telomeric repeats are not asserted to be uniformly nucleosomal.

discussions.prompt: Keep the multi-chromosome assembly separate from individual telomeres and other nuclear structures.
discussions.notes: Ignored- and hidden-inclusive identity, synonym and citation searches plus parsed YAML identities found no duplicate. OAK GO aliases and native definitions supplied no exact hypercluster term. It is a protein-DNA assembly within the nucleus, not part of one chromosome or necessarily the nuclear envelope. It differs from ordinary cycling-cell telomere clusters, the meiotic bouquet, telomerase and the quiescent nuclear microtubule bundle. Bare hypercluster names are broader synonyms because Sir3 overexpression can induce them outside quiescence.

discussions.prompt: Find exact whole-protein family identifiers for Sir3, Sir4, Taz1 and Esc1.
discussions.notes: Complete native InterPro matches were inspected for P06701, P11978, P79005 and Q03661. Broad ORC1/CDC6 membership and isolated SID, Myb/SANT or repeat domains do not exactly ground these four classes. Reviewed label-only entries retain verified sequence examples pending exact family terms.

discussions.prompt: Resolve condition-dependent central versus peripheral hyperclusters without assigning one universal position.
discussions.notes: The 2015 W303 study places the brightest hyperclusters centrally; the 2016 predominantly BY study places them near the envelope and shows Esc1-dependent position. The 2020 fission-yeast study finds peripheral attachment dependent on Bqt4. Population sorting, strain, age and starvation protocol differ, but no single tested explanation is imposed on the discrepancy. A diffraction-limited proximity measurement is not a molecular tether-distance measurement.

discussions.prompt: Review the full published 2026 Esc1 study when accessible.
discussions.notes: The published abstract of Ruault et al. (PMID 42584369; electronic publication 2026-08-12) proposes redundant PKA-dependent and Esc1-dependent anchoring, progressive loss of anchoring during entry, and central hyperclustering; it argues against altered Sir3-mediated attraction as the main driver. The publisher redirected to an abstract/subscription page and Europe PMC lists no full text. Only the abstract was read: no residue identity, quantitative model parameter or new causal edge is inferred. The 2025 preprint and conference abstract are not treated as independently inspected full-text evidence.

discussions.prompt: Separate required factors in specific assays from universal component necessity.
discussions.notes: Sir2/Sir3/Sir4 deletion impairs budding-yeast assembly, but this does not establish identical requirements across both yeasts or all mutant contexts; their record-wide essentiality is UNKNOWN. Ku80 is directly localized yet individually dispensable. Esc1 and Bqt4 are dispensable positioning machinery, not stoichiometric core residents. Sir3 abundance/spreading is not increased in 2015; 2016 reports a slight abundance change and suggests background differences. No universally increased Sir3 level is asserted.

discussions.prompt: Do not import whole regulatory complexes, markers or tethering diagrams as focus composition.
discussions.notes: Hho1/condensin and H4-state perturbations support chromatin assembly roles, but do not supply hypercluster-specific residence for all regulator subunits. Nucleosomes are retained as the packing class of subtelomeric chromatin, without assigning an H4 isoform or all terminal repeats to nucleosomes. Yku80 localization does not establish Yku70 residence; the 2016 Yku70 nondetection is reported as unpublished. Fission-yeast Rap1 belongs to the same TE2IP/Rap1 family, but the 2020 schematic/established tether is not a direct G0 localization experiment, so no second Rap1 sequence example is added. Bqt3, Man1/Fft3, the whole shelterin complex, telomerase, TERRA, nuclear-pore markers, nucleolus and spindle pole body are not automatically constituents.

discussions.prompt: Resolve survival effects without equating grouping, silencing and envelope attachment.
discussions.notes: The 2015 study reports a modest late chronological-survival benefit associated with Sir3-dependent clustering, including a silencing-defective rescue. The 2016 2/7/14-day assays find no significant requirement for survival or early regrowth in their conditions. These differ in strain, population and assay; no universal longevity function is asserted. In 2020, TERRA accumulation and rearrangements primarily track envelope attachment and become especially pronounced with telomere erosion. Those outcomes are not assigned to grouping alone, and steady-state RNA abundance is not a direct transcription-rate measurement.

discussions.prompt: Keep transcriptional transitions separate from hypercluster dynamics.
discussions.notes: The 2025 W303 study finds transcriptional shutdown before hyperclustering and largely unchanged shutdown in sir3 deletion. On refeeding, transcription starts before declustering; rpb1-1 and phenanthroline support largely independent dispersal, whereas thiolutin gives a distinct, pleiotropic result. RNA polymerase II is therefore not inferred a hypercluster constituent or mandatory disassembly trigger. The 2016 reverse-acetylation and chromosome-decondensation explanations remain hypotheses.

discussions.prompt: Keep experimental taxon, microscopy and morphology scope explicit.
discussions.notes: Only the two characterized yeast species are canonical. Reference-strain UniProt examples do not identify exact W303/BY or fission-yeast assay stocks. No broader fungal prevalence, absence, universal count, dimensions or maturation time is inferred. Foci do not supply molecular stoichiometry; 3C/Hi-C reconstruction is a model, not a micrograph. The 2020 figure captions say live microscopy while Methods describe formaldehyde fixation, so its images are not globally labeled live. The Swi6 centromeric focus and separate nucleolar Sir2 signal must not be mistaken for telomeric foci.

records.label: Ragulator complex
records.definition: A vacuolar membrane-anchored guanine nucleotide exchange factor (GEF) complex for the Rag GTPases (Gtr1-Gtr2 GTPase complex GO:1990131) in TORC1 signaling pathway. In human, Ragulator is comprised of the membrane anchor subunit LAMTOR1 (Meh1p in S. cerevisiae, Lam1 in S. pombe), a GEF subunit LAMTOR2 ( Slm4 in S. cerevisiae , Lam2 in S. pombe ) , LAMTOR3 (no S. cerevisiae ortholog identified, Lam3 in S. pombe) , LAMTOR4 (no S. cerevisiae ortholog identified, Lam4 in S. pombe), and LAMTOR5 (no S. cerevisiae or S. pombe ortholog identified).

records.label: retromer complex
records.definition: A conserved hetero-pentameric membrane-associated complex involved in retrograde transport from endosomes to the Golgi apparatus. The budding yeast retromer comprises Vps35p, Vps29p, Vps26p, Vps5p, and Vps17p. The mammalian complex shows slight variation in composition compared to yeast, and comprises SNX1 or SNX2, SNX5 or SNX6, VPS26A or VPS26B, VPS29, and VPS35.

records.label: retromer, tubulation complex
records.definition: The dimeric subcomplex of the retromer, believed to be peripherally associated with the membrane. This dimeric complex is responsible for remodeling endosomal membranes to form a tube-structure to which cargo molecules are selected for recycling. The budding yeast complex comprises Vps5p and Vps17p, and may contain multiple copies of a Vps5p/Vps17p dimer. The mammalian complex contains SNX1 or SNX2 dimerized with SNX5 or SNX6.

records.label: Rpd3L complex
records.definition: A histone deacetylase complex which deacetylates histones preferentially in promoter regions. Composed of a two copies of catalytic histone deacetylase subunit (S. pombe Clr6/ S. cerevisiae Rpd3p), an Sds-3 family protein (S. pombe /S. cerevisiae Sds3(p) ), two copies of SIN3 family co-repressor (S. pombe Pst1/ S. cerevisiae Sin3p, a WD repeat protein/ histone chaperone (S. pombe Prw1/ S. cerevisiae Ume1p), and a zf- PHD finger ( S. pombe Png2/ S. cerevisiae Pho23p), plus 4 additional subunits, and associated factors.

records.label: Rpd3L-Expanded complex
records.definition: A protein complex that contains a histone deacetylase and is part of the chromatin remodeling machinery. In Saccharomyces cerevisiae this complex contains the Rpd3p, Sin3p, Ume1p, Pho23p, Sap30p, Sds3p, Cti6p, Rxt2p, Rxt3p, Dep1p, Ume6p, Ash1p, Dot6p, Snt1, Sif2p, Set3p, Hos2p, Tos4p and Tod6p proteins.

records.label: Rpd3S complex
records.definition: A eukaryotically conserved histone deacetylase complex which deacetylates histones across gene coding regions. Composed of a catalytic histone deacetylase subunit, a chromodomain protein, a SIN3 family co-repressor, and a WD repeat protein (Clr6p, Alp13p, Pst2p, and Prw1p respectively in Schizosaccharomyces; Rpd3p, Sin3p, Ume1p, Rco1p and Eaf3 in Saccharomyces; homologs thereof in other species).

causal_graphs.title: RSC supports ATP-dependent chromatin remodeling
causal_graphs.description: In Saccharomyces cerevisiae, the Sth1 ATPase and accessory RSC subunits assemble into an ATP-dependent remodeler that engages nucleosomes through the core and Arp-module lobes.

records.label: SAGA complex
records.definition: A SAGA-type histone acetyltransferase complex that deubiquitinates H2A and/or H2B. This complex is organized into several functional submodules: a structural core including the activator binding module and consisting of ADA1 or a homolog, members of the SPT and TAF protein families as well as promotor recruitment factor TRRAP/TRA1, a histone acetyltransferase (HAT) module consisting of GCN5/KAT2A or PCAF/KAT2B, ADA2, ADA3/NGG1, and SGF29 or homologues thereof, a histone deubiquitinase (DUB) module consisting of ATXN7/SGF73, ATXN7L3/SGF11, ENY2/SUS1 and USP22/UBP8 or homologues thereof, and in some taxa a splicing module consisting of SF3B3 and SF3B5 or homologues thereof (not in fungi). In budding yeast also contains Spt8 which distinguishes it from SAGA-like (SLIK) complex (GO:0046695).

records.label: SAS acetyltransferase complex
records.definition: A protein complex that possesses histone acetyltransferase activity and links histone acetylation to the assembly of transcriptionally silent chromatin. In vitro, the complex acetylates lysine 16 of histone H4 and lysine 14 of histone H3, although the latter may not be relevant in vivo. The complex contains a catalytic subunit and at least two other subunits; in Saccharomyces, the catalytic subunit is Sas2p and additional subunits are Sas4p and Sas5p.

records.label: SHREC complex

records.label: SLIK (SAGA-like) complex
records.definition: A SAGA-type histone acetyltransferase complex that contains a smaller form of Spt7 (lacking the SPT8 binding region) than the fungal SAGA complex, and consequently lacks Spt8. The complex is involved in the yeast retrograde response pathway, which is important for gene expression changes during mitochondrial dysfunction.

records.label: stressosome
records.definition: A bacterial multiprotein regulatory assembly with an oligomeric core formed by RsbR-family and RsbS STAS domains and an associated RsbT kinase. Characterized stressosomes organize environmental-stress signaling; their subunit composition and requirement for downstream responses depend on the organism and experimental context.

components.label: Stressosome-associated protein Prli42
components.role: Listeria membrane-associated miniprotein implicated in RsbR-dependent stressosome tethering, not a generic core subunit. Dispensability refers to reconstituted RsbR-RsbS-RsbT assembly without Prli42, not normal localization or stress signaling in vivo.

evidence.notes: EGD-e co-immunoprecipitation identifies RsbR and RsbS among Prli42 partners; deletion and partial complementation support Prli42-dependent membrane association of a subset of RsbR. Fractionation measures RsbR, not counts of intact stressosomes. Purified RsbR-RsbS-RsbT particles assemble without Prli42.
The issuing authority identifies an exact Prli42 protein family; the family label does not establish occurrence of assembled stressosomes in every organism with a homolog.

Parental background of the 2025 genetic experiments, including rsbP-deleted derivatives that retain ethanol-induced sigma-B reporter activity without the RsbR/RsbS core.

functions.label: environmental stress response regulation
functions.description: The stressosome organizes stress-signaling proteins. In tested Bacillus subtilis PY79 derivatives, an intact RsbR/RsbS core promotes rapid onset and shutoff of the ethanol-induced sigma-B response; core loss does not abolish all environmental stress signaling.

evidence.notes: Structural and biochemical characterization establishes the RsbR-RsbS-RsbT regulatory assembly.

Core-deficient, rsbP-deleted PY79 derivatives retain a delayed, longer-lived ethanol response that remains RsbT dependent. Salt responses were also observed; the weak acid-stress response was inconclusive.

causal_graphs.title: Bacillus core-independent stress response
causal_graphs.description: Experimental dependencies of sigma-B reporter output, not a molecular model of stress recognition or kinase release.
causal_graphs.scope_notes: Khadka et al. 2025, PY79-derived strains with the RsbP energy-stress branch removed. Core-deficient conditions eliminate the relevant RsbR paralogs and RsbS while preserving RsbT production. Do not extrapolate to every stressor or species.

edges.subject: ethanol
edges.description: Ethanol retains an inducible response in the tested core-deficient backgrounds that preserve RsbT.

evidence.notes: Population and single-cell reporters detect stress-induced activity despite loss of core proteins.

edges.subject: rsbt
edges.description: RsbT removal abolishes the core-independent ethanol response; this does not identify RsbT as a direct sensor.

evidence.notes: RsbT deletion or translation block prevents core-independent signaling; the kinase-defective D78N allele also compromises the response.

edges.subject: core_loss
edges.description: Comparison with core-intact controls supports altered response kinetics, not direct observation of kinase recapture.

evidence.notes: Core-deficient cells respond later and sustain elevated reporter output longer after ethanol exposure.

discussions.prompt: Resolve exact RsbR, RsbS and RsbT family groundings.
discussions.rationale: The checked UniProt-to-InterPro mappings are broader than each component or describe domains. Label-only components preserve identity without substituting a shared STAS domain for a family.

evidence.notes: RsbRA and RsbS are distinct core subunits.

discussions.prompt: Does loss of stress signaling establish failure of stressosome assembly?
discussions.rationale: No. Formation essentiality is left unknown for the generic core constituents. Bacillus RsbRA/RsbS cores assemble without RsbT; Listeria preparation-dependent assembly results do not justify a universal RsbT requirement. The 2025 RsbT signaling requirement does not establish a structural formation requirement.

evidence.notes: Purified RsbRA/RsbS core reconstitution.
RsbT-dependent signaling without core proteins.

discussions.prompt: Is the stressosome indispensable for environmental stress sensing?
discussions.rationale: Not in every tested context. The 2025 PY79 experiments retain ethanol and salt responses after core loss. A clean rsbRA-rsbS deletion also depresses RsbT production, so its failure to signal cannot by itself establish core necessity. Translation-stop constructs address this confound. The study does not rule out sensory functions for individual RsbR paralogs.

evidence.notes: Genetic dissection with RsbT-production controls.

discussions.prompt: Is Prli42 a universal core constituent or a demonstrated channel?
discussions.rationale: Neither claim is made. Native co-isolation of RsbR and RsbS, fractionation and perturbation justify Listeria-associated membrane machinery. The direct-versus-indirect tether mechanism and localization of every intact assembled particle are not resolved by RsbR fractionation. Prli42 is absent from the reconstituted core and its proposed channel role is speculative.

evidence.notes: Prli42 co-IP, fractionation and reconstitution experiments.

discussions.prompt: Should RsbU, RsbV, RsbW, sigma-B or RsbX be generic core constituents?
discussions.rationale: The curated structural core is RsbR/RsbS with associated RsbT. Downstream signaling proteins are not made constituents merely because their activity depends on the pathway. RsbX-mediated resetting is also not evidence of a stable structural constituent; no RsbX occupancy or exact binding-state claim is imported here.

evidence.notes: Resolved core and biochemically associated RsbT are distinguished from the pathway model.

discussions.prompt: Should a single 60-subunit composition or an RsbS-only crystal shell define all stressosomes?
discussions.rationale: No. Listeria reconstruction supports a 40-RsbR/20-RsbS core, whereas Bacillus reconstructions vary with the reconstruction and symmetry treatment. Exact generic copy numbers are omitted. The RsbS-only icosahedron is crystal packing; solution measurements support a dimer, not a native RsbS-only stressosome.

evidence.notes: Listeria core reconstruction.
Bacillus reconstructions and RsbS SEC-MALS.

discussions.prompt: Resolve the molecular trigger and dynamic signaling mechanism.
discussions.rationale: Static loop accessibility, approximate turret placement and kinetic phenotypes do not directly measure gating, RsbT release or recapture, or direct stress recognition. Exact interface residue claims also require reconciliation of inconsistent numbering in the 2019 Listeria Results and Methods. The graph therefore records experimental dependencies only.

evidence.notes: Static structural models and perturbations.
Reporter dynamics with genetic perturbations.

records.label: t-UTP complex
records.definition: A protein complex that forms a subcomplex of the 90S preribosome and is required for the subsequent assembly of the rest of the preribosome. In S. cerevisiae, it is composed of Utp5p, Utp4p, Nan1p, Utp8p, Utp9p, Utp10 and Utp15p.

records.label: TRAMP complex
records.definition: A multiprotein complex having distributive polyadenylation activity of a variety of RNA substrates including hypomodified and incorrectly folded tRNAs, pre-snRNAs, pre-snoRNAs, incorrectly spliced or processed pre-mRNAs, cryptic unstable transcripts (CUTs), pre-rRNAs and rRNA fragments released as part of rRNA processing. In S. cerevisiae, the complex consists of either Pap2 (also known as Trf4) or Trf5, Air1 or Air2, and Mtr4, and is involved in RNA 3'-end processing and in RNA surveillance and quality control.

records.label: TRAPPI protein complex
records.definition: A complex that tethers COPII vesicles at ER-Golgi intermediate compartment. Its role in this part of the vesicular transport may start at the ER exit sites. Binds to a component of the COPII coat. In yeast it includes the following subunits: Bet3 (as homodimer), Bet5, Trs20, Trs23, Trs31, Trs33 which are regarded as the core subunits of all TRAPP complexes in yeast.

records.label: TRAPPII protein complex
records.definition: A complex that mediates intra-Golgi traffic, Golgi exit, endosome-to-Golgi traffic, and the trafficking of autophagy proteins from Golgi to the phagophore assembly site. Binds to a component of the COPI coat. In yeast it includes the following subunits: Bet3 (as homodimer), Bet5, Tca17, Trs20, Trs23, Trs31, Trs33, Trs65, Trs120, Trs130. The whole complex is thought to dimerize with itself.

components.label: Tpr86 TUSK subunit
components.grounding_notes: Native InterPro Tpr86 search returned no entry. The paper's IPR011990 and IPR002885 are a broad homologous superfamily and a repeat, respectively, not the Tpr86 component family. The source also has conflicting locus strings, so no protein accession is substituted for family identity.
components.role: Constituent recovered with SkpZ and Usp7; a substrate-scaffolding role is proposed, not demonstrated.

evidence.notes: Native SkpZ affinity isolation identified Tpr86; reciprocal tagged-Tpr86 isolation in three biological replicates recovered SkpZ and Usp7 (Results and Figure 6B). Figure 3A supports Tpr86-Usp7 co-isolation. These support complex membership, not exact pairwise contact sites or assembly essentiality.

components.label: Usp7 TUSK subunit
components.grounding_notes: Native InterPro Usp7 search returned IPR024729, an ICP0-binding domain rather than a whole Usp7 family. No exact source-neutral family mapping for this constituent was established. Exact source-locus UniProt queries returned no entries; that query limit is not proof that protein entries do not exist.
components.role: Deubiquitinase-family constituent; direct substrate delivery and a complete catalytic mechanism of the assembled TUSK complex remain unresolved.

evidence.notes: SkpZ and Tpr86 affinity isolations recover TbUsp7, and Figure 3A shows tagged-Usp7 immunoprecipitation co-enriching Tpr86 with an enolase control. The paper identifies Usp7 as the deubiquitinase-family member; molecular activity of individual candidate surface substrates is not assigned from these interactions.

components.label: SkpZ TUSK subunit
components.grounding_notes: Native InterPro SkpZ search returned no entry. The primary phylogeny distinguishes SkpZ from other Skp1 paralogs, so generic Skp1 or POZ domains would be broader than this constituent class. No exact family identifier was established.
components.role: Divergent Skp1-like constituent; its depletion alters other TUSK subunit levels and selected surface-protein cohorts. Direct substrate-adaptor action is a hypothesis.

evidence.notes: Affinity isolation of endogenously tagged SkpZ and reciprocal tagged-Tpr86 isolation identify the three-member TUSK association. The phylogeny distinguishes the SkpZ lineage from Skp1.1, Skp1.3 and Skp1.4. RNAi effects on protein abundance do not establish whether the residual complex can assemble without SkpZ.

canonical_examples.note: Native complex membership was examined using tagged proteins and affinity isolation. Tagging and immunoprecipitation Methods specify procyclic-form 427 cells, whereas the culture and RNAi experiments describe bloodstream-form 2T1 cells derived from Lister 427. The SILAC abundance comparison follows 48 hours of induction. These assay stages are retained separately. Strain 927 protein databases used for peptide identification are reference annotations, not the cultured experimental strain.

functions.label: regulation of surface-protein abundance
functions.description: In the studied bloodstream-form T. brucei RNAi context, SkpZ depletion reduces Usp7 and Tpr86 levels and decreases total abundance of selected transmembrane surface/endosomal proteins while increasing selected predicted GPI-anchored protein cohorts. Whole-cell proteomics measures abundance, not surface-specific occupancy or direct deubiquitination of each affected protein.

evidence.notes: Results, Table 1 and Figure 4 report qualitative cohort directions after 48-hour SkpZ RNAi; the ISG75 immunoblot corroborates reduced abundance. The Discussion explicitly allows indirect effects for GPI-linked proteins. ESAG7 is a soluble partner of GPI-anchored ESAG6, and ESAG5 anchoring is uncertain; neither is relabeled as a demonstrated GPI-anchored protein here.

datasets.title: SkpZ RNAi and affinity-isolation proteomics
datasets.description: Publication-linked proteomics supporting the TUSK interaction and abundance analyses; identifier and landing-page reference only.
datasets.notes: Native accession, organism 5691 and DOI were verified. The native PMID field is the placeholder zero, not a valid PMID to import. The paper and repository describe bloodstream-form RNAi and procyclic 427 immunoprecipitation separately. The paper's SILAC Methods name reference database release 24; this deposition instead names release 8.1. These source-specific processing descriptions are not harmonized. evidence.notes: Yamada et al. 2023, PMID:39816833. Checksum-verified PMC11732084.1 abstract, complex-isolation and knockdown Results, Discussion and relevant culture, tagging, SILAC, immunoprecipitation and BN-PAGE Methods inspected. Original Figures 3 and 4 visually inspected. Supports a named physical complex and bounded perturbation effects, not the proposed dark-cullin mechanism as established fact.

The ISG75 study names the same SkpZ/Tpr86/Usp7 association as the TUS deubiquitinase complex. Its reference 58 links the prior title/preprint to the TUSK paper; the inspected paragraph supplies synonym provenance, not a new composition.
