discussions.prompt: Keep TUSK distinct from the basal-body A-tusk and from cullin or SAGA-family complexes.
discussions.rationale: A shared name fragment or related enzyme family does not establish structure identity.
discussions.notes: Whole-repository hidden/ignored-inclusive alias, slug, locus, accession, DOI and PMID searches and parsed identities across 874 prior records found only unrelated A-tusk context, not this complex. Current native GO searches for TUSK, TUS, Tpr86, SkpZ and the three-protein combination returned zero hits; GO:0032991 is a verified broader parent, not an exact identity. Earlier broad queries containing complex exceeded QuickGO's 25-page cap and are not claimed exhaustive. Native Complex Portal TUSK, Tpr86 and SkpZ queries returned no entries. Figure 3 uses TUS complex, and the inspected ISG75 paper uses TUS deubiquitinase complex for the same three proteins. No equivalence to DUBm or an E3 ligase is asserted.

discussions.prompt: Resolve exact source-neutral family identifiers for the three TUSK constituent classes.
discussions.rationale: Shared repeats, domains and divergent paralogs must not be promoted to exact family identity.
discussions.notes: Native InterPro searches found no Tpr86 or SkpZ entry and only the IPR024729 ICP0-binding domain for Usp7. The paper's Tpr86-related IPR011990 is a homologous superfamily and IPR002885 is a repeat. These are declined as component identities. Protein-example accessions remain unset because exact source-locus UniProt queries did not resolve them; such bounded misses do not prove absence. Generic Skp1, TPR and deubiquitinase domains do not identify TUSK-specific membership.

discussions.prompt: Reconcile the Tpr86 locus and the percentage-versus-ratio wording before adding exact identifiers or effect sizes.
discussions.rationale: The source contains internal inconsistencies that do not invalidate the named reciprocal-isolation evidence.
discussions.notes: The main text calls Tpr86 Tb927.11.810, whereas Table 1 gives Tb927.10.810. No accession is guessed from either string. Results say Usp7 and Tpr86 are reduced by 38% and about 42%, whereas Table 1 lists ratios 0.38 and 0.42. Only the agreed qualitative decreases enter the function and graph; no arithmetic reconciliation or exact percent loss is asserted. Figure 4's inset is read as abundance corroboration, not a measured degradation half-life.

discussions.prompt: Establish native complex localization, subunit copy numbers and oligomeric state independently of tag artifacts.
discussions.rationale: Co-isolation establishes membership but not fixed stoichiometry, direct pairwise contacts or exact organellar parthood.
discussions.notes: The authors call TUSK heterotrimeric, but tagged-cell BN-PAGE gives apparent 400- and 600-kDa species and explicitly permits alternative stoichiometry or composition. Neither those migration values nor the summed subunit masses are curated as intrinsic complex properties. Their own tagged localization was ambiguous; TrypTag localization is discussed by the paper, but its native images were not independently inspected here. No fixed endosome/Golgi part_of, molecule count, dimension or structure-assembly essentiality is inferred.

discussions.prompt: Test direct TUSK substrate recognition and deubiquitination without treating the dark-cullin analogy as established mechanism.
discussions.rationale: An intervention's abundance outputs do not identify the intermediates connecting it to each affected protein.
discussions.notes: Tpr86 scaffolding, SkpZ substrate delivery, Usp7-mediated removal of ubiquitin from individual surface substrates and subsequent lysosomal routing remain proposed links. The curated NONMECHANISTIC graph preserves only measured RNAi outputs. The GPI-linked response may be secondary; ESAG7 is soluble and associated with GPI-anchored ESAG6, and ESAG5 anchoring is uncertain. No direct GPI substrate claim, universal cohort direction, catalytic specificity or narrower GO function is assigned from whole-cell proteomics. Ortholog conservation across kinetoplastids is not an experimentally demonstrated distribution of assembled TUSK, so only the studied species is a canonical example.

discussions.prompt: Do not promote initial co-isolates or analogous cullin machinery to TUSK constituents.
discussions.rationale: Not every enrichment hit is a specific, reproducible complex member.
discussions.notes: GRESAG4 and PFC17 were enriched in the initial SkpZ experiment but were not recovered in reciprocal Tpr86 isolation and were rejected as contaminants by the authors. The source also spells the latter PCF17 in one sentence. Cullin and Rbx1 machinery were not established as TUSK members; the dark-cullin analogy is not a cullin assignment. Vdu1 is a separate deubiquitinase, and changed abundance of VAMP7b or surface cargo does not make those proteins constituents.

discussions.prompt: Retain assay stages, reference-database versions and accession discrepancies without conflating samples.
discussions.rationale: Protein-search annotation strains and pipeline versions are not the experimental organism or one interchangeable protocol.
discussions.notes: Native NCBI confirms Trypanosoma brucei taxon 5691. The study distinguishes procyclic 427 tagging/immunoprecipitation from bloodstream 2T1/Lister 427 RNAi. The 927 annotation databases and source-specific releases 24, 8.1 and 39.0 are retained as processing context, not canonical strains. Native PRIDE metadata verifies both accessions and the paper DOI; PXD021000's PMID zero is not imported, and PXD021797 corrects the paper's XD021797 typographic form using its data-availability statement and native entry. Links are not exact complex xrefs. iModulonDB has no matching organism among the 28 listed datasets and is not negative evidence.

discussions.prompt: Obtain experimentally resolved imaging of the assembled TUSK complex.
discussions.rationale: Biochemical readouts, knockdown phenotypes and predicted architectures show different things.
discussions.notes: Original Figure 3 co-immunoprecipitation/BN-PAGE and Figure 4 proteomics/immunoblot graphics were visually inspected and their native media checksums verified, but no complex micrograph is asserted. Figure 7's membrane hypertrophy is a knockdown phenotype, not TUSK localization. Figure 6C is a predicted Tpr86 subunit model and Figure 8 a proposed architecture; neither is an experimentally resolved whole-complex structure. No image, dimension or atomic-model xref is inferred from these panels.

records.label: WASH complex
records.definition: A protein complex that localizes at the surface of endosomes, where it recruits and activates the Arp2/3 complex to induce actin polymerization. records.label: Cajal body
records.definition: A class of nuclear body, first seen after silver staining by Ramon y Cajal in 1903, enriched in small nuclear ribonucleoproteins, and certain general RNA polymerase II transcription factors; ultrastructurally, they appear as a tangle of coiled, electron-dense threads roughly 0.5 micrometers in diameter; involved in aspects of snRNP biogenesis; the protein coilin serves as a marker for Cajal bodies. Some argue that Cajal bodies are the sites for preassembly of transcriptosomes, unitary particles involved in transcription and processing of RNA.

records.label: cytoplasmic exosome (RNase complex)
records.definition: A ribonuclease complex that has 3-prime to 5-prime processive hydrolytic exoribonuclease activity producing 5-prime-phosphomonoesters. Participates in a multitude of cellular RNA processing and degradation events preventing nuclear export and/or translation of aberrant RNAs. Restricted to processing linear and circular single-stranded RNAs (ssRNA) only. RNAs with complex secondary structures may have to be unwound or pre-processed by co-factors prior to entering the complex, esp if the 3-prime end is structured.

causal_graphs.title: Yeast mRNPs and RNA-binding proteins assemble stress granules
causal_graphs.description: In Saccharomyces cerevisiae, stalled mRNP cargo localizes to cytoplasmic stress granules during glucose deprivation, Pab1/Pub1/Pbp1 RNA-binding markers or inputs support visible granule assembly, and heat-shock-localized eIF3/40S translation-initiation components concentrate in cytoplasmic stress granules, while P-bodies promote stress-granule assembly during glucose deprivation.
causal_graphs.scope_notes: This graph summarizes yeast glucose-deprivation and robust heat-shock stress-granule assembly inputs without asserting a complete condensate interaction network or flattening the stress-specific composition into one universal component set.

edges.subject: stalled_mrna_cargo
edges.description: Translationally stalled mRNPs concentrate in yeast cytoplasmic stress granules.

evidence.notes: Buchan, Muhlrad and Parker 2008 characterized yeast stress granules formed from nontranslating mRNPs.

edges.subject: pab1_pub1_pbp1_rna_binding_markers
edges.description: Pab1 and Pub1 mark yeast stress granules, while Pub1 and Pbp1 are needed for efficient visible stress-granule assembly.

evidence.notes: Buchan, Muhlrad and Parker 2008 linked Pub1 and Pbp1 to yeast stress-granule assembly.
Swisher and Parker 2010 tested localization and assembly effects of Pbp1-interacting stress-granule proteins.

edges.subject: eif3_40s_translation_initiation_cohort
edges.description: Robust heat-shock stress granules recruit eIF3 and 40S small ribosomal subunit markers in budding yeast.

evidence.notes: Grousl et al. 2009 observed eIF3 and 40S ribosomal subunits in robust heat-shock yeast stress granules.

edges.subject: p_body
edges.description: P-bodies promote glucose-deprivation stress-granule assembly in Saccharomyces cerevisiae.

evidence.notes: Buchan, Muhlrad and Parker 2008 found that P-body assembly was required for efficient yeast stress-granule assembly during glucose deprivation.

discussions.prompt: Resolve exact component groundings and stress-condition-specific boundaries for yeast glucose-deprivation and robust-heat-shock stress granules.
discussions.rationale: This first record groups Saccharomyces stress-granule mRNAs, RNA-binding proteins and translation-initiation markers by experimentally assayed stress-granule residency rather than guessing exact family accessions or asserting that glucose deprivation and heat-shock foci have identical composition.

functions.description: G-body-capable cells have a competitive growth advantage over cells expressing a G-body-targeted active RNase in the tested hypoxic cultures.

evidence.notes: Growth competition after normoxic preculture includes untargeted MqsR and Pfk2-D348S fusion controls. Targeted RNA degradation may affect local RNAs beyond morphology; this does not prove a single exclusive metabolic mechanism or universal survival requirement.

physical_properties.context: Approximate diameter of electron-dense, non-membrane-bound Pfk2-GFP-labeled bodies in hypoxic S. cerevisiae, measured by immunogold TEM in the 2017 study. Not an invariant size or the Gaussian radius inferred from later fluorescence images.

evidence.notes: Hypoxia triggers glycolytic body formation Results describe the approximate TEM diameter and cite Figures 1D and S2C.

causal_graphs.title: RNA-dependent G-body formation during hypoxic growth
causal_graphs.scope_notes: Cell-level interventions in S. cerevisiae. RNA dependence is supported, but an exclusive RNA-scaffold mechanism, transcript identity and a purified phase boundary are not established.

edges.subject: hypoxia
edges.description: Hypoxic growth with glucose induces glycolytic-enzyme foci.

evidence.notes: Figure 1 and glucose-deprivation controls establish the tested environmental context.

edges.subject: rna
edges.description: Associated RNA is required for efficient nascent G-body formation under the tested conditions.

evidence.notes: RIP-seq and smFISH establish RNA association; targeted MqsR/RNase A perturbations and activity/targeting controls support the requirement.

edges.subject: targeted_rnase
edges.description: G-body-targeted active RNase reduces the fraction of hypoxic cells forming G bodies.

evidence.notes: Pfk2-MqsR acts dose-dependently; untargeted MqsR does not reproduce the effect and MqsA inhibition rescues formation. RNase A provides a second enzyme test; H12A retains residual activity.

causal_graphs.title: Targeted RNase fractures preformed G bodies
causal_graphs.scope_notes: Bodies were first assembled during 20 hours of hypoxia and then followed in normoxia while RNase was induced. Fragmentation is not equated with complete dissolution.

edges.subject: targeted_rnase
edges.description: Targeted RNase causes preformed bodies to fragment.

evidence.notes: Preformed-body Results distinguish persistent single foci in vector controls from multiple foci following targeted RNase induction.

edges.subject: body
edges.description: Preformed G bodies lose single-focus integrity under targeted RNA degradation.

evidence.notes: Figure 5 and corresponding Results support partial structural disruption, not complete clearance of every body or degradation of every component.

discussions.prompt: Which broader or related structures must not be merged with the glycolytic body?
discussions.rationale: A local identifier is retained because complete cached OAK label/alias searches and current QuickGO glycolytic searches did not yield an exact cellular-component term. GO:0036464 is a broader class, not identity.
discussions.resolution_note: The defining microscopy distinguishes Pab1 stress granules and Edc3 P-bodies from G bodies; adjacent puncta do not establish identity. Membrane-bounded glycosomes and mammalian glucosomes are not exact mappings here.

discussions.prompt: Does the META-body terminology or engineered recruitment establish an exact synonym or native constituent?
discussions.rationale: Terminology and engineered localization must not inflate the native structural scope.
discussions.resolution_note: The 2023 Introduction uses META body collectively for multiple metabolic condensates, including purinosomes. It is not an exact synonym. Adh1 peptide-fusion recruitment is engineered and does not establish unmodified Adh1 as a resident.

discussions.prompt: Should adjacent proteins, genetic regulators and all proteomics hits be listed as constituents?
discussions.rationale: The 2017 workflow distinguishes 156 candidate hits from microscopy-supported localization.
discussions.resolution_note: Fas1 and Pre3/Pre8/Rpn2 adjacency in the inspected 2017 Results is not counted as residence. Snf1 loss affects formation but does not establish Snf1 residence. Snf1-dependent Pfk2 phosphorylation is dispensable in the tested phosphosite mutants. SOD1, IRA2 and ARD1 deletion phenotypes alone are not component evidence.

discussions.prompt: Which additional low-frequency or earlier-study candidates are bona fide G-body residents?
discussions.rationale: The inspected Results report more candidates than the conservative high-confidence inventory curated here. Pgi1, Tdh3, Gpm1 and Eno1 form hypoxic puncta with residual cytoplasmic signal, but their dual-label validation and the full supplemental/2013 candidate sets have not been independently audited.

discussions.prompt: Do gel-like observations prove a universal liquid-liquid phase-separation mechanism?
discussions.rationale: The 2020 study reports slow fusion, limited fluorescence recovery and incomplete sensitivity to 1,6-hexanediol.
discussions.resolution_note: Describe the observed bodies as membraneless, RNA-containing and gel-like in the tested assays. Do not equate hexanediol resistance with a definitive material-state diagnostic, rapid liquid behavior or reversible dissolution on return to normoxia.

discussions.prompt: How does G-body organization change metabolic output independently of pleiotropic perturbations?
discussions.rationale: Hypoxic preconditioning, Snf1 loss and targeted RNA degradation constrain but do not uniquely isolate the causal contribution of compartmentalization. The 2020 Discussion leaves substrate channeling, altered enzyme kinetics and local translation unresolved.

records.label: H-body
records.definition: A stress-responsive, polar, membraneless ribonucleoprotein condensate organized by Hfq in Escherichia coli, with polyphosphate-modulated assembly and enrichment of polyadenylated transcripts and RNA-processing proteins.

curation_history.changes: Scaffolded by scripts/new_record.py
Added six source-bounded components, MG1655 example, RNA/protein sequestration function, seven-edge assembly graph, identity and evidence boundaries, and an explicit TmaR family-grounding follow-up.
added 4 verified UniProtKB protein_example(s).

components.label: RNA-binding protein Hfq
components.role: Defining RNA-binding scaffold of the H-body; many Hfq molecules assemble into a mesoscale condensate, rather than one Hfq hexamer constituting the entire structure.

evidence.notes: Endogenous fluorescent reporters locate Hfq in polar bodies. Purified Hfq phase separates above a concentration threshold, reduced by polyphosphate within a concentration window (Figures 1 and 4).

protein_examples.role: Representative reviewed UniProtKB entry for gene hfq in Escherichia coli K-12. Identifier for the component's declared gene symbol; it is not itself evidence that the protein is part of this structure.

evidence.notes: Goldberger O et al. 2022, ‘Heterotypic phase separation of Hfq is linked to its roles as an RNA chaperone.’, Cell Rep. ECO:0000269 experimental evidence cited by UniProt for the 'Cytoplasm' localisation of P0A6X3.

components.label: polyphosphate
components.role: Inorganic polyanion that co-partitions with Hfq and modulates condensation, client enrichment and body persistence. Its absence does not eliminate all nitrogen-starvation-induced Hfq bodies.

evidence.notes: Figure 3 reports modest but significant Hfq/polyP colocalization, with strong enrichment in only a subset of foci. Figures 1 and 4 show residual foci in nitrogen-starved ppk mutants and Hfq-only droplets at high protein concentrations; excess polyP redissolves reconstituted droplets. The grounding denotes the polymer class, not a fixed chain length.

components.label: mRNA
components.role: Polyadenylated transcript cargo; the RNA-class grounding does not assert that all mRNAs localize to the body or that RNA is universally required for its assembly.

evidence.notes: Figure 5E FISH shows poly(A)-transcript colocalization with Hfq in a subset of nitrogen-starved WT cells, with limited signal-to-noise. Figure 4 uses an rA30 oligonucleotide, not a full mRNA, for ternary Hfq/polyP/RNA reconstitution. RNase A does not dissolve the lysate HMW Hfq assemblies in the tested assay.

components.label: Ribonuclease E
components.role: RNA-processing client enriched with Hfq in nitrogen-starvation bodies; neither catalytic inactivity within the body nor a requirement for H-body assembly is asserted.

evidence.notes: Figure 4G-I shows RNase E in polyP-dependent HMW Hfq assemblies and endogenous fluorescent RNase E enrichment at Hfq foci. Hfq is the organizing scaffold here; the Caulobacter BR-body RNase E-scaffold essentiality is not transferred.

protein_examples.role: Representative reviewed UniProtKB entry for gene rne in Escherichia coli K-12. Identifier for the component's declared gene symbol; it is not itself evidence that the protein is part of this structure.

evidence.notes: Liou GG et al. 2001, ‘RNA degradosomes exist in vivo in Escherichia coli as multicomponent complexes associated with the cytoplasmic membrane via the N-terminal region of ribonuclease E.’, Proc Natl Acad Sci U S A. ECO:0000269 experimental evidence cited by UniProt for the 'Cytoplasm' localisation of P21513.

Murashko ON et al. 2012, ‘Membrane binding of Escherichia coli RNase E catalytic domain stabilizes protein structure and increases RNA substrate affinity.’, Proc Natl Acad Sci U S A. ECO:0000269 experimental evidence cited by UniProt for the 'Cell inner membrane' localisation of P21513.

components.label: ATP-dependent RNA helicase RhlB type
components.role: RNA-helicase client whose endogenous fluorescent foci colocalize with Hfq under nitrogen starvation in the presence of polyP.

evidence.notes: Figure 5C directly images RhlB/Hfq colocalization in WT and its loss in the ppk deletion background. The verified E. coli RhlB product maps to the IPR023554 family, not the Xanthomonadaceae-focused IPR022077 family or the RhlB helicase domain.

protein_examples.role: Representative reviewed UniProtKB entry for gene rhlB in Escherichia coli K-12. Identifier for the component's declared gene symbol; it is not itself evidence that the protein is part of this structure.

evidence.notes: Taghbalout A et al. 2008, ‘RNaseE and RNA helicase B play central roles in the cytoskeletal organization of the RNA degradosome.’, J Biol Chem. ECO:0000269 experimental evidence cited by UniProt for the 'Cytoplasm' localisation of P0A8J8.

components.label: TmaR
components.role: Co-condensing polar regulator required for Hfq-body assembly during the tested nitrogen-starvation condition. It also forms distinct foci without Hfq, and is not universally required under stronger osmotic stress.

evidence.notes: Figure 1L compares endogenous Hfq/TmaR localization and deletion backgrounds; Hfq foci are lost without TmaR during nitrogen starvation. Figure 1M retains some Hfq foci without TmaR at 1.17 M NaCl. The Results discuss prior direct co-condensation evidence.

components.grounding_notes: Verified E. coli TmaR (formerly YeeX) maps to the DUF496 family IPR007458 and UPF0265 family IPR053375. These describe wider, largely uncharacterized sequence families; no exact TmaR functional-family boundary was established. A broad family or domain is not asserted as equivalent to the named pole-localizer class.

protein_examples.role: Representative reviewed UniProtKB entry for gene tmaR in Escherichia coli K-12. Identifier for the component's declared gene symbol; it is not itself evidence that the protein is part of this structure.

evidence.notes: Szoke T et al. 2021, ‘Tyrosine phosphorylation-dependent localization of TmaR that controls activity of a major bacterial sugar regulator by polar sequestration.’, Proc Natl Acad Sci U S A. ECO:0000269 experimental evidence cited by UniProt for the 'Cytoplasm' localisation of P0A8M6.

Szoke T et al. 2023, ‘Regulation of major bacterial survival strategies by transcripts sequestration in a membraneless organelle.’, Cell Rep. ECO:0000269 experimental evidence cited by UniProt for the 'Cytoplasm' localisation of P0A8M6.

canonical_examples.taxon_label: Escherichia coli str. K-12 substr. MG1655
canonical_examples.note: The study uses MG1655-derived strains with endogenous fluorescent fusions, nitrogen starvation in defined Gutnick medium, and strong osmotic stress at 1.17 M NaCl. This is an experimentally demonstrated strain example, not a prevalence assertion across E. coli or bacteria.

functions.label: RNA and protein sequestration
functions.description: Concentrates polyadenylated transcripts and selected RNA-processing proteins during nitrogen starvation. PolyP-dependent body organization is associated with selective transcript stabilization; the genetic comparisons do not isolate condensation from all other Hfq and polyP activities.

evidence.notes: Figures 4H-I and 5C,E directly localize RNase E, RhlB and poly(A) RNA. Transcript half-life and poly(A)-tail measurements in WT versus ppk deletion strains support selective preservation, but the Discussion calls for separation-of-function mutants before attributing survival specifically to condensation.

Guan et al. 2026, peer-reviewed PLOS Biology article. Full Results, relevant Methods and Discussion read through the publisher and NCBI PMC BioC (PMC13193609); Figures 1, 4 and 5 visually inspected. Uses the final H-body terminology and revised results, not unqualified claims from the earlier HP-body preprint.

causal_graphs.title: Polyphosphate modulates stress-induced H-body assembly
causal_graphs.description: Nitrogen starvation increases polyphosphate, which promotes Hfq condensation within a concentration window; the assembled bodies enrich selected RNA and protein cargo.
causal_graphs.scope_notes: Combines explicitly distinguished MG1655 cellular perturbations with purified Hfq/polyP reconstitution. PolyP is a promoter, not a universal prerequisite; TmaR dependence is restricted to the assayed nitrogen-starvation condition. Cargo enrichment is supported by localization, not proof of RNase inhibition or condensate-specific survival causation.

edges.subject: n_starvation
edges.description: Nitrogen-starved WT cells accumulate long-chain polyphosphate.

evidence.notes: Figure 1A measures polyP accumulation after entry into nitrogen starvation; the ppk deletion strain lacks detectable polyP.

edges.subject: polyp
edges.description: Polyphosphate lowers the Hfq concentration needed for droplet formation within a permissive concentration window.

evidence.notes: Figure 4A-D shows concentration-dependent reconstitution and ternary complexes. Figure 1 compares cellular ppk deletion and Ppk10k-driven polyP accumulation. Excess polyP dissolves droplets, so the effect is not monotonic.

edges.subject: hfq
edges.description: Hfq self-associates and forms condensates at sufficient protein concentration; polyP facilitates this at lower concentrations.

evidence.notes: Purified Hfq forms droplets at high protein concentration without polyP, while native gels show polyP-dependent HMW Hfq assemblies in starved WT lysates (Figure 4).

edges.subject: tmar
edges.description: TmaR supports Hfq-focus assembly in the nitrogen-starvation condition, but this requirement does not extend to every osmotic-stress condition.

evidence.notes: Figure 1L and S1H show loss of nitrogen-starvation Hfq foci in tmaR mutants, not rescued by Ppk10k. Figure 1M shows residual Hfq foci in tmaR mutants under strong osmotic stress.

edges.subject: condensation
edges.description: Cellular Hfq condensation produces the stress-responsive polar H-body.

evidence.notes: Endogenous Hfq imaging, focus dynamics, hexanediol sensitivity and FRAP support the cellular condensate interpretation (Figures 1-3); purified droplets are a reconstitution, not an assertion that every cellular constituent is reconstituted.

edges.subject: h_body
edges.description: Nitrogen-starvation H-bodies enrich RNase E as an RNA-processing client.

evidence.notes: Figure 4G-I combines HMW-complex association with live-cell RNase E/Hfq colocalization. These experiments do not establish whether the sequestered enzyme is catalytically inactive.

edges.subject: h_body
edges.description: H-bodies contain polyadenylated transcript cargo in the observed nitrogen-starved WT cells.

evidence.notes: Figure 5E shows poly(A)-RNA/Hfq colocalization in a subset of WT cells. Low FISH signal-to-noise limits quantification; no universal transcript occupancy or assembly requirement is inferred.

discussions.prompt: Keep direct localization evidence separate from candidate proteomic associations.
discussions.rationale: The native-gel screen can include polyP-binding proteins that do not interact with Hfq. The final paper reports mostly diffuse enolase fluorescence, unlike a stronger interpretation of the preprint.

discussions.prompt: Do not equate polyphosphate promotion with universal necessity or transcript preservation with proven RNase inhibition.
discussions.rationale: Residual Hfq foci persist without polyP during nitrogen starvation, whereas effects are stronger under 1.17 M NaCl. Knockouts affect multiple processes and cannot uniquely assign survival or transcript-stability changes to condensation.

Half-life sampling at 15-minute intervals emphasizes long-lived transcripts, as acknowledged in Methods.

records.definition: A nuclear body associated with the histone gene locus that is thought to contain all of the factors necessary for histone mRNA transcription and pre-mRNA processing. In Drosophila, U7 snRNP is located in the histone locus body rather than the distinct Cajal body.

records.label: interchromatin granule
records.definition: A class of nuclear body measuring 20-25 nm in diameter and distributed throughout the interchromatin space, linked together by thin fibrils. They are believed to be storage centers for various snRNAs, snRNPs, serine/arginine-rich proteins and RNA polymerase II. A typical mammalian cell contains 25-50 clusters of interchromatin granules. Interchromatin granule clusters do not contain the heterogeneous nuclear RNA-binding proteins (hnRNPs).

records.label: nuclear exosome (RNase complex)
records.definition: A ribonuclease complex that has 3-prime to 5-prime processive and distributive hydrolytic exoribonuclease activity and endoribonuclease activity, producing 5-prime-phosphomonoesters. Participates in a multitude of cellular RNA processing and degradation events preventing nuclear export and/or translation of aberrant RNAs. Restricted to processing linear and circular single-stranded RNAs (ssRNA) only. RNAs with complex secondary structures may have to be unwound or pre-processed by co-factors prior to entering the complex, esp if the 3-prime end is structured.

records.label: perinucleolar compartment
records.definition: The perinucleolar compartment (PNC) is a subnuclear structure associated with, but structurally distinct from, the nucleolus. The PNC contains large amounts of the heterogeneous nuclear ribonucleoprotein complex (hnRNP) called hnRNP I (PTB). Many RNA binding proteins as well as RNA polymerase III transcripts are highly enriched in this compartment. PTB and pol III transcripts are required for the integrity of the PNC.

records.label: prespliceosome
records.definition: A spliceosomal complex that is formed by association of the 5' splice site and the branch point sequence with specific snRNPs. The prespliceosome includes many proteins in addition to those found in the bound snRNPs. Commitment to a given pair of 5' and 3' splice sites occurs at the time of prespliceosome formation. Prespliceosome complexes are not active for splicing, but are instead an early step in the assembly of a spliceosomal complex.

records.label: ribonuclease MRP complex
records.definition: A ribonucleoprotein complex that contains an RNA molecule of the snoRNA family, and cleaves the rRNA precursor as part of rRNA transcript processing. It also has other roles: In S. cerevisiae it is involved in cell cycle-regulated degradation of daughter cell-specific mRNAs, while in mammalian cells it also enters the mitochondria and processes RNAs to create RNA primers for DNA replication.

records.label: ribosome
records.definition: The ribonucleoprotein particle that translates mRNA into protein. The bacterial and archaeal 70S ribosome comprises a small (30S) subunit built on 16S rRNA, which decodes the mRNA, and a large (50S) subunit built on 23S and 5S rRNA, whose 23S rRNA catalyses peptide bond formation. This record details that 70S form and the functional core shared with the larger eukaryotic cytosolic 80S ribosome; it does not enumerate 80S-specific components.

causal_graphs.title: RNA-dependent condensation couples BR-body assembly to RNA cleavage
causal_graphs.description: Caulobacter RNase E and available mRNA promote condensation; the resulting bodies stimulate RNA cleavage, which enables their dynamic disassembly.
causal_graphs.scope_notes: Based on NA1000-derived cellular perturbations and purified Caulobacter RNase E CTD assays from 2018 and 2020. RNA promotes rather than universally enables in vitro condensation. The graph describes the growth-condition decay cycle, not all stress states, all bacterial RNase E proteins, or a fixed stoichiometric complex.

edges.subject: rnase_e
edges.description: The disordered RNase E CTD drives condensate assembly under the tested conditions.

evidence.notes: CTD deletion abolishes foci, CTD-only constructs form foci, and purified CTD forms salt- and concentration-dependent liquid-like droplets.

edges.subject: mrna
edges.description: Available mRNA supports cellular body formation; RNA addition promotes purified CTD condensation over a broader salt range within a concentration window.

evidence.notes: Rifampicin/T7 experiments establish the cellular mRNA dependence; poly-A titrations promote droplets at intermediate RNA concentrations, while excess RNA inhibits condensation.

edges.subject: condensation
edges.description: RNase E condensation with RNA produces bacterial RNP bodies.

evidence.notes: Live-cell fusion dynamics, RNase E domain perturbations and purified-protein phase behavior support the condensate interpretation.

edges.subject: rnase_e
edges.description: The catalytic N-terminal domain cleaves RNA, distinct from the CTD assembly function.

evidence.notes: Catalytically impaired RNase E and CTD-only replacements retain bodies but fail to support their normal rapid disassembly.

edges.subject: rnp_body
edges.description: Condensate organization accelerates the initial cleavage of tested mRNA substrates in the assayed growth conditions.

evidence.notes: qRT-PCR half-lives are prolonged in the noncondensing NTD mutant and partly restored by the condensation-competent degradosome-binding-site mutant, separating condensation from client recruitment.

edges.subject: rna_cleavage
edges.description: RNA cleavage permits rapid BR-body dissolution during the observed growth-condition cycle.

evidence.notes: Wild-type bodies are dynamic on the minute scale; two catalytic mutants retain bodies throughout ten-minute imaging, and RNase A treatment dissolves stabilized bodies in lysates.

discussions.prompt: Keep the BR-body condensate distinct from one RNA degradosome and from eukaryotic granules.
discussions.rationale: The existing bacterial degradosome record describes a protein complex with an E. coli-centered component set. BR-bodies are mesoscale RNase E/RNA condensates whose assembly persists after several degradosome-client binding sites are removed. Eukaryotic P-bodies and stress granules are analogies, not exact identities.

records.definition: A ribonucleoprotein complex that contains an RNA molecule of the snoRNA family and associated proteins. Many are involved in a step of processing of rRNA molecules: cleavage, 2'-O-methylation, or pseudouridylation, but other RNA types can be targets as well. records.label: spliceosomal complex
records.definition: Any of a series of ribonucleoprotein complexes that contain snRNA(s) and small nuclear ribonucleoproteins (snRNPs), and are formed sequentially during the spliceosomal splicing of one or more substrate RNAs, and which also contain the RNA substrate(s) from the initial target RNAs of splicing, the splicing intermediate RNA(s), to the final RNA products. During cis-splicing, the initial target RNA is a single, contiguous RNA transcript, whether mRNA, snoRNA, etc., and the released products are a spliced RNA and an excised intron, generally as a lariat structure. During trans-splicing, there are two initial substrate RNAs, the spliced leader RNA and a pre-mRNA.

causal_graphs.title: The export gate feeds unfolded effectors into a host-cell conduit
causal_graphs.description: Inner- and outer-membrane rings align the export apparatus with the needle filament, creating a conduit through the bacterial envelope. The export gate recognizes unfolded substrates, the narrow needle conducts them away from the basal body, and the translocon completes the channel in the target-cell membrane.

Added Galan & Waksman 2018 as an independent second source (#63) and cross-linked the flagellum via xref, with a discussion noting that xref understates homology (#64).

component_role became required (#77) so the constituent/machinery distinction is machine-readable rather than prose. Set per component; ASSOCIATED_MACHINERY only where the protein acts on the already-assembled structure.

functions.label: DNA and protein substrate translocation

evidence.notes: Low et al. 2014 resolved a type IV secretion system architecture with inner- and outer-membrane complexes.

edges.subject: traffic_atpases

edges.subject: coupling_protein

records.label: type V protein secretion system complex
records.definition: A complex of proteins that permits the translocation of proteins across the outer membrane via a transmembrane pore, formed by a beta-barrel, into the extracellular milieu or directly into host cells; the secreted proteins contain all the information required for translocation of an effector molecule through the cell envelope. The type V secretion systems includes the autotransporters (type Va), the two-partner secretion system (type Vb) and the Oca family (type Vc).

curation_history.changes: Scaffolded by scripts/new_record.py
Added GO synonymy, protein-containing-complex parentage, a bacterial taxonomic scope row, GO/PubMed evidence, and open type V secretion subtype-boundary discussions.

taxonomic_distribution.note: Type V secretion systems are outer-membrane protein-translocation systems of Gram-negative diderm bacteria rather than a universal bacterial structure.

evidence.notes: Gene Ontology cellular-component term for the type V protein secretion system complex.
Desvaux et al. 2004 review type V secretion as an outer-membrane beta-barrel translocation pathway that includes type Va autotransporters, the type Vb two-partner system, and the type Vc Oca family.
Henderson et al. 2004 review Gram-negative type V secretion as a family encompassing autotransporter proteins, the two-partner secretion system, and type Vc or AT-2 proteins.

discussions.prompt: Resolve subtype-specific component boundaries for type Va autotransporters, type Vb two-partner systems, and type Vc/Oca trimeric autotransporters before adding constituents to the generic GO:0098046 record.
discussions.rationale: GO:0098046 spans several outer-membrane beta-barrel secretion architectures, so the first generic T5SS record records the shared GO-defined complex boundary without treating a type Va autotransporter domain layout as universal.

evidence.notes: Desvaux et al. 2004 distinguish type Va, type Vb, and type Vc systems within the type V secretion pathway.
GO:0098046 covers autotransporters, two-partner secretion systems, and the Oca/type Vc family.

discussions.prompt: Review whether GO:0046819 should be modeled as the generic GO:0098046 secretion function or narrowed to autotransporter-heavy type Va usage before adding a function row.
discussions.rationale: The GO:0046819 label is broad, but its definition describes self-mediated secretion through a beta-barrel pore formed by the C-terminal domain of the protein precursor. That wording fits type Va autotransporters more directly than two-partner type Vb systems.

evidence.notes: The type V secretion-system complex cellular-component term explicitly covers type Va, Vb, and Vc members.
Henderson et al. 2004 review autotransporters, the two-partner secretion system, and type Vc proteins as members of the type V secretion pathway.

records.label: spore inner membrane
records.definition: The membrane surrounding the spore core (endospore core) that separates it from its external environment.

taxonomic_distribution.note: Spore inner membranes surround the dormant core in endospore-forming Bacillota lineages, while many non-sporulating Bacillota lack the endospore pathway.

canonical_examples.note: Classical bacterial endospore model in which the mature core is surrounded by the spore inner membrane and external cortex and coat layers.

records.label: spore wall
records.definition: The specialized envelope lying outside the cell membrane of a spore.

curation_history.changes: Scaffolded by scripts/new_record.py

Added GO synonymy, cell-wall parentage, Microsporidia and Bacillota taxonomic scope, Saccharomyces, Encephalitozoon, and Bacillus examples, a spore-wall protection function, GO/DOI evidence, a nonmechanistic microsporidian endospore/exospore wall graph, and resolved boundary decisions for lineage-specific child layers and the broad spore-coat synonym.

taxonomic_distribution.note: Infectious microsporidian spores are enclosed by a thick wall with exospore and chitin-rich endospore layers.
Bacterial endospore-forming lineages build an external spore wall with cortex, coat, and sometimes exosporium layers, while many Bacillota lineages have lost endospore formation.

canonical_examples.note: Budding-yeast model in which the ascospore wall forms as a multilaminar envelope around each meiotic spore.
Microsporidian model in which the spore wall contains an outer exospore and an inner, chitin-rich endospore.
Bacterial model for morphogenesis of the multilayered coat and cortex surrounding the dormant endospore.

functions.label: spore wall protection

evidence.notes: Wu et al. 2008 describe Nosema bombycis spores as protected by a thick wall containing a glycoprotein-rich exospore and chitin-rich endospore.

causal_graphs.title: Microsporidian endospore and exospore form a protective wall

causal_graphs.scope_notes: This graph scopes the generic spore-wall parent to a curated Microsporidia example and does not assert that endospore or exospore layers are universal across fungal or bacterial spore walls.

discussions.prompt: Do not add every lineage-specific spore-wall layer directly to the generic spore-wall has_part list.
discussions.rationale: GO places the microsporidian endospore and exospore as parts of spore wall, but those layers are specific to microsporidian spores. Fungal ascospore layers remain under GO:0005619 ascospore wall and bacterial endospore layers remain under GO:0043591 endospore external encapsulating structure.

discussions.prompt: Keep the GO:0031160 spore coat synonym separate from the bacterial endospore coat record.
discussions.rationale: GO:0031160 uses spore coat as an exact synonym for the broad spore wall class, whereas GO:0043593 denotes the specific bacterial endospore coat layer curated separately.
